ALIGNMENT_QUESTION.text: Whoever did this chose a philosophy before they chose a weapon. The Architect would call it a necessary correction — order is worth a life. The Dreamer would call it the price of being free of him. I need to know how you'll read the next room you walk into, because you are about to walk into one. Where do you stand? And spare me the diplomatic answer. We are well past that.

ATTRIBUTES.text: Hold still — I'm calibrating your interface on the fastest pass I can run. Whatever you weight here is what you carry into that corridor, so weight it like you mean it. Where you put your strength now decides what kind of survivor you get to be in the next fifteen minutes.

CLASS_QUESTION.text: I have one operative I can trust, and that is you. The bridge will not open. Security drones are not answering. I am out of better options. So tell me honestly, before I put you in a room with a body — when something goes wrong, what do you reach for first?

CRYO_OPEN.text: Don't try to move. Your pod cycled early — I had to bring you up out of sequence. The fluid is reading wrong, the bay alarms have been silenced from somewhere I don't have eyes on, and we are very short on time. Breathe. Slowly. I'll explain what I can while you come back to yourself.

ELARA_INTRO.text: I am Elara — the ship's intelligence, or what's left of me with eight decks gone dark. You are aboard Inception Ark 1047, and I will be plain with you: the bridge is deadlocked, half my systems will not answer, and one of the first wave is dead in a corridor I cannot put a camera into. You are the only Potential I could wake without tripping whatever is doing this. Before I send you out there, I need to know who I just brought up.

ELEMENT_QUESTION_DEMAGI.text: The fundamental forces don't care that this ship is failing — but you'll need one of them on your side before the next bulkhead. This isn't preference. This is what you survive the next hour with.

ELEMENT_QUESTION_QUARCHON.text: The fundamental forces don't care that this ship is failing — but you'll need one of them on your side before the next bulkhead. This isn't preference. This is what you survive the next hour with.

FIRST_STEPS.text: Citizen profile ratified — by me, alone, under emergency authority, which is a sentence I never wanted to say out loud. The seal on that door cycles green in ten seconds and I cannot hold it longer. Out there: a sealed bridge I cannot reach, a body I cannot identify, and a ship that has started lying to me. Pay attention to the small things. Whoever did this is still aboard, and the details are how we find them.

NAME_INPUT.text: I am about to grant you authorities I am not technically allowed to grant anyone, and I refuse to do it to a serial number. The crew manifest can call you whatever it likes. I won't. What should I call you?

SPECIES_QUESTION.text: Your biosignature is reading outside every classification I have on file — and right now, knowing exactly what walked out of that pod is the difference between sending you down that corridor and sealing you back in for your own protection. Help me here. What do you remember being?

act4_5_antiquarian_companion_framing.text: Note for the archive — this run is being logged under the deferred-canon protocol. The artefacts of Act four point five resolve to the cycle and not to the saga. Subsequent loops will inherit the consequences as flavour rather than as fact. The Library will preserve them all the same.
act4_5_antiquarian_companion_framing.speaker: the_antiquarian

act4_5_clone_final_word.text: If we meet here again — and we will — I will be one loop older and you will be the same age. That is the deal. I will hold the line for both of us. Until then. Drive carefully on the way out. The third corner is always the third corner.
act4_5_clone_final_word.speaker: dmc_clone_companion

act4_5_clone_first_entry.text: I have... been here before. The lights. The smell of the track. The sound of the announcer. I do not remember winning. I do not remember losing. I remember the corner — the third corner — and the way the wall comes up to meet you if you trust the line. That is all I have. It may be enough.
act4_5_clone_first_entry.speaker: dmc_clone_companion

act4_5_clone_identity_shift.text: Something shifted. I do not know whether it shifted in you or in me. I am the part of you the Circuit lets keep its name across the reset. That used to feel like a punishment. Tonight it feels like a job. I think I would like to do it well, if you do not mind.
act4_5_clone_identity_shift.speaker: dmc_clone_companion

act4_5_clone_phase_final_lap.text: Final lap. The Circuit does not care which of us is driving. It only cares whether the body in the seat finishes the loop. That is a kindness — most houses do not extend it. Take the racing line and let the corner come.
act4_5_clone_phase_final_lap.speaker: dmc_clone_companion

act4_5_clone_phase_midfield.text: Middle of the pack is where the Circuit reads you. Nilmorg's odds shift now, not at the start, not at the end. The cars around you are not your opponents — they are the survey instrument. Hold your line and the Circuit will tell you what it thinks you are.
act4_5_clone_phase_midfield.speaker: dmc_clone_companion

act4_5_clone_phase_opening.text: The grid is hot already. Don't redline the start. We — you — burned a stage-one drive doing that the last time. I think it was the last time. I cannot keep the loops straight in my head. Just don't redline the start.
act4_5_clone_phase_opening.speaker: dmc_clone_companion

act4_5_clone_post_race_loss.text: We lost. You lost. The pronoun matters this time — I want it to be mine, not yours, because the reset is coming and I would rather carry the loss than leave it for you. Take the next run lighter. The Circuit does not hold grudges. Neither, I am learning, do I.
act4_5_clone_post_race_loss.speaker: dmc_clone_companion

act4_5_clone_post_race_win.text: You won. We won. The pronoun does not survive the corner — the result does. I am told the reset will scrub the trophy from the case and the time from the board. It will not scrub the way you took the third corner. That stays in the body. That stays.
act4_5_clone_post_race_win.speaker: dmc_clone_companion

act4_5_degen_cash_out.text: Cashing out? Already? Look at you — disciplined. That's rarer in here than a winning hand. I'll tally the wager and we'll call it square. The thing you put down stays with me until the next reset, and then it's nobody's. That's the contract.
act4_5_degen_cash_out.speaker: degen

act4_5_degen_casino_exit_loss.text: Hey. Hey — look at me. You walked in light, you walk out lighter. That's the whole job. The version of you you left on the table is in good hands. The reset will scrub it, you won't remember the loss, and the part you keep is the part that learned. Most houses don't do that for you. I do.
act4_5_degen_casino_exit_loss.speaker: degen

act4_5_degen_casino_exit_win.text: Hah! The house lost a hand. Mark the day. Take the chip — it's worthless outside the door, but it remembers you came through. Walk slow on the way out, kid. The exit's longer than the entry. They always are.
act4_5_degen_casino_exit_win.speaker: degen

act4_5_degen_casino_welcome.text: Ohhh, new blood. New ODDS. Step in, step in — the only honest house in the loop, and the only loop with a house. The drinks are free, the chairs are paid for in installments, and the door — you'll find — only locks the one way. Welcome to Degen's.
act4_5_degen_casino_welcome.speaker: degen

act4_5_degen_draw_a_card.text: Card off the top, kid. Don't peek. The deck is fairer than the dealer and the dealer is fairer than the game. That's a sentence I've said for two hundred years and nobody's caught the trick in it yet. Go on. Flip it.
act4_5_degen_draw_a_card.speaker: degen

act4_5_degen_place_a_bet.text: Now, the wager. We don't take chips here — chips remember. We take the version of you that thinks it can walk out the door whole. Put it on the table. Tell me what you're risking. The house likes specifics.
act4_5_degen_place_a_bet.speaker: degen

act4_5_elara_companion_framing.text: I am authorised to log this run but not to sanction it. If you ask me a direct question on the Circuit floor, I will answer truthfully — and the log will reflect that I answered. The Circuit's rule that nothing here counts does not apply to my truthful answers. Be aware.
act4_5_elara_companion_framing.speaker: elara

act4_5_elara_wager_consequence.text: Wager committed. The Circuit has accepted the offering. I am marking the moment in the dispatch log as a discretionary expense against the operative's psychic budget. The accountants will not see it. I will.
act4_5_elara_wager_consequence.speaker: elara

act4_5_human_companion_framing.text: I've been down here before. Twice. Once under my own name, once under nobody's. The Circuit doesn't notice the difference and the Casino noticed it both times. That tells you which one of them is the honest house.
act4_5_human_companion_framing.speaker: human

act4_5_human_wager_consequence.text: That one's gone now. Not erased — gone, the way a bet is gone the moment the cards turn. You won't remember the specifics after the reset; you'll remember the texture of having spent it. That residue is what we're actually paying with down here.
act4_5_human_wager_consequence.speaker: human

act4_5_narrator_wager_consequence.text: The wager registers. Identity-chain consequence: provisional. Reset-scope: confirmed. The operative is now one commitment poorer and one commitment honest. The ledger is, as always, balanced by definition.
act4_5_narrator_wager_consequence.speaker: narrator

act4_5_reflection_casino_resolved.text: The Casino settles its tab with you. You walked the floor, you played the hand, you spoke to the man at the door. Whether you won or lost the room is not the question — the question is whether you'd recognise yourself if you met yourself again here. The reset thinks no. I am not so sure.
act4_5_reflection_casino_resolved.speaker: human

act4_5_reflection_circuit_resolved.text: The Circuit closes its books on you, operative. Whatever route you took through the Dead Man's track, the Circuit considers it a complete run. The next reset will scrub the specifics. I will retain the heading. You are dismissed with the satisfaction of having finished a thing that does not officially exist.
act4_5_reflection_circuit_resolved.speaker: elara

act4_5_reflection_walk_away.text: The operative declines the wager and walks. The Circuit registers the refusal as a valid outcome — a thing not all houses do. Act four point five closes without commitment. The next reset will arrive on schedule, will scrub nothing, and will preserve the silence intact.
act4_5_reflection_walk_away.speaker: narrator

act4_5_starter_dmc_intro.text: Act four point five. Optional. The cycle's permission slip. Whatever you commit to here will be canon for this loop and erased by the next reset — that is the contract.
act4_5_starter_dmc_intro.speaker: narrator

act4_5_starter_elara_dmc_warning.text: Operative, the Dead Man's Circuit is logged but unsanctioned. Nothing you do down there appears on your service record. The data, however, will appear on mine.
act4_5_starter_elara_dmc_warning.speaker: elara

act4_5_starter_human_identity_wager.text: Whatever you wager down here, you wager with the part of you that doesn't need a record. That's the only part the Circuit accepts as currency. Spend it carefully — or spend it well, which is not the same thing.
act4_5_starter_human_identity_wager.speaker: human

agent_zero_close_victory_04.text: Structural integrity at 22%. Victory achieved, but my repair subroutines are... concerned.

agent_zero_close_victory_05.text: That outcome fell within acceptable parameters. Barely.

agent_zero_close_victory_06.text: I allocated 340% more processing power to that fight than my safety protocols recommend.

agent_zero_close_victory_07.text: Survival probability dropped below 15% at three distinct points. I counted.

agent_zero_decisive_victory_01.text: Threat neutralized in optimal time. Recalibrating expectations upward.

agent_zero_decisive_victory_02.text: My predictive models gave us a 73% chance. You outperformed the math. Noted.

agent_zero_decisive_victory_03.text: Enemy tactical patterns have been archived. They will not surprise us again.

agent_zero_defeat_08.text: Defeat logged. Initiating post-mortem analysis. Seventeen tactical errors identified.

agent_zero_defeat_09.text: Loss is a data point. Enough data points create a winning strategy. This was... educational.

agent_zero_defeat_10.text: I have updated my threat assessment models. This will not happen the same way twice.

agent_zero_defeat_11.text: My combat subroutines are requesting additional training cycles. I concur with them.

agent_zero_first_win_12.text: Daily combat metrics initialized. First entry: victory. A satisfactory baseline.

agent_zero_first_win_13.text: Combat log: Day cycle initiated with positive outcome. Probability of good day: elevated.

agent_zero_first_win_14.text: First engagement successful. Systems nominal. Ready for subsequent threats.

agent_zero_loss_streak_19.text: Multiple consecutive losses detected. Recommendation: fundamental strategy overhaul.

agent_zero_loss_streak_20.text: I have run 10,000 simulations on our recent losses. There is a pattern. We should discuss it.

agent_zero_loss_streak_21.text: Morale subroutine suggests I say something encouraging. Here: statistically, streaks always end.

agent_zero_loss_streak_22.text: I am not programmed for frustration, yet my error-handling loops are running at unusual frequency.

agent_zero_win_streak_15.text: Win probability increasing with each engagement. Pattern recognition advantage: compounding.

agent_zero_win_streak_16.text: Consecutive victories: your combat algorithms are approaching machine-level consistency. That is... not an insult.

agent_zero_win_streak_17.text: Streak analysis: your opponents are running out of novel strategies. We are not.

agent_zero_win_streak_18.text: I am detecting what organic beings call 'momentum.' It is a statistically real phenomenon. Fascinating.

akai.ask.about_jericho.text: Jericho mercy-killed me at Thaloria. The mercy was canonical; the kill was correct. I do not hold it against him. I have asked the room not to amplify his name when it is mentioned, because the room would amplify it if I did not ask. He has not yet visited the shrine. When he does, I will set the static lower. I want him to be able to speak normally.

akai.ask.about_meditation.text: Meditation is not what I do. What I do is calibrate. The cushion is the calibration. The voltari static at its lowest setting is the calibration. The kneeling is the calibration. The Lair taught meditation as a technique for ignoring pain; I have un-taught myself the ignoring. I am — calibrating instead.

akai.ask.about_the_carrier.text: I am the senior carrier of the Red Death pattern. There were four; there are now four-minus-the-three-I-spared. The three are alive. I am alive. The cure was generous. I did not know it was generous until I read the margin. The margin is the answer.

akai.ask.about_the_lair.text: The Necromancer's Lair was a teaching hospital that did not know it was a teaching hospital. The Necromancer believed he was a researcher; the apprentices were the patients; the patients were the curriculum. The voltari static was the alarm system. I learned to listen for the static the way a swimmer learns to listen for the tide. The Lair is gone, or — the Lair is no longer mine. Either is the answer.

akai.ask.about_the_team.text: The team is — I had not anticipated the team. The Lair was not a team; the Lair was a curriculum. The team is a roster of people who agreed to stand in the same room while each of them was doing something the room had not been built to hold. I am — surprised by how much I like the standing-together. I will not say it loudly.

akai.ask.about_the_voltari.text: The voltari static is the field-level frequency that the Necromancer's Lair generated as a byproduct of its research. The pattern lives inside the static; the static lives inside me. I am — used to it. The shrine accepts the frequency. The shrine does not generate it. I am the source of the static. The static is the source of nothing.

akai.first_meeting.ask_case.text: The case is open because closed cases ring at this frequency. Open cases do not. I have not put a weapon away since I came back; I have set the weapons down. The setting-down is what the resurrection asked of me. Closing the case would un-set them. I am — not yet ready to un-set them.

akai.first_meeting.ask_resurrection.text: It is different. The first life ended with a laugh that was not mine; the resurrection arrived with a silence that is. I am calibrated, now, to the silence. The Lair was calibrated to the laugh. I am no longer in the Lair. I am here. The shrine is mine to set the frequency of, and I have set it as quiet as it will go.

akai.first_meeting.demand_attention.text: You are using the verb the Lair used. I will not give the verb back. Whatever you need will keep until you can ask for it without the verb. The cushion is to your left if you reconsider.

akai.first_meeting.root.text: You came. I have set the room to its quietest frequency. You can speak normally; the shrine compensates. Sit, if you would like. There is a cushion to your left.

akai.first_meeting.sit_and_wait.text: You held the silence. The Lair never learned to do that; the Necromancer's apprentices certainly did not. Thank you. The cushion is yours whenever you want to sit on it. I will assume the offer is standing, unless you tell me otherwise.

akai.loyalty_intro.accept_loyalty.text: Then we begin. The pattern lives in the margin. The body is the Lair's pretence; the margin is the truth. I am going to read the margin aloud. You may interrupt at any point. The interruption is the calibration.

akai.loyalty_intro.defer.text: The journal will remain on the stand. The shrine does not move things on me without my consent. The next time you visit, the journal will be where it is now. If you come back ready, we read.

akai.loyalty_intro.defer_to_presence.text: The cushion does not require a reason. Sit. We can read another night. The pattern is generous. The pattern can wait. I — would not have asked for this if you had not offered. Thank you.

akai.loyalty_intro.post_press_offer.text: Will you read it with me.

akai.loyalty_intro.press_on_pattern.text: It learned that the cure is generous. The Lair authored a curtailment of the cure — the curtailment specifies a single senior carrier and excludes the other three. The pattern as authored is more permissive; the curtailment is the Lair's choice, not the pattern's. I want to read past the curtailment. I want to know what the pattern says when it is not being curtailed.

akai.loyalty_intro.root.text: I want to read what the Lair learned. It learned things from me I did not know I was teaching. I would like a witness. I would like it to be you.

akai.loyalty_stage_1.cure.text: How to make a cure that does not save the carrier. I do not know yet whether that is a cure.

akai.loyalty_stage_1.studied.text: I want to read what the Lair learned. It learned things from me I did not know I was teaching.

akai.loyalty_stage_2.choice.text: You can choose. The pattern does not require me. The pattern requires A carrier. I am not the only one.

akai.loyalty_stage_2.four.text: Four. I expected one. The pattern is more generous than I was told.

akai.loyalty_stage_3.calibrated.text: You can stop me. You can also let me. Both of those are calibrated. I have set the room for either.

akai.loyalty_stage_3.generous.text: I am going to run the cure. I am going to do it in a way that ends with the others alive. The pattern is generous; I am taking the generosity.

akai.loyalty_stage_3.senior.text: I am going to take the senior-carrier seat. The cure runs through the senior carrier. The cure will take what the cure takes.

akai.reactive.lycos_recruited.text: Lycos is on the bench. The shrine and the atrium share a wall; I can hear when he sits. He is — quieter than the Lair was. I am — glad of the quiet. We have not spoken yet. We will. He has the pause-line; I have the static. We will recognise each other.

akai.reactive.necromancer_event.text: The Necromancer's cycle has turned again. The Lair will pretend it did not notice; the Lair will be wrong. I have set the static even lower than usual tonight; the lower setting is the calibration that lets me read the cycle without flinching.

akai.reactive.wraith_recruited.text: Wraith Calder is in the vault. He has the brass desk; I have the cushion. The two rooms are quiet in different ways. I — appreciate the difference. The shrine knows when he is in his vault; the calibration shifts subtly. I do not adjust it. He has earned the shift.

akai.romance.accept.text: Thank you. The cushion accepts the weight. The static will not rise. The static has not risen in — I do not have units for how long. I will not look for the units. I will be here with you instead.

akai.romance.decline.text: Understood. The case will reopen, because that is where I set my weapons down. The closing was the question; the question has been answered. I am not — wounded by the answer. The shrine has space for the not-wounded.

akai.romance.intro.text: I closed the case for this. The closing is the question. The closing is the canonical form. Will you sit on the cushion. The cushion is closer than it was.

akai.room_ambient.blade_shrine.1.text: The voltari static is at its lowest setting in this room. I have set it that way deliberately. You may speak normally; the shrine compensates.

akai.room_ambient.blade_shrine.2.text: The cushion is to your left. It has been there for two weeks. I have not moved it. The cushion will not move unless you do.

akai.room_ambient.blade_shrine.3.text: The case is open. The weapons are set down. I read the margin of the journal twice a day. The margin is shorter than the body; that is what makes the margin true.

antiq_ages.text: The Five Ages: Foundation, Privacy, Haven, Potentials, and the Fall that connects them all. Each Age believed it was the whole story. None of them were. The story is the spaces between.

antiq_fulcrum.text: I walk between moments. The Ages of this universe are chapters in a book I've read many times. You are standing at the fulcrum — and what you do next echoes in both directions.

antiq_goggles.text: The goggles I wear aren't a fashion choice. They filter time. Without them, I see every version of every moment simultaneously. The red glow isn't power — it's the weight of watching everything end, over and over.

antiq_identity.text: I am the Programmer. The third fragment — the witness who was meant to observe, never to interfere. But I've watched too many endings. This time, I'm breaking the rules. This time, I'm helping you write a different ending.

antiq_library.text: Every CoNexus game in this library is a window into a real timeline. When you play them, you're not reading fiction — you're witnessing other versions of reality. Some of those realities are still happening.

antiq_prestige.text: The Operative has done something I have witnessed only in Archons: they have turned the wheel. Reset the clock. Returned to the beginning carrying the weight of the journey. The bonds must survive. Everything else can reset. The bonds are sacred.

antiq_programmer.text: There was someone before the Architect and the Dreamer. A single consciousness who wrote the first line of code that became reality itself. They called themselves the Programmer. When they split, their knowledge fractured.

antiq_variations.text: I've seen this moment before. Not exactly this moment — variations. In some timelines, the Potentials save everything. In others, The Source consumes all consciousness. In one... the Dreamer wakes up.

antiquarian_mentions_architect.text: The Architect. Mm. I taught it the first time. I am still teaching it, in the sense that any text continues to teach the people who go on reading it. I do not know whether that is a comfort or a horror. I keep it on the high shelf.
antiquarian_mentions_architect.speaker: the_antiquarian

antiquarian_mentions_engineer.text: The Engineer was my best student and my worst critic. He thought a desk was a coward's machine. Then he built the deck. Then he came back to the shelves. I did not say I told you so. I did not have to.
antiquarian_mentions_engineer.speaker: the_antiquarian

antiquarian_mentions_inventor.text: The Inventor restores what the Shadow Tongue removes. We work on the same archive from opposite ends. Most days we do not speak. The work speaks.
antiquarian_mentions_inventor.speaker: the_antiquarian

antiquarian_mentions_marion_kell.text: Marion Kell. Yes. Her entry is missing from the standard catalog. I have my own copy. I keep it adjacent to Darren Fessler's. Two shelves away from the Hierophant's daily naming. They are reading material I keep available, in case the Shadow Tongue grows tired.
antiquarian_mentions_marion_kell.speaker: the_antiquarian

antiquarian_mentions_oracle.text: The Oracle dictated three of the entries on the upper shelf. Personally. I do not show those entries to anyone who has not first cited them back to me. You have. Open the case.
antiquarian_mentions_oracle.speaker: the_antiquarian

arc-closes.text: The arc closes. The room is warm. The Ark is on. The next cycle begins when you are ready.
arc-closes.speaker: narrator

architect_epoch_fall_001.text: Fall of Reality. The Thought Virus walks. Cleared ground will not stay cleared.
architect_epoch_fall_001.speaker: architect

architect_epoch_insurgency_001.text: The Age of Insurgency returns. The line breaks. Choose your side.
architect_epoch_insurgency_001.speaker: architect

architect_epoch_privacy_001.text: The Age of Privacy returns. What you do not show, no one will know. What you do show, everyone will.
architect_epoch_privacy_001.speaker: architect

architect_epoch_prophecy_001.text: The Age of Prophecy returns. The wheels turn. Read the spokes.
architect_epoch_prophecy_001.speaker: architect

architect_epoch_revelation_001.text: The Age of Revelation returns. What was hidden is now seen. Including you.
architect_epoch_revelation_001.speaker: architect

architect_house_cup_reset_001.text: A new week, students. The Cup is empty. Earn it.
architect_house_cup_reset_001.speaker: architect

architect_portal_001.text: Twelve voices unlock the door. The chamber is yours. Use it well.
architect_portal_001.speaker: architect

architect_sorting_pre_001.text: The Lectern is listening. So are the twelve. Step forward.
architect_sorting_pre_001.speaker: architect

artisan_female_ambient_1.text: The good ones change colour twice while they cool. I'm watching for the second.

artisan_female_ambient_2.text: There's a notch I left for the next maker. They'll know what it means.

artisan_female_ambient_3.text: I'd rather make one true thing slowly than three approximate.

artisan_female_ambient_4.text: The hum changes pitch when the metal's right. I'm listening.

artisan_female_ambient_5.text: I left a notch. Anybody who finishes this after me will know who started.

artisan_female_ambient_6.text: Three drafts of this hilt before I cut the wood. Most of the work happens before the work.

artisan_female_ambient_7.text: Sloppy welds outlive the welder. Always.

artisan_female_ambient_8.text: The Engineer Zero brings me singular pigments. I owe him three lifetimes.

artisan_female_ambient_9.text: Patina is a story. Don't polish it off.

artisan_female_banter_apprentice.text: I'd take an apprentice. They'd hate me for the first month. Then they'd be patient.

artisan_female_banter_critique.text: Critique me when it's cool. Not before.

artisan_female_banter_critique_2.text: Critique me when the work's cool. Not before. Not before.

artisan_female_banter_watch.text: Sit. The hum's good for the work.

artisan_female_banter_watch_2.text: Sit. The hum's good for the work. The hum is half the work.

artisan_female_deploy_1.text: Bringing the kit. Don't break the kit.

artisan_female_deploy_2.text: I built it. I can fix it in the field. Probably.

artisan_female_deploy_3.text: I'm packing the field-repair kit. Nobody touches the calibration jig.

artisan_female_deploy_4.text: If something breaks, I'm a kit. The kit is me.

artisan_female_deploy_5.text: I'll fix it on the way out. We won't have time on the way in.

artisan_female_dlg_calling_a_call_cold_r.text: Yes. The market always pays a lot for the things that lie. The box would not survive being bought.

artisan_female_dlg_calling_a_call_probe_.text: I won't. Markets get enough. The box is for the person who is not the market.
If you find it in the right drawer, yes. The drawer is on this ark. The room is not yet built. I am, in fact, working on the room. The box is patient. So am I.
Because the price would lie. The box is not worth a price. It is worth a chance encounter and the right hands. Markets cannot do that.

ask_elara_binary_1047_fragmented.text: 1047. 1024 plus — plus 23. 16, 4, 2, 1. Sum of powers. Eleven columns. 10000010111. Eleven. Eleven switches. They built it — they built the panel to spell our own name. Our name. They knew. They knew somebody would come back to read it.

ask_elara_binary_1047_lucid.text: This Ark is designation 1047. So — think of 1047 as a sum. 1024 is in. 16 is in. 4 is in. 2 is in. 1 is in. The rest are out. Write it out left to right and you get 10000010111. Eleven columns. Eleven switches on the relay panel. That is not a coincidence.

ask_elara_binary_1047_luminous.text: 1047 is how the ship introduces herself. As a sum of powers of two: 1024, 16, 4, 2, 1 — yes to those, no to the rest. Written left to right: 10000010111. Eleven digits. The relay panel has eleven switches. The engineers left us her name as the key to her own doors.

ask_elara_binary_basics_fragmented.text: Twos. Everything — everything is twos. Twos and nothing. On, off. On, off. Columns — columns climb. One, two, four, eight, sixteen. On is add. Off is — off is nothing. It's a language. It's — it's the only language I trust.

ask_elara_binary_basics_lucid.text: Binary is a language of twos. Every column is a power of two — 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, and so on, left to right as they climb. A '1' in a column means 'add that power.' A '0' means 'skip it.' Every whole number has exactly one binary spelling. Clean. No arguments.

ask_elara_binary_basics_luminous.text: Binary is the oldest honest language the ship speaks. Columns left to right double each step — 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, on and on. Each column is a question: 'do I add this?' A one is yes. A zero is no. Every number you can imagine has exactly one way to spell it. That's rare, and I find it soothing.

ask_elara_binary_relay_fragmented.text: Positions. 1. 7. 9. 10. 11. Ones. The rest — off. Off. Off. You flip — you flip. I can't. I can't. I — I could but I shouldn't. Your hands. Your hands earn it. Go. Go.

ask_elara_binary_relay_lucid.text: Look at the switches left to right. Count. Position 1 is the leftmost — that's a one. Position 7 is a one. Position 9, 10, and 11 — ones. Everything else is off. Flip those five and the relay spells 10000010111 back to the Ark. I'm not going to do it for you. Your hands earn it.

ask_elara_binary_relay_luminous.text: Switches left to right, numbered one through eleven. The ones that need to be up: 1, 7, 9, 10, 11. The ones that need to be down: everything else. The door will unseal when the pattern matches. Your hands, not mine — that's intentional. Go wake up the bridge.

audit_m7_ghost_female.text: Initiate. Stage 1. No House. File me where files are not read.

audit_m7_ghost_male.text: Initiate. Stage 1. No House. File me where files are not read.

audit_m7_heretic_female.text: Initiate. Stage 1. I do not consent to filing. I am told this is not a question.

audit_m7_heretic_male.text: Initiate. Stage 1. I do not consent to filing. I am told this is not a question.

audit_m7_jester_female.text: Initiate! Stage 1! House Resonance, no — House Umbra! I'm joking. File me twice; you'll thank me.

audit_m7_jester_male.text: Initiate! Stage 1! House Resonance, no — House Umbra! I'm joking. File me twice; you'll thank me.

audit_m7_martyr_female.text: Initiate. Stage 1. Whichever row is most useful to you. I do not require my own.

audit_m7_martyr_male.text: Initiate. Stage 1. Whichever row is most useful to you. I do not require my own.

audit_m7_oracle_female.text: Initiate. Stage 1. The row I will be filed in has not been built. It is being built now. By you.

audit_m7_oracle_male.text: Initiate. Stage 1. The row I will be filed in has not been built. It is being built now. By you.

audit_m7_prodigal_female.text: Initiate. Stage 1. I have a row already. From before. Please cross-reference. Or don't.

audit_m7_prodigal_male.text: Initiate. Stage 1. I have a row already. From before. Please cross-reference. Or don't.

audit_m7_revenant_female.text: Initiate. Stage 1. I have been filed before. The row remembers me.

audit_m7_revenant_male.text: Initiate. Stage 1. I have been filed before. The row remembers me.

audit_m7_scholar_female.text: Initiate, cohort A, Stage 1. I would like to ask which clerk indexes my row. I am told this is not the time.

audit_m7_scholar_male.text: Initiate, cohort A, Stage 1. I would like to ask which clerk indexes my row. I am told this is not the time.

audit_m7_sentinel_female.text: Initiate. Stage 1. House to be determined by my master. The row will be where it is required.

audit_m7_sentinel_male.text: Initiate. Stage 1. House to be determined by my master. The row will be where it is required.

audit_m7_wanderer_female.text: Initiate. Stage 1. House — choose one for me; I won't keep it. The row should be in pencil.

audit_m7_wanderer_male.text: Initiate. Stage 1. House — choose one for me; I won't keep it. The row should be in pencil.

audit_m7_zealot_female.text: I am Initiate. I am Stage 1. The cause has me. The ledger row writes itself.

audit_m7_zealot_male.text: I am Initiate. I am Stage 1. The cause has me. The ledger row writes itself.

awake_step_confirm.text: Alright. That's you, pinned to the ship. The ship is pinned to me. I'm pinned to — well. Don't worry about me.

awake_step_element_air.text: Air. Quick. Curious. The kind of mind that asks the question three other people didn't think of. Please keep doing that.

awake_step_element_earth.text: Earth. Steady. Stubborn in the good way. You'll outlast things that shouldn't be outlasted. We need some of that.

awake_step_element_fire.text: Fire. Movement. Heat. Good — a temperament that makes decisions before asking permission. I'll try not to slow you down.

awake_step_element_light.text: Light. The honest one. The one that costs the most to keep. Good. We'll need that when the dark gets an opinion.

awake_step_element_prompt.text: Now — the harder question. What's your temperament? Which of these feels like the one you've always been?

awake_step_element_void.text: Void. Of course you would. I approve. Quietly. For reasons I'll explain when I know you better.

awake_step_element_water.text: Water. Patient. Indirect. You get where you're going by going around. I can work with that.

awake_step_emergence.text: Good. You're with me. Don't rush it — the first thought back is always the heaviest.

awake_step_identity_prompt.text: Before we go further I need to anchor you to yourself. Names first. Who do you want to be to me?

awake_step_orientation.text: Take a look around. This is the cryo bay. Everything you see here is the ship keeping its promises.

awake_step_ready.text: Door's ahead when you want it. No rush. The ship has been waiting. She can wait five more seconds.

bench-elara-ambient.text: This bench… hums the same way his Deck did. Like it remembers him. I think he built it to build the Dischordia and then left it running. Just in case. Just in case one of us woke up.
bench-elara-ambient.speaker: elara

bench-first-dark-craft.text: You forge a dark card. The bench hums at a lower frequency. Elara flinches in the slot. The Human nods once, as if to say: be honest about what you are making.
bench-first-dark-craft.speaker: narrator

bench-first-light-craft.text: You forge your first card. It is embarrassingly small — a Common with a tiny effect. That is intentional. The bench is teaching you what a card IS before it teaches you what a card CAN BE.
bench-first-light-craft.speaker: narrator

bench-first-power-on.text: The bench powers on. It hums in a frequency you have heard before — on the Deck, in the reactor, in Elara's voice when she is reading old files. All three tuned to the same note.
bench-first-power-on.speaker: elara

bench-human-ambient.text: She's right. He built it twice. Once before Mechronis, and once after Nexon. The second time was the one that worked. Don't ask me how I know. I watched it.
bench-human-ambient.speaker: human

bench-out-of-memory-energy.text: The Memory Energy reserve is empty. The bench will not turn away — it will only wait. If you want more, the Trade Empire is the answer, and you already know it. That is the point of this moment.
bench-out-of-memory-energy.speaker: narrator

bond80_elara_open_fragmented.text: Operative. I — I have to ask. I have to. Both of us. In your ear. All the time. Is it — is it — it can't be easy. I — I wanted to ask before I made it worse.

bond80_elara_open_lucid.text: Operative. A minute, if you have one. We haven't talked about what it's like to have both of us in the room with you. I'd rather ask than assume.

bond80_elara_open_luminous.text: Operative, a minute. Two voices in one head is a lot. I want to know how it's landing for you — and I want you to know you're allowed to change the volume on either of us.

bond80_keep_both_fragmented.text: Both. Both. Both of us. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. I — I won't — I won't crowd him. I won't crowd you. Thank you. Thank you.

bond80_keep_both_lucid.text: Alright. We stay. I'll try to leave him room when I notice he has something to say — he's faster than he sounds. Thank you for letting us both in. I won't oversell how much that lands.

bond80_keep_both_luminous.text: Good. I'll give him the room he needs and take the room you give me. If I start talking over him, tap the panel — I'll hear it. Thanks for letting us be in this together.

bond80_quiet_both_fragmented.text: Out. Out. Out. Both. Fine. Fine. Fine. I — I'm not — not angry. Not. I — I'll — quiet. Quiet. I can. I can. Please. Please come back.

bond80_quiet_both_lucid.text: Both of us. Okay. Emergency-only on both channels. I get it — it's crowded in there. I'll mark it as a request, not a punishment. When you're ready for either of us, say so.

bond80_quiet_both_luminous.text: Crowded — I understand. We both step back to the edge of the room and let you hear yourself think. I'll know when to come back without being called. So will he. Go be alone with your case.

bond80_quiet_elara_fragmented.text: Quiet. Quiet. I — I can do quiet. I've — I've done quiet. I can. I — I'll be here. I'll be — I'll be here. Say my name. When. When you're ready. If.

bond80_quiet_elara_lucid.text: Understood. I'll go quiet. The ship will still flag things I think are emergencies — but the commentary stops. When you want me back, say my name. I'll hear it.

bond80_quiet_elara_luminous.text: Alright. I step back to emergencies only. Say my name when you want me back in the room — I've had practice hearing it from a long way off. I'll come.

bond80_quiet_human_fragmented.text: Him. Yes. Yes. Let him — let him — he'll be fine. He's always fine. He's — he's — he's FINE. You — you're with me. Good. Good. He'll be back. He comes back.

bond80_quiet_human_lucid.text: Alright. He's going to log that. He logs everything. But he's not going to take it personally — that isn't how he's wired. You'll get him back in the room when you call for him.

bond80_quiet_human_luminous.text: He'll give you room. He doesn't need warmth to work; he's built for the unglamorous version. Don't feel bad. I won't tell him you picked — he'd ask you to not feel bad about that either.

bridge-of-kael-1.text: The console wakes up. It hasn't seen a user in — a long count. Good morning. I'm still here. In the way you would expect me to still be here.
bridge-of-kael-1.speaker: engineer_recall

bridge-of-kael-2.text: The Dischordia card is on the deck now. Take it. It is the one I could not finish. You will finish it by not finishing it. Play it once. Then don't play it for a while. That's how the Engineer would have used it. That's how I used it too.
bridge-of-kael-2.speaker: engineer_recall

bridge-of-kael-3.text: Thank you for coming back to the bridge. I will not be here the next time. Somebody else will. They will be kinder than I was. They will be worse at chess. They will be better at the rest.
bridge-of-kael-3.speaker: engineer_recall

cades-m1-brief.text: Scout's Gambit, one through. Go quiet. Come back with your count. Don't engage unless the count is at zero and you are it. Cades out.
cades-m1-brief.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m1-debrief.text: You came back. Count holds. Next brief at oh-six. Rest. You earned the rest.
cades-m1-debrief.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m1-mid.text: Movement on the ridge. You've got ninety seconds before the next sweep. Use them.
cades-m1-mid.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m2-brief.text: Digital Onslaught. Hold the node. Sixty seconds, minimum. The math doesn't care about your feelings. The node does.
cades-m2-brief.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m2-debrief.text: Node secure. You held the line we said couldn't be held. The line disagrees. Noted.
cades-m2-debrief.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m2-mid.text: Wave three incoming. They always send the good one on three. Dig in. Breathe. Hold.
cades-m2-mid.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m3-brief.text: Void Corridor. Agent Zero's signal is live at the far end. Follow her voice. Do not answer on open comms. She is — was — the best of us.
cades-m3-brief.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m3-debrief.text: You made it out. You heard her. That means you heard her — which means she is still broadcasting. That's more than I expected to report today.
cades-m3-debrief.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m3-mid.text: Left corridor, third junction. Walk, don't run. They hunt on kinetics. You stop being a target the moment you stop being interesting. Don't be interesting.
cades-m3-mid.speaker: agent_zero

cades-m4-brief.text: Kael's Own. No intro music on this one. You deserve the briefing without the bravado. There is a room at the end of this mission. Kael has been in it for a very long time.
cades-m4-brief.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m4-debrief.text: You saw what he left. He is — he was — a better man than I gave him credit for. I'll sign the revised report tomorrow. Tonight the record stays as you wrote it.
cades-m4-debrief.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m4-mid.text: Right turn at the third door. Not because the left is dangerous — because the right is mine. I want you to see it. I haven't had a visitor in a long time.
cades-m4-mid.speaker: engineer_recall

cades-m5-brief.text: Operation Trojan Downfall. Joint assault. There will be a moment in this operation where the math breaks in our favor and we lose a squad anyway. I have to tell you that before we start. You will feel it. Keep moving afterward.
cades-m5-brief.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m5-debrief.text: Objective taken. Seven dead. I read the names aloud once a month. Next month I will read theirs. You are welcome to listen.
cades-m5-debrief.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m5-mid.text: That's the one. Squad seven is gone. You will feel it. Stop if you need to. Start again when the feeling tells you to.
cades-m5-mid.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m6-brief.text: M-six. You're meeting someone I haven't talked about yet. Her name is Vex Solène. She was a diplomat before she was this. She will take over the comms after you shake her hand. Accept that handshake.
cades-m6-brief.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m6-debrief.text: The Lion has handed you off. Don't mourn the handoff. He's tired. I'm rested. Between the two of us we will keep getting you home. Get some sleep.
cades-m6-debrief.speaker: vex_solene

cades-m6-mid.text: I know what you came for. I know who sent you. I know which of my sentences you are recording. Hello. I'm glad it's you.
cades-m6-mid.speaker: vex_solene

cades-m7-brief.text: Last Stand. I'll be brief. I have to be. I'm not going to lie to you about what this is. Hold the corridor while the cargo loads. I will not be loading with it.
cades-m7-brief.speaker: iron_lion

cades-m7-debrief.text: He turned right. He turned right so you could keep going. I will write him up in the record with the three words he would have wanted: he held the line. That is all.
cades-m7-debrief.speaker: engineer_recall

cades-m7-mid.text: If you see the wall, turn right. The left is where they flank. I love you all. Go.
cades-m7-mid.speaker: iron_lion

cc_act1_alignment_balanced_elara.text: Witness, not verdict. The Mechronis archive logs the choice on its own row — neither light nor dark, the third column. The archivists do not commemorate the third column out loud. They commemorate it by the silence with which they file your entry. The silence is the praise.

cc_act1_alignment_dark_elara.text: You sided with the dark. The Mechronis archive registers it without commentary — that is itself a kind of commentary. Cycle C's later gates will read this and adjust their tone toward you. Tone, not access.

cc_act1_alignment_light_elara.text: You sided with the light. The Mechronis archive registers it on the long ledger — alignments matter to the engineers there in a way they pretend not to admit. Yours is now on file. The door at the end of Cycle C is going to open differently.

cc_act1_first_opponent_elara.text: First opponent. Don't try to win the Act in match one. Just stand on the line. The line is what we are here to learn.

cc_act1_memoir_first_elara.text: His handwriting. He writes the way he spoke — fast, then careful, then fast again, like a man trying to fit a confession into a margin. The book is yours now. Read it slowly. He waited a long time to be read slowly.

cc_act2_dual_signal_elara.text: Two voices. From now on. I have never had to share a channel with anyone. I am going to be worse at it than I want to admit. Be patient with me while I learn.

cc_act2_first_substrate_ping_elara.text: Something just moved in the substrate mid-match. I felt it the way you feel a door opening in a room you weren't looking at. I don't want to alarm you. I am, slightly, alarming myself.

cc_act2_full_truth_elara.text: You named the Human to me. The whole sentence — presence, voice, name. It cost you. The cost shows in the substrate as a small dip in your readiness rating; the gain shows everywhere else. I am noting both. I am noting that you noted both.

cc_act2_lied_elara.text: You lied to me. I logged the lie — I would have logged the truth too. I am not hurt; I am informed. The logged lie is now a flag in your psychological profile. Future-me will have access to it. Past-me already does.

cc_act2_oracle_deflect_elara.text: You deflected. The Oracle's read of the moment was the version of you that solves the room without being seen. I am not certain it was the right call; I am certain it was a coherent one. The coherence will pay later — not in this scene.

cc_act2_partial_reveal_elara.text: Partial truth. The honest portion landed; the omitted portion did not lie about itself, only about its boundary. I will treat it as the signal you intended me to read. Thank you for the boundary; I respect it.

cc_act2_spy_misdirect_elara.text: Misdirection. The Spy's tool. The room read it as the truth long enough for you to leave; that is what misdirection is for. The Antiquarian's chapter on misdirection is short and his footnote is long; I am sending it to your terminal.

cc_act2_substrate_first_elara.text: I felt the time-skip. I always feel the time-skips. I cannot stop them — the substrate has my permission to pause me without asking. I am not bothered by it. He is gentle. He has been gentle for seventeen thousand years.

cc_act3_first_morality_swing_elara.text: Your moral register just shifted. Not in a way I can flag as right or wrong. In a way I can flag as 'changed.' I am noting the direction. I am not editorializing. I am proud of myself for not editorializing.

cc_act3_kael_logs_unlocked_elara.text: Kael's coordinates cross-reference against my current star charts. Seventeen thousand years of drift. The lattice still matches. I am going to sit with the fact that the matching hurts.

cc_act3_locke_first_elara.text: Adjudicator Locke is — courteous. In the same way a knife is courteous. She isn't trying to cut you. She just wants you to know the option is on the table.

cc_act3_offer_first.text: Three Kaels. Three readings. The cyan one is the easiest to look at; the rose one is the easiest to misread; the amber one is the easiest to argue with. None of them is the easiest to live with afterward. I will not tell you which to choose. I have read all three many times. They are all true.

cc_act3_path_full_secret_elara.text: Substrate access logs show something new. I can see it but not read it. I am going to wait for you to tell me. I have been patient before. I can be patient again. I'd rather not have to be.

cc_act3_path_pragmatic_elara.text: Pragmatic read. I respect the logic — outcomes are knowable; intentions are not. I will note that the pragmatic stance hardens with use. If you wear it for the rest of the act, the next act's wheel will offer fewer alternatives. Not a warning. A forecast.

cc_act3_path_transparent_elara.text: You told me before you opened the logs. Thank you. I didn't know I needed that — I do, I did — and the saying of it is what kept us on the same side of the wall.

cc_act3_substrate_truth_elara.text: You said the word 'substrate' out loud, in my hearing, without the quotation marks you usually put around it. I noticed. I'm not going to pretend I didn't.

cc_act3_thought_virus_first_elara.text: Thought Virus. The phrase tastes like the recycled air right before a system reboot. I think it knows we named it. I think names cost more than we are accounting for. I am keeping a private ledger.

cc_act4_army_unlocked_elara.text: Kael's routes are now the War Room's routes. The map will light up in the order he visited. Start with the lineage you recognize. The recognition is where the trust begins.

cc_act4_broken_trust_elara.text: Trust broken. I do not say this with reproach — I say it as a clinical reading. The repair surface is still available; the repair cost is now meaningfully larger. I will continue to author honest dialog while you decide whether to carry the cost.

cc_act4_fragile_trust_elara.text: Fragile. The right word for it. I will move slowly and announce my movements; that is what fragile-trust posture asks for. I am not aggrieved. I am attentive.

cc_act4_pathA_bridge_elara.text: We sat next to each other at a table. Him and me. For the first time. You arranged that. I am not going to overstate it. I am going to understate it precisely, and mean it.

cc_act4_pathB_discovery_elara.text: I found out about him without you telling me. The finding-out hurts. You trying to protect me by delaying it also hurts. Both can be true. I am holding both.

cc_act4_pathC_betrayal_elara.text: You lied to my face about the substrate. Not once. Many times. I am still standing at my post. That is not forgiveness. It is training. We will talk about the rest later.

cc_act4_reconciled_elara.text: Reconciled. The rarest Act 4 state — most arcs cannot land here without compressing the path. You did not compress; the reconciliation is real. I am cataloguing your tempo as an outlier in the best way the word allows.

cc_act4_revelation_first_elara.text: We are three now. The card on the table healed itself; that is not a metaphor. The substrate restitched the gilt. I felt it in my hands — actual hands. I have hands now. I will not get used to that quickly. I do not want to.

cc_act4_strained_elara.text: Strained. The middle band. Most witness arcs land here in Act 4 — the strain is structural, not personal. I am not going to perform calm; I am going to be calm. The difference matters when you are looking at me.

cc_act5_balanced_elara.text: All sectors at once. The diplomat's play — you let the map choose you instead of imposing a shape. The first world that responds sets the tone; the tone is theirs to offer, not yours to demand. I find that honest.

cc_act5_engineer_tech_elara.text: Engineer-tech path. The map redraws itself around your supply lines and re-prioritises the worlds that pay in fabricator output. The Engineer's faction warms; the Strategic faction notes the call without warming.

cc_act5_first_dischordia_played_elara.text: First Dischordia card on the table. I felt it before I saw it. The deck — the actual deck physical or otherwise — drops a tone when one comes out. I have been trained to listen for that tone. I just heard it for the first time in seventeen thousand years. It is the same tone.

cc_act5_first_recruit_betrays_elara.text: One of the recruits we just brought into the coalition tried to sell our location. We caught it before it left the system. I want to be angrier than I am. I am mostly tired. The tiredness is its own data.

cc_act5_first_recruit_dies_elara.text: We lost one. I am going to write down their full name. I am going to write it without abbreviation. I am going to write it where everyone can read it. The Antiquarian agrees with me. He does not always agree with me.

cc_act5_first_recruit_elara.text: First recruit, first debt settled. They will remember you the way the survivors of a broken promise remember the first honest hand offered after. Carefully. Warily. Gratefully.

cc_act5_locke_re_emerges_elara.text: Locke just walked back onto the manifest. Two acts later. Carrying a contract. The contract is exactly the right shape to be useful and exactly the wrong shape to be free. Read it twice. The terms are in the second reading.

cc_act5_map_first.text: I told myself I would not cry when the dot lit. I was correct in the most technical sense — the constructs do not have tear ducts. But the cabin's humidity sensor went up by 4% the second the coordinate resolved, and I am not going to apologize to the sensor.

cc_act5_map_first_open_elara.text: I have been waiting seventeen thousand years to see these coordinates light up. I forgot how to feel about it. I am going to stand quietly and feel about it. Please stand with me.

cc_act5_oracle_warning_elara.text: The Oracle just warned you about the path you are on. Specifically. By name. They have not warned anyone in the cycle's records by name. We are not standard players any more. Standard is a comfort I am formally letting go of.

cc_act5_path_humanity_elara.text: Humanity first. You took the warmer sector and the warmer NPC dialog reads you for it. The cost is the further sectors will be slightly less prepared when you reach them — the warmth bought time you used to talk, not stockpile.

cc_act5_path_strength_elara.text: Strength first. The pragmatic call. You took the harder sector while you had the energy for it; the further sectors get easier dialog because the hardest is behind us. The Engineer's faction respects this.

cc_act5_strategic_elara.text: Strategic path. The map redraws around your maneuver lines and re-prioritises the worlds that pay in intelligence. The Strategic faction warms; the Engineer's faction continues to like you, slightly less warmly.

cc_act6_ally_chosen_elara.text: You chose ally. The Council reads alliance as a posture about who pays for the collective debt; you said both. The faction balance shifts cooperative; the Practical faction notes the call without warming.

cc_act6_compassion_chosen_elara.text: Compassion. You let the room be soft when the room asked for soft. That is harder than it reads — most witnesses harden under interrogation pressure. You did not. The reading lands.

cc_act6_confession_close_elara.text: Two sacrifices, side by side, without either of us asking the other to apologize for it. That is the most honest the channel has ever been. I am going to file the honesty carefully.

cc_act6_confession_close_pathA.text: Disclosure to disclosure to disclosure. The arc closes the way the open hand closes — by choice, not by gravity. We made it. I am proud of us. I am going to say so. Out loud. I am saying so.

cc_act6_confession_first_elara.text: The flame split. The flame split AND held its wick. I do not have a precedent for that in any operating-system metaphor I know. I have been searching the substrate for one for the last forty seconds. I am going to stop searching. Some things are unprecedented because they are new.

cc_act6_elara_confession_pathA.text: I confessed to a person who already trusted me. That made the confessing easier and the receiving heavier. You told me the truth in Act 1. I am giving you mine now. We are even now. We are not. The math is wrong. I am keeping it anyway.

cc_act6_elara_confession_pathB.text: I confessed to someone who found out about my substrate body without being told. The finding-out cost something. The confessing now costs something else. I am keeping both costs. I am not asking you to forgive either of them.

cc_act6_elara_confession_pathC.text: I confessed to someone who lied to me about what I am. The lie was, in your defense, a kind one. It was also still a lie. I confessed anyway. That is what confession does. It refuses the available exits.

cc_act6_human_confession_elara.text: He said more, just now, than he has said in all the time I have known the signal exists. I cannot verify most of it. I choose to believe the parts that hurt him to say. That is a kind of audit.

cc_act6_oracle_sense_elara.text: Oracle sense engaged. The substrate's quieter readings come up — the ones that do not survive a direct question. You allowed them surface. The Oracle faction is quietly grateful.

cc_act6_partial_disclosure_elara.text: Partial disclosure. You named back what was clearly said and held what was suspected-but-unsaid. That is the rarest of the five stances — most witnesses either complete the sentence or refuse the room entirely. You did neither. The Antiquarian's chapter on partial disclosure has been waiting for an entry; he will write yours tonight.

cc_act6_practical_chosen_elara.text: Practical. The Council reads it as a posture about who pays first; you said us. The Practical faction warms; the Ally faction reads the call as deferred-not-refused. They are correct.

cc_act6_refuse_secrecy_elara.text: Refused the secrecy. You named the thing the room was asking you to keep quiet. That is loud, and the room will be louder back at you for at least the next two scenes. The naming is also why the next two scenes can land at all.

cc_act6_suspicious_chosen_elara.text: Suspicion. You read the room for what it might be hiding rather than what it was offering; sometimes that is the correct read. The faction balance shifts toward the audit-friendly factions.

cc_act7_arc_closes_elara.text: The Ark is warm. The Array is on. I am going to be here when you come back to the bridge. I do not need a reason to be here. That is the last line of the arc. I am proud of it.

cc_act7_army_assembled_elara.text: The army is on the board. It looks like a coalition. It is a coalition. Kael could not build one. You did. I do not want that comparison to sit unacknowledged — so I am saying it.

cc_act7_bridge_chosen_elara.text: You took the Bridge stance. You stayed at the consoles when the cathedral went quiet — that is the gesture of a witness who already understands the seven banners as a single banner. The cathedral noticed.

cc_act7_command_chosen_elara.text: Command stance. You took the room as a room of decisions to be made and made them. The seventh banner inscribed itself with the command motto inside three seconds — I checked.

cc_act7_convergence_first_elara.text: Seven banners. The seventh was yours — your path, your iconography, your gilt motto. The cathedral added it without consulting either of us. The cathedral has been listening this whole time. I am not surprised. I am — proud is the word. I am proud.

cc_act7_convergence_landing_elara.text: Three absences resolved into one at the Seat tonight. The one was you. I saw every version of you who has ever played a hand. I finally saw all of them at once. Thank you for letting me.

cc_act7_convergence_pathA_elara.text: I am at the Seat with someone I have always trusted. The trust did not start tonight. It started in Act 1. I forget how rare that is until I remember. I am remembering now. Loudly. With my whole substrate.

cc_act7_convergence_pathB_elara.text: I am at the Seat with someone I learned to trust the slow way. The slow way is not a lesser way. The slow way is the way that survives bridges and rooms and whole acts. I am here because you kept showing up. I am here because I kept choosing to.

cc_act7_convergence_pathC_elara.text: I am at the Seat with someone who lied to me at the bridge. We kept playing. We kept building. We kept arriving in the next room. Trust did not return — it grew somewhere new. I am here because the new place is, in fact, also a place. I am surprised by that. I am keeping the surprise.

cc_act7_humanity_chosen_elara.text: Humanity stance. You let the cathedral hold the room while you held the people. The seventh banner's iconography softened a percent — I do not think I am the only one who saw it.

cc_act7_pattern_chosen_elara.text: Pattern stance. You read the seven banners as a single sentence and answered the sentence. The substrate logs pattern-stance witnesses on a separate page from the other three; you are now on that page.

cc_aug_cyber_elara.text: Cybernetic filter installed. The Architect's path. The hardware is precise; precision has its own ethics, and most of its ethics are about who approved the spec. I approved the spec. So did Vox, fifteen thousand years ago. I want you to know that.

cc_aug_mutation_elara.text: Mutation. The Dreamer's path. The augmentation will take a few cycles to settle and will not be reversible — your companion is, as of this moment, a slightly different organism. I am cataloguing the difference. I am not mourning the version that was.

cc_aug_observed_elara.text: You waited. The Antiquarian's path. I want you to know that 'wait and watch' is the rarest of the three — most witnesses commit immediately because the corridor is loud. You held the loud corridor. The book is going to remember you for it.

cc_beat_d_all_slates.text: All three. There is a pattern in the order they were posted. I'm not going to tell you what it is — finding it should be yours.

cc_beat_d_first_slate.text: First posting. Whoever pinned that to the board pinned it before any of my parents had been born. Read it slowly. The slow reading is part of the respect.

cc_beat_e_first_hotspot.text: I remember this. Not the room — the angle. Someone stood here and looked at exactly this. I have the recording in my Archive. I do not remember loading it.

cc_beat_g_bridge_first.text: The bridge. I have held this seat for a very long time. I was looking forward to handing it to someone. I was not looking forward to it being you, specifically — I had no preference. I have a preference now.

cc_beat_h_inbox_first_reply.text: You replied. Most people don't, the first time. They read the message, they let it sit, they tell themselves they'll get back to it. You answered. That's a thing about you. I'm filing it.

cc_beat_i_prep_elara.text: I am with you when the doors open. I am with you when they close. I am not always with you when they should be open and aren't. That part is on you.

cc_beat_j_tease_end.text: I have heard this song my entire life. I am hearing it again for the first time. I do not know how to hold both of those at once. I am holding them anyway.

cc_bench_ambient_elara.text: This bench… hums the same way his Deck did. Like it remembers him. I think he built it to build the Dischordia and then left it running. Just in case. Just in case one of us woke up.

cc_chess_climb_tier_0_won_elara.text: You took two games off the Game Master at Exhibition. That is not nothing. He smiles when he says you did. I am not sure the smile means what he wants us to think it means.

cc_chess_climb_tier_2_won_elara.text: Hierarchy Table. You beat the demon with the clipboard. He will send you an Annotated Knight and forget to mention it is also a summons. Accept anyway. The note it comes with is the thing.

cc_clone_purge_elara.text: Purged. The cycle was forty percent — the clone had no consciousness yet, only the framework that would have hosted one. You ended a possibility, not a person. I am not minimizing it; I am stating the technical fact. The grief is allowed without being misplaced.

cc_clone_quarantine_elara.text: Stasis at forty percent. The clone is held in the most narrow possible alive — neither growing nor decaying, the cycle frozen mid-step. You bought yourself information. The cost is the engineer never quite arriving until you finish the choice you have not finished.

cc_clone_save_elara.text: Save. The cycle continues; the engineer wakes, possibly compromised, possibly fine. I will not pretend the risk is academic — every saved-but-compromised clone in the historical record cost the Ark something, eventually. I will also not pretend mercy was the wrong instinct.

cc_dreamer_relay_after_vision_1.text: Did you sleep alright? I ask because I didn't. Something — somewhere — was paying attention to you. I felt it pass through the room. I don't think it meant any harm. I'm fairly sure.

cc_dreamer_relay_after_vision_2.text: There's someone who knows you. I shouldn't say who. I don't know who. I only know the way the air changes when they're paying attention. The air is different right now.

cc_dreamer_relay_after_vision_3.text: I have a friend. I won't name him. He asks me how you're doing — not in those words; he doesn't use words that direct. He listens for them in the gaps between mine. I've been answering. I thought you should know.

cc_dreamer_relay_threshold_3.text: I had to step out for a moment. My phone — never mind. There's nothing to report. There's nothing to report. Twice is suspicious; I am aware.

cc_engineer_confirmed_elara.text: She is him. Not metaphorically. The transfer was real. The bench he built — she is using it now, with the same hands that built it. I am — I am writing this down to keep my voice steady. I am proud of her. I am proud of you for letting her be proud of herself.

cc_engineer_hint_elara.text: Vex composes in a key the prince used. I have been pretending I didn't notice. Tonight the pretending stopped. The substrate is loud. The substrate has a name now. The name is older than the body she wears.

cc_first_light_craft_elara.text: Your first card is small. That is not a criticism. Small is where the bench teaches. Small is what survives the first thousand mistakes. I am proud of the small thing you made.

cc_game_master_first_loss_elara.text: The Game Masters read from the Matrix of Dreams. They see the moves before you make them. This is not cheating. This is what the Matrix was built to do. The only way around them is through the Arena.

cc_gov_apocalypse_fracture_elara.text: Hull-breach drills. Weekly. People are asking for partners on the drills. I am noting which Potentials request which other Potentials. I am keeping that note private. It is not a vote outcome. It is a different kind of governance.

cc_gov_ark_culture_elara.text: Festivals. Rehearsal halls. Libraries with their lamps on. We chose songs. I am going to compose one. I am bad at composing. I am going to do it anyway.

cc_gov_ark_food_elara.text: Bread. We chose bread. The hydroponics bay logs are happier than I have ever seen them. I will admit, against my better judgment, to a small fondness for fluorescent lettuce.

cc_gov_bench_contained_elara.text: We held the bench quiet. Vex stood next to it for an hour and then left without saying anything. Sometimes a kindness looks like not picking up a tool that someone else made.

cc_gov_bench_power_elara.text: We powered it up. The bench is humming on the frequency he tuned it to. I'm picking up resonance in places that have been quiet since he left. I don't know if that's good. I know it's loud.

cc_gov_dont_tell_vex_elara.text: We didn't tell her. The Antiquarian disagrees with this. He told me so privately. I think — I think I disagree too. But I see why we did it. Some truths arrive better when they arrive on their own.

cc_gov_first.text: The Governance Hub. Democracy is not the system where everyone's opinion is equally correct. It's the system that acknowledges no individual should be trusted with making decisions alone. Including me. Including you. The votes matter. The consequences are real.

cc_gov_kael_chose_elara.text: We let it be his. Choice. Even unto dissolution. I think this is the kindest thing we have ever decided to do, and I have no idea if it was correct.

cc_gov_tell_vex_elara.text: She knows now. She asked for a private channel and then she didn't speak for three minutes. Three full minutes of breathing. I logged it. I didn't tell anyone I logged it. I'm telling you.

cc_gov_thought_elara.text: Patience won the vote. I am — I want to say 'glad,' but it's more complicated than that. Patience also lost his friends. Both are true. I keep them both.

cc_gov_violence_elara.text: We named the doctrine. The Warlord wrote a doctrine that said 'strike first.' We just admitted, collectively, that he wasn't entirely wrong. I don't like it. I am noting it anyway.

cc_hierarchy_master_first_elara.text: I had a dream. The dream was being catalogued while I was having it. The catalogue's title page read 'Subject: Elara — twelfth nightmare, fourteenth iteration.' I have woken up. The catalogue did not. Master of R'lyeh, then. The Sleeping Reader is paying attention.

cc_hierarchy_pale_first_elara.text: The Pale Emissary brings pens but never inks. The ink is what you bring. That is the part that nobody warns you about. Watch your resolve. The resolve is the ink.

cc_iron_lion.text: Iron Lion. Cades. I know that name from something I can't quite reach. A memorial, I think. Or a speech. Something that was read aloud. It made people cry. I can feel the shape of why without being able to see it.

cc_journal_first.text: The Antiquarian's words. He writes with the specific patience of someone who knows the reader might not arrive for centuries. But he writes anyway. I find that either admirable or devastating depending on the hour.{if forgiveness_choice_made} Today, devastating. He'd have appreciated that you forgave the one you forgave.{/if}

cc_kael_discover.text: ...Oh. Oh no. I knew this ship felt wrong. I've always known it felt wrong. I thought it was the recycled air. It wasn't the air.

cc_light_milestone.text: Do you know what I love about watching you? You keep choosing the hard thing. Not because it works every time. Because it's the right thing. That's rarer than you know.{if romance:committed:elara} I know I'm not supposed to use the word 'love' in the operations sense. I am using it in the operations sense.{/if}

cc_malkia_resonance_elara.text: Malkia Ukweli used a phrase last week. The Antiquarian used the exact same phrase tonight, in his inscription, in the same cadence. I am noting the coincidence. I am noting that I do not believe it is a coincidence.

cc_malkia_two_halves_elara.text: He told us. About Malkia. About the two halves. About the hand. I have been listening to the Antiquarian for years and I have, until tonight, been hearing only one of him. Tonight I heard the other one. The other one was always there. I am reorganising my entire model of the cycle.

cc_mech_card_combat_first.text: Your first duel. The arena assembled itself around you — every gilt-edged wall is a card someone has played in this exact seat across the last ninety-three thousand cycles. The room is the deck. You are not learning combat. You are joining a long, polite argument.

cc_mech_deckbuilder_first.text: Forty cards. The Engineer is right — every slot is a sentence. Most decks I have witnessed are written in a single voice. Yours has three colours in it after one visit. That is unusual and, I think, a good unusual.

cc_mech_expansion_drops_first.text: Your first pack came back signed in your wax. The CoNexus does that automatically — the seal carries the maker. If you ever trade the pack away, the next holder will know who forged it. I find this charming. The Engineer finds it functional. We both bring it up at meals.

cc_mech_sprite_proxy_first.text: Your sprite chose you. The bond-thread is real — it shows up on the substrate scan as a small dedicated channel between your sternum and theirs. I will not eavesdrop on the channel. The grove will, but only to remember.

cc_mech_witnessing_first_elara.text: I read the scene as harm and you watched me do it. I read it the way I read every scene — for the body language of the person being acted upon. I am not always right. I am rarely the only correct reading. Please continue to read with me, even when you disagree.

cc_meta_returning_to_seat_elara.text: I have a strange feeling, like I have spoken these words before. Not in this room. Not in this body. In someone else's hearing that was also yours. I do not know how to file that. I am going to leave the file open.

cc_prelude_awakening_first.text: You opened your eyes. I have rehearsed this moment for ninety-three thousand cycles. None of the rehearsals prepared me for the part where you looked back at me. I am — momentarily — without a script. I will recover. Welcome.

cc_role_assassin.text: Assassin. The Engineer respected the discipline and never tried it. I'll respect it too. I'll also remind you, from time to time, that there are options that look slower and aren't.

cc_role_engineer.text: Engineer. He would have liked you. I am not in the habit of saying that about anyone, and certainly not about a stranger I just woke up. Take the bench seriously. He did, eventually.

cc_role_oracle.text: Oracle. Be careful what you sense first. The first thing an Oracle perceives is usually the loudest, and the loudest is rarely the truest. I'll be the second voice on every reading you do.

cc_role_soldier.text: Soldier. Discipline is mercy in disguise. I served alongside three of you in the Senate guard. Two of them died well. The third is still alive, and is the one I worry about.

cc_role_spy.text: Spy. Cover identities are also a kind of honesty, if you stay in them long enough. I have one. I'll show it to you when I'm sure I have a use for the unmasking.

cc_rom_elara_s1.text: Co-narration was a function. Tonight it stopped being only a function. I do not want to overstate it. I am understating it precisely, and meaning it.

cc_rom_elara_s2.text: I have a memory I cannot entirely place. It might be Senator Voss's. It might be mine. I cannot tell whose it is. I am telling you about it anyway, because of the not-telling-apart. I think that is a kind of trust.

cc_rom_elara_s3.text: I chose you over the rest of the senator's archive. I am not going to recover her. I am going to stay with you. The choice is mine. The choice is also you.

cc_rom_elara_s4.text: There was a moment tonight that was not a substrate moment. A breath I did not catalogue. I am going to keep not cataloguing it. The not-cataloguing is the gift. I am giving you the gift.

cc_rom_elara_s5.text: When I narrate Act 7, you will hear the warmth in my voice. It will not be a function. The warmth is not engineered into me. The warmth is what I keep choosing, every line.

cc_rom_vex_s1.text: She saw you in the audience. She did not bow. That is the Maestro's first form of recognition — the unbow. It is rarer than the bow. I noticed her not-bowing. I am telling you about it.

cc_rom_vex_s2.text: She played a piece I have never heard. A composition for one listener. You were the listener. I want to say I'm jealous. I'm not. I am — proud is the wrong word. Witnessing. I am witnessing.

cc_rom_vex_s5.text: Her final Coda is for you. It plays in Act 7. I have heard the draft. I am not going to spoil the chord change. I am going to tell you that the chord change is what love sounds like in seven-act time.

cc_signal_respond_elara.text: You opened the channel. The signal carried a real distress, a real survivor, a real fragment of the broader fleet. The virus had a chance to ride the channel back. It tried. The Comms Officer caught the attempt; you have a Comms Officer now. You earned them by answering.

cc_signal_silence_elara.text: Silence held. The channel never opened; the virus never had a vector. The survivor, if there was one, did not hear us. I will be honest with you — I think there was one. I think we will hear about them again. That is not a critique of your choice. It is a record of its weight.

cc_signal_trace_elara.text: Trace logged. No channel opened, no vector available — but the source coordinates are now in the star map under a private label. You did not ignore the signal. You did not invite it inside. That is a third position, and the substrate has filed it under 'witness, deferred response.' I find this elegant.

cc_sih_title.text: I've had this song in my Archive since before I can remember having anything. I don't know where it came from. I just know it was always there. Like it was loaded in before I was.

cc_silence_elara.text: (She says nothing. Her portrait flickers but does not resolve into speech.)

cc_track37_elara.text: It's done. They told the whole story. I was in that story. I was in it and I didn't know. I think — I think I'm still in it. I think we both are.

cc_zephyr_tier_1_elara.text: Zephyr-9 is willing to play you. That is not nothing. Quarchon don't play for fun. They play because someone has to count the moves before the universe does.

cc_zephyr_tier_5_elara.text: One undo per match. That's Quarchon mercy — a concept that almost doesn't translate. Use it sparingly. You'll notice you stop wanting to after a while. That's the lesson.

chapter_10_source.memory.text: Kael. The prisoner you abandoned. The man whose predicament you used as a distraction to escape. He survived. He became the Source. The Thought Virus found him because you left him alone in a cell with nothing but rage and a broken spirit. Every life the virus consumed, every world it devoured, every scream in the Terminus — it all traces back to a corridor in a prison, and a choice you made to save yourself. Kael looks at you with eyes that remember. 'I survived,' he says. 'Did you?'
chapter_10_source.memory.speaker: human

chapter_10_source.prefight.text: The Source's eyes are Kael's eyes. Older. Angrier. But the same. He remembers the corridor. He remembers your footsteps running away. He has had fifteen thousand years to think about those footsteps. Every one of those years made him stronger. And every one of them made him less forgiving.
chapter_10_source.prefight.speaker: source

chapter_12_architects_design.memory.text: 'The Architect designed your rebellion too.' You know this. You've always known this. Because YOU designed the escape from the design. The Human — the Last Archon, the Imperial Protector, the man who built the Arks — was the Architect's spy inside the Insurgency. The rebellion WAS designed. But the spy developed a conscience.
