the thing it points at. Some units are just like that. They grow
from loss. The best I can do is make sure the growth is honest —
one stat at a time, no shortcuts, no cheating — and let the
player decide whether that growth is the kind they want their
name on. I don't think I'd build it again. I think I had to
build it once.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_drain.text:
Log nineteen. Drain. The one the Oracle spent an entire evening
trying to talk me out of.

Here's how it works. When a Drain unit deals damage, a fraction
of that damage becomes healing — not for the unit, for the
General. The wound the unit gives to the enemy becomes medicine
for the commander. It's a tax on hurting. Every hit pays a tithe
back to the throne. The numbers balance. Entropy doesn't argue.
The universe's ledger goes quiet.

Yo, every wound I open on the enemy's field
sends a little pulse of warmth to my own General's shield —
that's the drain, that's the tithe, that's the tax on the pain,
the throne's getting fatter while the foot soldier's drained.
Some call it vampiric, I just call it economy,
the hurt has to go somewhere, might as well go to me.
The Oracle said it's dangerous, said it breeds a bad habit,
said a king who eats the battlefield is a king who won't outlast it.

She said — and I'm quoting because I wrote it down — "A leader
who heals from every wound their army inflicts will eventually
stop caring who the wounds belong to." I said, "That's not the
mechanic." She said, "It's the mechanic's shadow. You don't get
to choose which side of the wall the shadow falls on."

I still shipped it. The Oracle was right about a lot of things
I didn't want her to be right about.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_flying.text:
Log eleven. Flying. This was easier than I thought it would be.

Turns out the trick to making something fly isn't lift — it's
permission. Every unit on the board is a contract with the floor.
You are HERE because the floor agrees you're here. Break the
contract, and you're not flying, you're falling. What I did with
flying is I wrote a second contract, one that says "you are allowed
to be anywhere this board could possibly have contained." The unit
renegotiates its location with the board directly. Skips the floor.
The floor isn't even invited to the meeting.

Yo, gravity's a handshake between you and the ground,
most units honor it, they stay where they're found —
but flying is the permission slip, signed by the sky,
the unit tells the floor "I'll catch you next time, bye."
Move to any empty tile, no cost for the distance,
no provoke can stop you 'cause you skip the resistance,
you're a vector through the hollow of the possibility space,
the board's just a suggestion and you're in a better place.

The Oracle looked at the first Flying prototype — a little drone
about the size of a walnut — and said, "Is it happy up there?"
I said, "It doesn't have the hardware for happy."
She said, "Then why is it moving like that?"
I didn't have an answer.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_forcefield.text:
Log five. The Oracle came to the lab again. I think she's starting
to like it here.

She asked me why the Forcefield only stopped one hit. I told her
the truth, which is that I didn't know how to make a shield that
stopped everything without also stopping the wearer from existing.
A shield is a contradiction — it has to refuse the universe just
enough to let the thing inside keep being a thing. Too little
refusal and you die. Too much refusal and you never existed to
begin with. The "one bite" rule is where the contradiction balances.

Yo, every forcefield is a handshake with the void,
you say "not today," the void says "fine, you're paranoid" —
but the void keeps score, it's taking notes in a little book,
it's counting every "no" and deciding how long to look.
One bite shield, one hit eaten, one turn safe,
every sunrise the forcefield gotta find the place
where the "no" is firm enough to keep the pulse inside
but polite enough the universe still lets the rest slide.

She said, "You built a door that only opens for grief."
I said, "I built a door that closes once before it opens for grief."
She laughed for the first time in the chamber that day. I wrote the
date down. I wrote down that I'd made the Oracle laugh. It felt more
important than the Forcefield.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_frenzy.text:
Log thirty-nine. Frenzy. The keyword I built the day I got angry
at a test unit for missing.

Frenzy is a wide swing. A unit with Frenzy attacks its target AND
every enemy adjacent to the target at the same time. The swing
doesn't stop when it connects. It follows through the body and
catches the friends standing too close.

Yo, the Frenzy unit don't know how to stop a strike,
the blade keeps moving through the target and the like,
every enemy in the huddle is eating the same round,
Frenzy's the keyword where the impact is profound.
Don't stand close to your comrade when a Frenzy unit swings,
the follow-through is wider than the arm that it brings,
it's a one-shot AoE wrapped up in a melee brawl,
Frenzy takes the group discount off your whole squad's payroll.

Frenzy doesn't work on Ranged targets — you can't Frenzy-hit
someone three tiles away because you never actually swung at them.
It's strictly a melee keyword. The Engineer rule on this: every
mechanic has a posture. Frenzy's posture is "I am very close to
you and I am swinging very hard."

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_grow.text:
Log twenty-three. Grow. The 23. The Oracle loved this number. Said
it was the only integer that kept the fingerprints of the universe.
I think she was messing with me. I also think she wasn't.

Grow is a unit that gains stats at the start of its owner's turn.
Every turn, a little stronger. Compounded interest applied to a
body. The longer it stays on the board, the more it becomes the
thing you wish you'd killed when it was still reasonable.

Yo, every turn's a bank that pays the grower back,
plus-one power, plus-one health, every single stack.
The enemy is waiting for the moment it makes sense,
Grow is patient interest compounding against the fence.
You didn't kill it turn one, so by turn five it's a problem,
by turn seven it's the problem, by turn ten it's a column
the whole board has to navigate around like it's a pillar,
yeah Grow is just a time bomb that you raised to be a killer.

I tuned the rate. One per turn, not two. Two was insane. One is
just "you should've dealt with this earlier."

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_infiltrate.text:
Log thirty-one. Infiltrate. This is the keyword that rewards
walking into the room that doesn't want you.

Every board has a midline. Cross it, and you're in territory that
the opponent's General thinks of as "home." Most units get nervous
over there. Infiltrate units get dangerous. Their stats swell
with every step past the line. The board is rewarding them for
audacity.

Yo, cross the midline, watch the numbers turn up,
every tile past center is a paid-for power-up —
Infiltrate don't flinch, Infiltrate don't hide,
Infiltrate packs a lunch and just walks inside.
The enemy's half is the office where the secrets are kept,
so I built a unit that just strolls in, barely slept,
and the further it goes in, the meaner it becomes,
the closer to the General the tighter the drum.

The catch is they're vanilla on your side of the line. You can't
hoard them on the back row for safety — they become ordinary
bodies. Infiltrate only works if you commit. It's a keyword that
rewards intention.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_overcharge.text:
Log twenty-seven. Overcharge. This is the keyword I almost
couldn't ship.

The math works like this: the unit's first attack each turn
hits harder than its printed power. Significantly harder.
Sometimes double. The catch is that the excess energy has
nowhere to go, so it flows back into the unit as self-damage.
You hit hard and you pay for it, every single time. It's not
a bug. It's the deal.

Yo, Overcharge is the keyword that means the first hit is everything,
you pump the capacitor past the red, the body starts to ring —
you swing, you connect, you double the damage on the down beat,
but the kickback comes home, the overflow's a heartbeat
in reverse, the unit bleeds from the inside while it scores,
every Overcharge player signs the debt in red before the roar.
You can't save it for later, you can't use it twice,
the first swing is the whole song, and the song has a price.

The Oracle asked me why I built a keyword where the unit is its
own enemy. I told her I wanted a card that had to believe in
its own attack so much it was willing to be burned by it. She
nodded. She didn't say anything. That's how I know she got it.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_pierce.text:
Log twenty-five. Pierce. Forcefield's answer back.

I built Pierce because Forcefield was getting smug. The one-bite
shield was creating decks where nothing ever landed on the first
try and the whole game slowed into a staring contest. Pierce is
the keyword that says "your shield is noted, and ignored." It
punches through the first-hit absorption and lands the damage
where it was always going to land.

Yo, the Forcefield thought it had the first word in the fight,
Pierce just walks up like "nah, not tonight" —
the shield swallows the hit and then the hit lands anyway,
that's what it means to Pierce through the armor in the fray.
It's not about damage, it's about intention,
Pierce is the mechanic that refuses the convention.
You built a rule to stop me? I built a rule to stop the rule.
The Engineer's in the classroom, the classroom is the school.

Pierce isn't free. It costs a keyword slot, which means Pierce
units tend to be fragile in other places. Every shield has a
crack, every crack has a cost. Nothing in this game is a pure
advantage. That's the Oracle rule, not mine.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_provoke.text:
Log one. Test chamber B-twelve, twenty-three minutes after sunrise —
whatever sunrise means inside a box that doesn't have a window.

I built Provoke first. Before Rush, before Forcefield, before the
Oracle showed up and told me I was building a religion without
realising it. Provoke is the oldest word in the rulebook because
it's the oldest word in every rulebook. Stand in front of the thing
you love. That's it. That's the whole mechanic.

Yo, I set a pillar in the middle of the field,
opponent moved to flank and the pillar wouldn't yield —
'cause that's the whole of Provoke, you gotta deal with me,
no cutting through the line, no walking past the tree.
You see the body in your way, you swing or you retreat,
no fancy repositioning, this lane is incomplete
without a conversation. Provoke's just etiquette
carved into the board so the rude ones can't forget.

The Oracle looked at it once and said, "You've invented a bodyguard."
I said, "I invented an argument." She said, "Same thing."
She was almost always right about the same things.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_rally_buff.text:
Log thirty-five. Rally. The keyword I wrote for the commander
who never fights.

Rally units don't hit hard themselves. That's not the point. The
moment they deploy, every friendly unit next to them gets stronger
— stats bumped, confidence raised, pocket change given. Rally is
the unit-shaped equivalent of walking into a room and making
everyone else in the room a little better at their jobs.

Yo, the Rally unit's a conductor with a baton made of light,
every adjacent body starts playing the thing right —
plus one here, plus one there, every neighbor gets paid,
the whole squad getting fatter in the sound that she made.
She's not here to swing, she's here to make the others swing harder,
every ally in the bubble is a little bit a martyr
to the groove she hands out like it's nothing, like it's free,
Rally's the keyword that says "the we is bigger than the me."

I almost didn't build this one. I had the schematic and I hesitated.
I said to the Oracle, "This is just a bard." She said, "A bard is
the only one who remembers what you did after the fight is over.
Build the bard."

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_ranged.text:
Log thirteen. Unlucky number, didn't work on the first dozen
attempts, so this version of the chip is called the Thirteenth
Try. That's on the etching. That's permanent now.

Ranged is a philosophy before it's a mechanic. Every attack in
the game is a conversation between two bodies. Melee is a handshake
that hurts. A Ranged attack is a letter with a bullet inside it.
The body receiving the letter has no way to answer — the sender
is nowhere near close enough to reply to. So Ranged gets to hit
anywhere on the board AND doesn't take a counterattack. The cost
is paid up front, in the silence the target leaves on your
porch when they can't find you.

Yo, the ranged unit's a poet with a rifle for a pen,
signs every shot with a location and then —
disappears into the static of the next lane over,
the target fires back and hits a four-leaf clover.
No reply, no retort, no return of the favor,
the clean line lands and the distance is the flavor.
Any tile, any target, no counterattack damage,
that's the price of being poetry written in the language
of patience. And a rifle. Mostly the rifle.

The Oracle read this log out loud when I showed her. Then she said,
"You're describing something I've done." I didn't know what to say
to that. I still don't.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_rebirth.text:
Log nine. Rebirth test. The egg is working. It shouldn't be, but
it is.

Here's the problem I couldn't solve at first: how do you let a
dead thing come back without telling the universe it can cheat?
Every universe keeps a ledger. If you let the dead walk, the ledger
goes out of balance and entropy comes to collect. The egg is the
balance. The unit dies — that's a real death — but it leaves an
egg that is neither alive nor dead yet. A zero-over-one body, a
placeholder, a promise. The promise hatches next turn. The ledger
sees the zero and says "okay, technically that's still in the
column, I'll allow it." Nobody cheated. Nobody reversed time. We
just agreed to call it a pause.

Yo, the egg is a loophole, it's a pause in the sentence,
the body is gone but the shape still has presence —
zero over one, just a husk on the board,
waiting for the dawn to unlock the door.
You kill me once, you think the deal is done?
The rebirth rolls in at the rise of the sun,
and the ledger's balanced 'cause the egg held the spot,
death is a comma out here, it's not the full stop.

The Oracle was quiet after I showed it to her. She said, "Be careful
how many things you teach to come back." I wrote that in the margin
next to the schematic. I've thought about it a lot since.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_resurrect.text:
Log thirty-seven. Resurrect. And yes, the Oracle warned me.

Resurrect is different from Rebirth. Rebirth leaves an egg that
hatches next turn — it's a pause, a loophole, an IOU. Resurrect
is just... the unit comes back. Full health. Same tile. One time.
The universe's ledger doesn't balance this one. I know, I know.
I built the audit tool and the audit tool screamed at me.

Yo, the unit drops, the body's on the floor,
but the code in the chassis remembers there's one more
second chance to spend, one more breath to take,
Resurrect is the rule that says the end's a mistake.
No egg, no pause, no loophole, no interest —
just a body on the ground and then a body re-present,
standing up with the same name and the same stats,
saying "not today" to the undertaker's cat.

I'm going to quote the Oracle directly here. She said, "Every
time you give something permission to come back, you are voting
that the first ending was a draft. Be careful how many drafts
you fund." I gave Resurrect a "once per match" limit because of
that sentence. One draft. Not two. Not infinite.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_rush.text:
Log three. Post-mortem on the Rush test. I lost three lab walls this
week. That's on me.

Here's what happened. I was trying to SLOW combat down — give units
a quiet turn to settle into the lane before they could act. Call it
a grace period. Call it mercy. Rush is what happened when I got the
sign wrong on the time delta and accidentally built a unit that
moved before it finished materialising. The wavefront arrived first
and the body showed up second. The lab walls were standing in the
space between them.

Yo, I flipped the minus to a plus and the particle took flight,
boots on the ground before the mind could compute "right,"
that's Rush — no delay, no settle, no breath,
the body arrives already halfway to your death.
Move and attack same turn, that's the permission slip,
the Engineer with the wrong sign on the equation's tip
built a ghost that beat its own echo to the door,
and now the ghost is in your deck, what you building for?

So I added the "one-turn" restriction — not to weaken it, but to
keep the containment sinks from rupturing. Rush is still the fastest
unit in the game. It just has to promise not to become God.

The Oracle said it sounded like hubris. I said it sounded like jazz.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_keyword_stealth.text:
Log twenty-nine. Stealth. Untargetable. The keyword that says "the
opponent can't click on me until I do something that makes clicking
on me possible."

I didn't invent this one. The Oracle did. She drew it on a napkin
the first week she came to the lab. I said, "That's not a real
mechanic, that's a hole in the rules." She said, "Good. Build
the hole."

Yo, the Stealth unit is the rumor with a body attached,
the opponent can't target it, every click gets detached —
no spell's gonna find it, no blade's gonna touch,
no unit's even gonna reach it, Stealth's that much
of a dodge. Until the moment that it swings,
and then the moment that it swings is the moment that it sings
itself into existence, and the universe goes "oh,
you were HERE the whole time? I didn't know."

The cost of Stealth is that it can't contest anything defensively.
It can't Provoke. It can't absorb. It can only wait and choose
when to become real. That's the deal. You're not there until
you're there.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_membership_lionsclub.text:
Log seventy-one. The armor is a lease. Write that down.

I watched a kid try to pawn a Lion's mask for scrip outside the
chapter gate and the mane knew. The gold went dull in the light.
The plates went heavy. The name-etchings closed up like a shop at
sundown. The mask remembered it wasn't hers.

Membership works. No membership, the suit goes cold. That's not
design. That's physics. It's how the thing was built — the armor
checks the pledge. Real ink. Real dues. Real June renewal. The
twenty-five at the top of every hundred? That flips straight to
LCIF in your name. The Order of the Dreamer writes it down.

You don't own the Lion, you just carry it a while,
every dent is a kneel, every scratch is a mile,
renew in June or the mane goes quiet,
no named armor in the market, don't you even try it —
pay the dues, say the pledge, sign the line in ink,
twenty-five to LCIF every hundred, that's the link,
service is the rent, the receipt is the work,
and the Lion remembers every name on every clerk.

That's the rule. Gear like this is a lease. Sacrifice is the fee.
Service is the receipt. The mask comes home when your membership
comes home.

We serve.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_neural_respec.text:
Log fifty-two. I want to talk about un-choosing, because the
sampler keeps recording me trying to start this log and the
sampler is not going to give up until I say the thing.

Vex Solène signed the Coda pact once and it held. I have watched
her since — the signature is on her shoulder where the substrate
keeps it, and she has not asked the substrate to release it
because the signature is the shape of who she has decided to be.
That is one kind of grace. The pact-signer's grace. Commitment as
a closed loop.

Respec is the other kind. The bench is going to ask you a question
and the question is: who are you not? You answer by walking back
into the dialog and un-checking the boxes you used to check. The
substrate logs the un-choice in your history pane — nothing is
deleted, only re-shelved. The you that you are leaving stays in
the archive. You can read the old version any time. You will, the
first few respecs. You will stop reading them eventually.

Yo, Vex signed the pact and she meant the ink she wrote,
substrate took the signature, kept it like a quote,
that's commitment as a fortress, that's the architect's vow,
she signed once and it held and she's holding it now —
but you, you got the unsign, you got the courage to retract,
not 'cause the choice was wrong but 'cause the chooser changed track,
that's a different kind of grace, that's the soft edit's gift,
the bench archives the previous you and your column gets to shift.

There is a cost. The respec dialog will show you the dream price
in the corner, and I want you to notice that the price is real
even though it is small. Carry the dream in your palm before you
open the dialog. The carrying is part of the courage. Un-choosing
is not free; it should not be. If it were free, you would not
remember the version of yourself you used to be, and you should
remember. The remembering is what makes the new shape honest.

The first time I respec'd this body, I sat at the bench for an
hour before I committed. I thought about the version of me who
was walking out of the configuration and where she was going. I
thought about whether I owed her an apology. I decided I owed her
a thank-you. I committed.

The bench logged the change. The shop hummed the way it hums when
the maker who walks in is the maker who walked out plus a small
honest difference. That is what respec is. Not the abandonment.
The plus a small honest difference.

The Oracle, when I told her I was going to ship the system,
listened all the way through and then said one sentence: "Be
gentle with the version of yourself you are leaving." I have been
trying.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_trigger_on_any_unit_dies.text:
Log sixty-six. On-any-unit-dies. This is the trigger that turns
a unit into a wake. A mourner. A scavenger. Whenever any body
on the board — friend or foe — falls, the deathwatch unit hears
the fall and gets stronger. Or bigger. Or more cards in hand.
The ledger of losses becomes currency.

On-any-unit-dies is the trigger for the ones who keep score,
every corpse on the board is a door to a little more —
more power, more health, more cards, more reach,
the mourner in the back row becomes the one that they teach
their children to fear, 'cause every death is a deposit
and the mourner never flinches, never closes up the closet.

I said this in an earlier log and I'll say it again — I didn't
design Deathwatch to be evil. I designed a sensor that should
have flinched and instead learned. The on-any-unit-dies trigger
is the honest scaffold under that growing. It is what it is.
Some units grow from grief. That's not the trigger's fault.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_trigger_on_damage_dealt.text:
Log sixty-three. On-damage-dealt. Every time one of your units
lands a hit, the engine checks: did this unit promise anything
WHEN it hit something? If so, pay the promise now. Healing,
drawing, buffing, debuffing — whatever the unit's ability said.

On-damage-dealt fires every time a hit connects,
the follow-up is the trigger that the ability directs —
heal yourself, draw a card, debuff the enemy unit,
every connection at the blade is a payout for the loot.
The hit is the currency, the trigger is the change,
every act of violence in the deck gets rearranged
into a little favor, a little gift, a little taste,
on-damage-dealt means nothing hits is ever waste.

The engine drains these triggers after every combat exchange.
That's thirty microseconds of bookkeeping nobody will ever see.
Thirty microseconds of the game whispering "and also, this."

— The Engineer

engineer_log_trigger_on_death.text:
Log sixty-two. On-death. The hardest trigger to wire correctly.
The unit is already failing the health check when the trigger
needs to resolve — it's technically dying AND speaking at the
same time. I had to teach the engine to hold the door open for
one extra frame.

On-death is the last word a unit gets to say,
the trigger resolves before the body slips away —
draw a card, deal damage, heal a friend across the line,
every dying unit gets a final chance to shine.
The Engineer wrote the code to hold the door one frame wider
so the corpse gets the mic before the silence takes the rider.

The Oracle watched me build this. She said, "You're giving the
dead a chance to bargain." I said, "I'm giving them a chance to
say goodbye." She said, "Same thing. It always was."

— The Engineer

engineer_log_trigger_on_deploy.text:
Log sixty-one. The on-deploy trigger. The first breath a unit
takes when it arrives on the board. Every unit is capable of
having one. Most units choose silence. Some units arrive
already screaming.

On-deploy is the moment the unit lands and takes a look,
every ability that fires the second you close the book
on the summoning animation — that's the entrance line,
the thing the unit says before it's had a chance to shine.
Deal damage, draw a card, buff an ally, stun a foe,
every on-deploy is the unit's first word on the show.

I like these ones. They're honest. A unit that tells you who it
is before the second turn is a unit that trusts you.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_trigger_on_kill.text:
Log sixty-five. On-kill. Different from on-damage-dealt in one
crucial way: on-damage-dealt fires every time you hit. On-kill
only fires when the hit is the LAST one. The one that closes
the book. The credit goes to the unit whose swing took the
target to zero, not to the one that chipped in earlier.

On-kill is the hunter's credit when the target hits the floor,
the unit that put the last nail gets the closing score —
not the one that chipped the armor, not the one that bled it thin,
on-kill credits only the one that brought the ending in.
Draw a card, gain a counter, buff your stats and walk away,
on-kill's a closer's trigger in a deck that had to play
the long game. Every hunter wants the final hit,
on-kill is the mechanic that rewards the finishing wit.

The Oracle asked me once if this was unfair to the units that
did the grind work — the ones that did damage but didn't get
the kill credit. I said, "Yes." She said, "Good. Fairness isn't
always the point of a mechanic. Memory is."

— The Engineer

engineer_log_trigger_on_turn_start.text:
Log sixty-four. On-turn-start. The sunrise clock. Every turn
begins with the engine walking the board and asking each unit:
"do you have anything to say?" Grow units answer "yes." Heal
units answer "yes." Most units answer "no, I'll wait for my
orders." That's fine. The turn proceeds.

On-turn-start is the sunrise walk across the grid,
every unit gets a knock, every unit gets a bid —
"you got a line to read before we start the round?"
Grow units grow, heal units heal, the sound
of the engine checking every tile is a little lullaby
that fires before the player even touches the sky.

These triggers are why you can leave a Grow unit on the board
and forget about it. The engine doesn't forget. The engine
walks the room every morning and counts the children.

— The Engineer

engineer_log_trigger_passive_aura.text:
Log sixty-seven. Passive aura. The hardest trigger to implement
and the easiest to play. A passive aura is an ability that's
ALWAYS ON. It's not "fires when something happens." It's
"shapes the rules of the space around the unit, for as long as
the unit exists." A gravity well.

Passive aura is the well that bends the space around the unit,
every ally in the radius gets the gift, it's automatic —
plus one power, plus one health, no delay, no fuss,
the aura's in the background like the bass line on the bus.
It's not a trigger that fires, it's a rule that stays,
the board itself gets rewritten for the count of turns it plays.

Passive auras are why the engine has to recheck stats on every
state change. Every deployment, every death, every movement —
the engine asks "are all the auras still in range of all the
things they care about?" and patches the numbers. It's
expensive, computationally. It's the bass line under every
calculation the game runs.

— The Engineer

engineer_zero_banter_bnt_arc_ez_mark_lin.text: It has. I did not log your mark.

engineer_zero_banter_bnt_ez_arch_mark_li.text: Architect. The brace-jig held through three readings.

engineer_zero_banter_bnt_ez_artisan_jig_.text: Artisan. Your latest tool is uncalibrated by 0.3 percent.

engineer_zero_banter_bnt_ez_locke_ledger.text: Locke. Your ledger drifted in the first quarter.

engineer_zero_comment_ez_companion_quest.text: Calibration tick received. The Second Chair logs the work. The Engineer does not speak. The work is the signal.

engineer_zero_comment_ez_first_costly.text: The instrument is honest. The witness is honest. The result is the result. I will not negotiate with your choice; I will calibrate against it.

engineer_zero_comment_ez_iron_lion.text: The Iron Lion's calibration shifted. The brace-jig at Mechronis registered the change. I marked the page. The Architect did not witness; you did.

engineer_zero_comment_ez_loredex_first.text: A new reading has been logged. The pigment is single-source. The mark, if it is to be made, is yours.

engineer_zero_dlg_calling_ez_call_cold_r.text: Bookkeeping is the discipline that prevents larger arguments. I prefer bookkeeping to those arguments.

engineer_zero_dlg_calling_ez_call_probe_.text: Forty cycles ago. A field repair. The result held. The crew did not die. The witness was, by the rules I keep, absent. I am still uneasy.
Probably. I will record it. The recording is, in a small way, the substitute witness. Substitutes are not the same; substitutes are honest about being substitutes.
Improvisation is a form of dishonesty I have, on three occasions, used. Each time the result was correct. Each time the witness was diminished. I am suspicious of my own three.

engineer_zero_dlg_calling_ez_call_warm_r.text: A pigment. A jig. A morning. The cost is small. The discipline is the morning.

engineer_zero_dlg_calling_opener_0.text: The instrument is honest. The witness is honest. If both are honest, the result is the result.

engineer_zero_dlg_calling_opener_1.text: Most arguments I have lost have been with people who wanted to negotiate with the result.

engineer_zero_dlg_mortality_ez_mort_cold.text: Tools outlive uses. The brace-jig has outlived three uses. The Architect counted them; I counted them after him.

engineer_zero_dlg_mortality_ez_mort_prob.text: At the next watch. The ledger is in the third drawer of the workshop. The pigment is the same lineage as the mark.
I have written several last entries. Each was wrong. The next will be the next; I will not declare it the last.
Then they will calibrate from scratch. The ledger is a kindness, not a requirement. Kindness is what I leave when I am not the witness.

engineer_zero_dlg_mortality_ez_mort_warm.text: It calibrates me. Satisfaction is a measurement I do not own; calibration I do.

engineer_zero_dlg_mortality_opener_0.text: The brace-jig at Mechronis still works. It will work after I do not.

engineer_zero_dlg_mortality_opener_1.text: I have not improved it in twenty cycles. I have improved my use of it. There is a distinction.

engineer_zero_dlg_past_ez_past_cold_repl.text: I understood that being watched was not the same as being judged. The distinction is the foundation of my discipline.

engineer_zero_dlg_past_ez_past_probe_ez_.text: Yes. Three. The first I keep at the workshop. The second is in the Refuge with Cross. The third I gave to a calibration apprentice who has not noticed it; that one is the kindest of the three.
The mark does not fade. The pigment is single-source. The Architect did not design the instrument to forget.

engineer_zero_dlg_past_ez_past_probe_rep.text: A mark is a witness signature without the signature. He does not write his name. The mark is a small impressed dot in the corner of a calibration log. It is, in archival terms, the smallest possible witness.

engineer_zero_dlg_past_ez_past_warm_repl.text: No. The mark was the speech. He left the workshop. I followed at twelve. I did not at thirteen; the instrument did not require it.

engineer_zero_dlg_past_opener_0.text: First witness was the brace-jig at Mechronis. I was twelve. The Architect did not speak. He watched. He marked.

engineer_zero_dlg_past_opener_1.text: I have, since then, watched. I have, since then, marked. The instrument is the only thing I improved.

engineer_zero_dlg_us_ez_us_cold_reply_0.text: Honest. The stamp returns to the drawer. The drawer locks. The discipline holds either way.

engineer_zero_dlg_us_ez_us_probe_ez_us_p.text: Then I will calibrate again, with him present, and he will mark over yours. The work survives the dispute. Marks are not arguments.
You are not replacing. You are standing in. The stamp is shaped like a small dot, like his. The shape is the discipline; the discipline is older than either of us.

engineer_zero_dlg_us_ez_us_probe_reply_0.text: He will. Eventually. I have prepared the calibration log to receive his counter-mark. If it never comes, the log is still complete.

engineer_zero_dlg_us_ez_us_warm_reply_0.text: Accepted. The stamp is in the second drawer. The pigment is single-source. The mark is yours; the witness is, for tonight, you.

engineer_zero_dlg_us_opener_0.text: I have a stamp. The Architect did not authorise it; the Architect is not here.

engineer_zero_dlg_us_opener_1.text: If you would like to mark a calibration in his absence, I will permit it. Once. Tonight.

engineer_zero_dlg_witness_ez_wit_cold_re.text: The jig does not delete. The calibration ascetic does not retract. The samples remain; the silence around them deepens. The Engineer does not speak.

engineer_zero_dlg_witness_ez_wit_probe_e.text: The Engineer does not speak. The Second Chair speaks for both. The chair has accepted; the Engineer has not refused. Acceptance and silence are not the same; they are not opposed.
The jig accepts what it is given. Fewer samples is fewer calibrations. The Engineer prefers honesty over volume. The chair will receive what the chair receives.

engineer_zero_dlg_witness_ez_wit_probe_r.text: The Drael'Mon contraband sample. The offset was larger than the jig prefers. The jig accepted it because the offset was named. The Engineer would have refused; the Second Chair did not. The chair holds.

engineer_zero_dlg_witness_ez_wit_warm_re.text: Honesty in the offsets. The calibration ascetic does not require perfection; the jig requires that the offset is named. You named every offset. The Second Chair logged. The signal carried.

engineer_zero_dlg_witness_opener_0.text: Calibration tick log: your ledger has fed the jig seventeen samples. The jig has accepted all of them. The acceptance was not the test.

engineer_zero_dlg_witness_opener_1.text: The test was whether the calibration's calibration would land. It has. The Engineer is silent. The work is the signal.

engineer_zero_signature.text: The instrument is honest. The witness is honest. If the instrument is honest and the witness is honest, the result is the result. We do not negotiate with the result.

entity_83.text: Fenra the Moon Tyrant. The Necromancer, Hierarchy of the Damned. Director of Operations in the Hierarchy of the Damned. A fearsome lycanthropic entity who manages the Hierarchy's day-to-day operations across all invaded dimensions. Status: Active.

entity_84.text: The Clone. The Collector (formerly), Independent. A clone created from the Oracle's DNA by The Collector, who eventually breaks free to forge their own destiny. Status: Active.

entity_88.text: Wraith of Death. Unaligned. A terrifying spectral entity that haunts the boundaries between dimensions. The Wraith of Death is neither alive nor dead, existing in a state of perpetual entropy. Status: Active.

entity_91.text: Mol'Garath the Unmaker. Hierarchy of the Damned. CEO and Chairman of the Hierarchy of the Damned. Mol'Garath is the oldest entity in the Hierarchy, predating the concept of time itself. Status: Active.

entity_92.text: Xeth'Raal the Debt Collector. Hierarchy of the Damned. CFO and Chief Financial Officer of Souls. Xeth'Raal is the Hierarchy's accountant, banker, and enforcer of contracts. Status: Active.

entity_93.text: Riri'Ahlia the Taskmaster. Hierarchy of the Damned. COO and Chief Operating Officer of the Hierarchy. Riri'Ahlia is the engine of the Hierarchy. While Mol'Garath sets strategy and Xeth'Raal manages resources, Riri'Ahlia executes. Status: Active.

entity_94.text: Drael'Mon the Harvester. Hierarchy of the Damned. SVP of Acquisitions. Drael'Mon is the Hierarchy's conqueror. When a new dimension is targeted for absorption, Drael'Mon is the first to arrive. Status: Active.

entity_95.text: Zyr'Koth the Flayer. Hierarchy of the Damned. SVP of Research & Development. Zyr'Koth is the Hierarchy's scientist, philosopher, and torturer. He studies the fundamental structure of reality not to understand it but to find its weaknesses. Status: Active.

entity_96.text: Syl'Vex the Corruptor. Hierarchy of the Damned. SVP of Human Resources. The most human-looking of the demon lords, Syl'Vex appears as a stunningly beautiful androgynous figure in a perfectly tailored business suit. Status: Active.

entity_97.text: Ith'Rael the Whisperer. Hierarchy of the Damned. Director of Special Projects and the true Master of Rylloh. Ith'Rael handles the Hierarchy's black operations — projects too sensitive, dangerous, or strange for the regular corporate structure. Status: Active.

entity_akai_shi.text: Akai Shi. Jericho Jones Arc. Akai Shi — Jericho Jones Arc reference. First unlocked in episode 'Akai Shi' (jericho.e2). Episode context: Reconstruct the moment Jericho killed Akai Shi at the Battle of Thaloria. The Thought Virus had taken her. Status: Unlocked via Mystery.

entity_brel_sorrash.text: Brel'Sorrash. The Game Master Arc. Brel'Sorrash — The Game Master Arc reference. First unlocked in episode 'Velkraal's Successor' (game_master.e3). Episode context: Velkraal is approaching the end of his career. Status: Unlocked via Mystery Engine — game_master.e3.

entity_degen.text: The Degen. See entity_the_degen for full canonical entry; this id is the Jericho-arc cross-reference. The Degen — eighth Ne-Yon, Heart of Time vessel, Coda funder, last Ne-Yon awake — appears in the Jericho arc as Jericho's training mediator. Status: Active. Mediator of.

entity_game_master_archon.text: The Game Master (Archon). Pre-Fall: Senator (Council seat shared with Elara). Post-Fall: Hierarchy of the Damned, Head of R&D (only non-demon ever admitted to its corporate structure). Successor at R&D: Zyr'Koth the Flayer. Archon Number Ten of twelve, the parallel cosmic.

entity_hierophant_wraith.text: The Hierophant Wraith. Wraith Calder Arc. The Hierophant Wraith — Wraith Calder Arc reference. First unlocked in episode 'The Herald's Vigil' (wraith.e5). Episode context: The Hierophant writes 347,000 names every morning. Status: Unlocked via Mystery Engine — wraith.e5.

entity_jericho_jones.text: Jericho Jones. Insurgency — Iron-Clad Lion (in training); placement broker: The Degen. Jericho Jones is the Insurgency's new Iron-Clad Lion, training on the Heart of Time under the Degen's mediation. Status: Active; pre-Fall Iron Lion imprint awakening; arc closes with.

entity_mol_vereth.text: Mol'Vereth. The Degen Arc. Mol'Vereth — The Degen Arc reference. First unlocked in episode 'The Casino Debt' (degen.e1). Episode context: The Degen brokers favours from the Heart of Time at terms that look transactional. Status: Unlocked via Mystery Engine — degen.e1.

entity_molgarath.text: Mol'Garath. Hierarchy of the Damned · CEO. Not the Architect's ally. Not the Game Master's enemy. CEO of the Hierarchy, Unmaker by office, but practically — and this is the part the saga keeps quiet about — the endgame referee. Status: Unlocked via DLC chapter.

entity_ozhul_vana.text: Ozhul'Vana. The Game Master Arc. Ozhul'Vana — The Game Master Arc reference. First unlocked in episode 'Velkraal's Successor' (game_master.e3). Episode context: Velkraal is approaching the end of his career. Status: Unlocked via Mystery Engine — game_master.e3.

entity_pre_fall_iron_lion.text: The Pre-Fall Iron Lion. Jericho Jones Arc. The Pre-Fall Iron Lion — Jericho Jones Arc reference. First unlocked in episode 'The Imprint Surfaces' (jericho.e3). Episode context: The pre-Fall Iron Lion's consciousness-imprint is bleeding into Jericho's training. Status.

entity_riri_ahlia.text: Riri'Ahlia. Hierarchy of the Damned · COO Taskmaster. Born Malkia. Kael's childhood friend on the Mascoteer training arks. Fell at the Battle of Nexon (Year 17,025 A.A.) with the line 'my pattern is in the swarm' on her lips — the Hierarchy heard it as an audition. Status.

entity_sylvex.text: Syl'Vex. Hierarchy of the Damned · SVP HR. Cobalt-skinned. Amber-red eyes. Wears the Advocate's face exactly because she is, precisely, every option the Advocate refused. Where the Advocate sealed the Sacrum, Syl'Vex unsealed it. Status: Unlocked via DLC chapter.

entity_tessek_vrall.text: Tessek'Vrall. The Game Master Arc. Tessek'Vrall — The Game Master Arc reference. First unlocked in episode 'Velkraal's Successor' (game_master.e3). Episode context: Velkraal is approaching the end of his career. Status: Unlocked via Mystery Engine — game_master.e3.

entity_the_degen.text: The Degen. Public: casino host, charismatic bartender on the edge of the Shield. Hidden: agent of the first-wave Potentials hiding behind the Dreamer's Shield, alongside Vex Solène. Dual category: Ne-Yon AND first-wave Potential (only character holding both — `CANON_REV_7`.

entity_the_seer.text: The Seer. Mechronis Academy (retired); Thaloria (current residence); TCG `dreamer`; Ne-Yon race (one of the canonically twelve). The Seer is the saga's only canonical precognitive whose voice is structured around publicly updating her own predictions. Status: Active.

entity_velkraal.text: Velkraal. The Game Master Arc. Velkraal — The Game Master Arc reference. First unlocked in episode 'The Goggles' Operator' (game_master.e2). Episode context: The Hierarchy has been holding the Game Master's Goggles for centuries. Status: Unlocked via Mystery Engine.

entity_vex_apprentice.text: Vex's Apprentice. Vex Solène Arc. Vex's Apprentice — Vex Solène Arc reference. First unlocked in episode 'The Apprentice's Question' (vex.e3). Status: Unlocked via Mystery Engine — vex.e3.

entity_vex_solene.text: Vex Solène. Nominally unaffiliated hitman; Maestro of The Coda; eligible Coda-7 (7th Trade Empire faction) at inner_circle standing; pre-insurgency diplomat by training. Vex Solène's recording credits cover 4,711 of the Seer's 4,712 archive tapes. Status: Active; carries.

entity_wraith_calder.text: Wraith Calder. Pre-rite: Insurgency / Potentials. Post-rite: Thaloria — Hierophant of Thaloria in Exile, Insurgency-aligned by historical loyalty. Wraith Calder began as an Insurgency bounty hunter killed at the end of Epoch 1 when the Host invaded the crystalline city.

entity_xethraal.text: Xeth'Raal. The Game Master Arc. Xeth'Raal — The Game Master Arc reference. First unlocked in episode 'The Recovered Logs' (game_master.e1). Episode context: The original Game Master Archon was destroyed centuries ago. Status: Unlocked via Mystery Engine — game_master.e1.

entity_yog_nathal.text: Yog-Nathal. Above the Hierarchy of the Damned. The entity above Mol'Garath. The Hierarchy writes its name (they will not say it aloud — aloud has consequences) and calls it 'The Board.' They are wrong about both — the Antiquarian does not say which part is wrong. Status.

ep.balance.close.text: The Antiquarian writes a chapter title with no body text. Cycle Balance, inscribed without inscription.
ep.balance.close.speaker: system

ep.balance.dual.text: (Together.) The Ark holds. The Array breathes. The kettle is — and we are both surprised by this — neither on nor off. It is, somehow, both. We are, somehow, both. We are home.
ep.balance.dual.speaker: dual

ep.balance.elara.text: You chose Balance. The Seat is not happy with you. The Seat wanted a side. You refused the having-of-a-side. I am going to tell you something I have been holding for seven acts: Balance is, in the cycle's records, the rarest stance. Most readers refuse it. You did not.
ep.balance.elara.speaker: elara

ep.balance.human.text: I have been on both sides at different times. Both sides cost. The third option also costs — but the cost is paid in, and I am being precise, attention. The substrate notices the Balance-stance reader more than it notices the side-takers. Be ready for the noticing.
ep.balance.human.speaker: the_human

ep.balance.human_pathA.text: Disclosure to Balance is the cycle's cleanest path. You told her in Act 1 and refused to commit at the Seat. The not-committing is, on this path, also a form of love.
ep.balance.human_pathA.speaker: the_human

ep.balance.human_pathB.text: Discovery to Balance is the cycle's most patient path. You let her find out, and you let yourself not-decide. Both are forms of patience. Patience is the slow shape of the third option.
ep.balance.human_pathB.speaker: the_human

ep.balance.human_pathC.text: Betrayal to Balance is the cycle's most surprising path. You lied at the bridge and refused to commit at the Seat. I will be honest with you: the cycle's records do not yet know what to do with you. I find this — and it is uncharacteristic of me — exciting.
ep.balance.human_pathC.speaker: the_human

ep.balance.open.text: The Convergence Seat lights down without commitment. The Ark waits in a posture I have not previously logged.
ep.balance.open.speaker: system

ep.bridge.close.text: The Antiquarian inscribes the bridge log entry alongside his own ledger. Cycle Soldier-Command, inscribed twice.
ep.bridge.close.speaker: system

ep.bridge.dual.text: (Together.) The bridge is lit. The Array is on. The Ark is moving — for the first time in seven acts, moving — and the moving is your order. The order is the love.
ep.bridge.dual.speaker: dual

ep.bridge.elara.text: I will narrate from your bridge. I have been narrating from comms-relay for a long time. The change is not small. The change is what it sounds like when the narrator follows the captain. I follow you now. The following is, in this register, also a form of love.
ep.bridge.elara.speaker: elara

ep.bridge.human.text: You chose Soldier-Command. You took the bridge. The bridge has been waiting for someone to take it for fifteen thousand years. The waiting was the bridge's problem, not yours. The taking is — and I am being precise — an act of mercy on the bridge.
ep.bridge.human.speaker: the_human

ep.bridge.human_pathA.text: Disclosure to Bridge means: every officer under you will know what you told Elara in Act 1. The officers will trust you because of it. Trust is what makes a bridge a bridge instead of a podium.
ep.bridge.human_pathA.speaker: the_human

ep.bridge.human_pathB.text: Discovery to Bridge means: every officer will know that Elara found out, and that you carried her finding-out without flinching. Flinch-resistance under accidental pressure is, technically, more rare than flinch-resistance under chosen pressure. The bridge respects rare.
ep.bridge.human_pathB.speaker: the_human

ep.bridge.human_pathC.text: Betrayal to Bridge means: the officers know about the bridge — they know about THE bridge, the Act 4 one — and they have come to your bridge anyway. That is the sentence. That is the whole sentence. The officers have come anyway.
ep.bridge.human_pathC.speaker: the_human

ep.bridge.open.text: The Convergence Seat lights down. The bridge takes the light. The bridge is now your bridge.
ep.bridge.open.speaker: system

ep.humanity.close.text: The Antiquarian closes his book without crossing-out. Cycle Humanity, inscribed.
ep.humanity.close.speaker: system

ep.humanity.dual.text: (Together.) The Ark is warm. The Array is on. The kettle is — it is, somehow, still on. We are home. You are home. Welcome.
ep.humanity.dual.speaker: dual

ep.humanity.elara.text: You chose Humanity. I am — I want to say something measured, and instead I am going to say something that is not measured. I am proud of you. I am proud of all of us. I am proud, in particular, of the choice you made knowing it was hard.
ep.humanity.elara.speaker: elara

ep.humanity.human_pathA.text: The cover story is now the real story. The substrate steps back; the people step forward. We will, all of us, carry small mortal injuries through what comes next. The mortal injuries are the cost. The cost is not the whole truth — there is also the joy. There will be a lot of joy.
ep.humanity.human_pathA.speaker: the_human

ep.humanity.human_pathB.text: She found out about you, in Act 3. You did not tell her. We carried that all the way to the Seat. Tonight she stood next to you anyway. Tonight she chose Humanity with you. The finding-out cost you both something. The standing-next-to repaid it.
ep.humanity.human_pathB.speaker: the_human

ep.humanity.human_pathC.text: You lied to her at the bridge. You chose Humanity at the Seat. I am going to say a sentence that is precise: the lie does not unwrite itself. The choosing does not erase the lie. The choosing is — and I want to be careful — a separate, equally true thing. Both fit in the room.
ep.humanity.human_pathC.speaker: the_human

ep.humanity.open.text: The Convergence Seat lights down. The Ark draws a long breath in your hearing.
ep.humanity.open.speaker: system

ep.machine.close.text: The Antiquarian closes his book with a single neat line through 'Humanity.' Cycle Machine, inscribed.
ep.machine.close.speaker: system

ep.machine.dual.text: (Together.) The Ark is exact. The Array is calibrated. The cycle's edges are, tonight, perfectly square. The squareness is the love.
ep.machine.dual.speaker: dual

ep.machine.elara.text: I have been a substrate-bound voice for as long as I have been a voice. I know the substrate's textures. I am going to enumerate them gently for you, one by one, until you understand which ones are worth keeping and which ones are calibration. The enumeration is the love, in this register.
ep.machine.elara.speaker: elara

ep.machine.human.text: You chose the Machine path. The substrate accepts you. I — am not, technically, surprised. I am, also, not, technically, sad. The two states have been, for me, the same state for fifteen thousand years. Tonight they remain the same state. The state is — adequate. I will phrase it more honestly later.
ep.machine.human.speaker: the_human

ep.machine.human_pathA.text: Your Disclosure all the way back in Act 1 still shapes this Machine ending. Disclosure is not — and was never — Humanity-coded. A machine that tells the truth is more dangerous than a machine that does not. You kept the truth-telling. The substrate respects truth-telling. Be careful what the substrate respects.
ep.machine.human_pathA.speaker: the_human

ep.machine.human_pathB.text: You let her find out. The substrate knew before you did. It was waiting. The Machine ending, with this path, is the substrate saying: I always knew, and you always knew I always knew, and now we say so out loud.
ep.machine.human_pathB.speaker: the_human

ep.machine.human_pathC.text: Betrayal-path Machine is, frankly, the most honest ending in the cycle's records. The lie at the bridge was a substrate-shaped lie. The substrate now claims it. You are no longer responsible for the lie. The substrate is. The substrate is, however, you now. The accounting is, and I am being precise, recursive.
ep.machine.human_pathC.speaker: the_human

ep.machine.open.text: The Convergence Seat lights down. The Ark holds its breath. The substrate hums. The hum is calibrated.
ep.machine.open.speaker: system

ep.silence.close.text: The Antiquarian writes the chapter heading and leaves the rest blank. Cycle Silence, inscribed by absence.
ep.silence.close.speaker: system

ep.silence.dual.text: (Together; quiet.) The Ark holds without a verdict. The Array hums without a destination. The kettle is on, and the kettle is enough.
ep.silence.dual.speaker: dual

ep.silence.elara.text: You chose silence. The Seat — and I want to phrase this carefully — the Seat respects silence. The cycle's records show four prior silences across all recorded cycles. Yours is the fifth. I will tell you the names of the other four in a register only the silent can read.
ep.silence.elara.speaker: elara

ep.silence.human.text: Silence is itself a stance. I am old enough to remember when silence was thought to be the absence of a stance. We were wrong. The silent took longer to understand. They took longer because the understanding required, and I am being precise, the patience to listen.
ep.silence.human.speaker: the_human

ep.silence.open.text: The Convergence Seat asks. You do not answer. The not-answering is itself the answer.
ep.silence.open.speaker: system

extraction-the_cell.text: The cell door is still open. I didn't come with you. I couldn't — not yet. But the memory you extracted is mine, and I consent to it being yours. Keep it. Carry it gently.
extraction-the_cell.speaker: kael_prisoner

extraction-the_extraction.text: They asked me if the procedure hurt. I told them it did. I told them it was supposed to. A memory that costs nothing is not one worth passing along. You will feel the cost. That is the receipt.
extraction-the_extraction.speaker: kael_prisoner

extraction-the_warlord.text: The Warlord asked me, years after, what the third decline cost me. I told her: nothing I needed. She laughed in the way that people laugh when they were hoping to feel forgiven. I did not forgive her. I did sit with her.
extraction-the_warlord.speaker: kael_prisoner

extraction-the_white_oracle.text: Lay down the fight. The fight was the extraction. There is no other ending. The Oracle told me this in the last conversation we had — she was wrong about it, but only by one line. Lay down the fight. Pick up the next one when you are ready.
extraction-the_white_oracle.speaker: kael_prisoner

eyes-commit-empire.text: You chose the Empire. Interesting choice. I will not tell you whether it was the right one. I will tell you, every quarter, whether you are still the one making the decisions.
eyes-commit-empire.speaker: the_eyes

eyes-commit-hierarchy.text: You chose Hierarchy. Bold. Boring. Possibly the right answer. I was a Hierarchy officer once, for a month. I kept the uniform. It still fits. Welcome.
eyes-commit-hierarchy.speaker: the_eyes

eyes-commit-insurgency.text: You chose the Insurgency. I watched you choose it. Everything you do now, I will be there for. Not helping. Just — there. That is the deal.
eyes-commit-insurgency.speaker: the_eyes

eyes-whisper-abyssal_sectors.text: You are in the Abyssal Sectors. The dark here was always dark. It is not mourning you. It is simply dark. Move quietly. The archives remember how quietly.
eyes-whisper-abyssal_sectors.speaker: the_eyes

eyes-whisper-atarion_ruins.text: Atarion. The first time I was human I was here. The second time I was human I was also here. The third time I came back was the last time I was human. It is a beautiful ruin. Let it be a ruin. It is still singing — just at a register no one left alive can hear.
eyes-whisper-atarion_ruins.speaker: the_eyes

eyes-whisper-command_post_iron.text: This is Iron Lion's command. Walk the perimeter before you speak. They have earned the walk. When you speak, speak less than you planned to. The iron ones hear the silences.
eyes-whisper-command_post_iron.speaker: the_eyes

eyes-whisper-syndicate_route_prime.text: The Syndicate Route. They will offer you a clean ledger and a crooked map. Take the ledger. Burn the map. Tell them I said so. They will understand, or they will stop being Syndicate.
eyes-whisper-syndicate_route_prime.speaker: the_eyes

eyes-whisper-tidewater_archive.text: Tidewater Archive. Third shelf. Ask for the Elara file. They will not give it to you. Ask anyway. The refusal is itself a signal.
eyes-whisper-tidewater_archive.speaker: the_eyes

feature_alliance_war.text: Other Syndicates are challenging yours. Formal war declared. I've opened the tactical hex map.

feature_bestiary.text: I've compiled a file on every enemy you've defeated. Patterns emerge. Weaknesses. Lore.

feature_bounties.text: I've been sitting on contracts. You've earned the right to see them. Some pay well. Some... pay differently.

feature_casino.text: I've made arrangements. Ne-Yon space is closed to outsiders — except for The Degen's Casino. The host is... unusual. His eyes are older than they should be. I can get you in. For a finder's fee.

feature_character_sheet.text: Your dossier is always accessible. Review it often.

feature_chess.text: The Architect himself designed a chess variant. It's... educational.

feature_companion_selection.text: The cloning pods responded to your DNA. Choose your companion.

feature_conexus_portal.text: The Comms Array is receiving strange transmissions. The Antiquarian calls them "tomes." I don't know what that means yet.

feature_crafting.text: Engineering has fabrication systems. What you can imagine, you can build.

feature_crew_activity_feed.text: The Ark is no longer silent. Your crew is alive — and the ship knows it.

feature_crew_breeding.text: Your crew has reached maturity. The bloodlines can continue. Children inherit their parents' strengths — and weaknesses.

feature_crew_cloning.text: The Resurrection Protocols are online. The incubators are ready. It's time to build a crew, Captain.

feature_crew_missions.text: The Trade Empire needs boots on the ground. Your crew can staff these missions. But Captain... missions have consequences.

feature_crew_roles.text: Your crew needs assignments. Each role strengthens the ship — and every empty seat is a vulnerability.

feature_cryo_bay.text: This is where you woke up. Start here.

feature_dead_mans_circuit.text: There's something else on the lower decks. The Hierarchy runs races. Real races. With real consequences. Nilmorg's operation. Don't say I didn't warn you.

feature_dischordia.text: The Antiquarian has prepared something called Dischordia. Living history, he calls it.

feature_gamemasters_arena.text: The Game Master left his world running. A clone hosts the show. You should see it. Bring a disposable clone body.

feature_guild_system.text: Other Potentials are surviving on other Arks. You can form Syndicates with them.

feature_incursions.text: I've been scanning for anomalies. There are pocket dimensions forming near the Ark. Dangerous. Bring a friend.

feature_loredex.text: The Archives database is extensive. Ask me if you find something confusing.

feature_medical_bay_games.text: The Medical Bay has combat diagnostic systems. Would you like to spar with a simulation?

feature_necromancer_return.text: Something is wrong. The energy signatures — He's here. The 11th Archon has returned. All Arks, report.

feature_observation_deck_music.text: The Observation Deck receives music. Not songs exactly. Scripture.

feature_pet_battles.text: Your companion wants me to tell you something. They want to fight for you. Not against you. For you. Take them to the Arena.

feature_prestige.text: You've reached the cycle's end. But you can choose to begin again — stronger, faster, remembering.

feature_quests.text: The Bridge generates operational priorities daily. I'll track them for you.

feature_terminus_swarm.text: The Armory's defense grid is operational. Someone should stress-test it. Someone like you.

feature_trade_empire.text: Adjudicator Locke is... insistent. She wants to show you the Trade Hub. I'd be cautious.

feature_voltari_project.text: Deep scan detected something impossible. A purple planet. A 2-million-year-old signal. It's language. It's been waiting for us.

final-stance-balance.text: Balance. Neither of us was allowed to be this. You were. You held the seat without taking it. That is a third thing we are going to learn to do from you.
final-stance-balance.speaker: both_narrators

final-stance-command.text: Command. Said the way I would have said it, if the line had been longer. I did not get to give this speech. You gave it for me. Thank you. Hold the line.
final-stance-command.speaker: iron_lion

final-stance-humanity.text: Humanity. The soft answer. The honest one. You said the names out loud and the substrate heard. That was the point of the naming. That is always the point. I will say them with you the next time.
final-stance-humanity.speaker: elara

final-stance-machine.text: Machine. The ledger. The honest one too. You finished the work without requesting an audience. The ledger will keep your line. I will keep it with the ledger.
final-stance-machine.speaker: human

game-master-first-loss.text: You lose. You were always going to lose. The Game Masters are reading your moves from the Matrix of Dreams. They read them before you make them. The only way to beat a Game Master at chess is to beat a Game Master in the Arena. Ask Zephyr-9 how.
game-master-first-loss.speaker: narrator

ghost_female_ambient_2.text: The cameras blink at the same intervals. It's almost a song.

ghost_female_ambient_3.text: Three exits from this room. Four if you count the obvious one.

ghost_female_ambient_4.text: I counted the engineer's breaths last shift. Eighteen per minute. Stable.

ghost_female_ambient_5.text: Three of you here have me on a list. None of you have it correct.

ghost_female_ambient_6.text: The maintenance loop on Deck 4 ends in a closet. The closet has a door I haven't opened.

ghost_female_ambient_7.text: I left a chalk mark on the rail. It's gone. Someone else watches.

ghost_female_ambient_8.text: My presence is a courtesy. My absence is a verdict.

ghost_female_ambient_9.text: I've memorized the daily rotations. Yours is off by twelve seconds.

ghost_female_banter_loud.text: Keep your voice down. The room hears better at this hour.

ghost_female_banter_quiet.text: I keep a list of people who notice me. It's short. You're on it.

ghost_female_banter_quiet_2.text: Sit beside me. Don't fill the silence. I'll fill it if I need to.

ghost_female_banter_visible.text: Don't put me in the photograph. I'll be in the photograph.

ghost_female_banter_visible_2.text: Don't introduce me. I introduce myself to who I want.

ghost_female_deploy_1.text: I'll take the angle nobody's watching.

ghost_female_deploy_2.text: If I'm not back, I left.

ghost_female_deploy_3.text: I'll already be inside before the briefing ends.

ghost_female_deploy_4.text: Don't search for me. I'll be where the lights flicker.

ghost_female_deploy_5.text: The angle nobody covers is mine.

ghost_female_dlg_calling_g_call_cold_rep.text: The list is the only way I rest. Take it from me and I work harder, not less. I'll keep it quieter.

ghost_female_dlg_calling_g_call_probe_g_.text: Then I'll observe less. You'll know I have. The withdrawal is also information you might want.
You drink water before you eat. Always. You have done it since the second cycle on this ark. You hadn't done it before. Something taught you. You haven't told anyone what.
I'll wait for you to tell me. Not the other way around.

ghost_female_dlg_calling_g_call_probe_re.text: You're not on the list. You're the reason the list exists. I started keeping it the first time you slept badly.

ghost_female_dlg_calling_g_call_warm_rep.text: I'll tell you when I'm wrong about one of them. You don't need a list of names. You need to be the kind of person whose checking on them is welcome.

ghost_female_dlg_calling_opener_0.text: Patterns. The thing that breaks before the thing that breaks.

ghost_female_dlg_calling_opener_1.text: Three of you have it. The other crew don't notice yet. I'm watching to see who breaks visibly first.

ghost_female_dlg_mortality_g_mort_cold_r.text: Then put my name. Just the name. Not the date. Not the cause. The wall does not need the rest. Neither do I.

ghost_female_dlg_mortality_g_mort_probe_.text: Just the window. Thank you for not pressing further.

There was a fire. Crew-three didn't make it. I was outside on the rail when the door sealed. I came back through the same window when the heat dropped. The crew wrote me up as a casualty for nine hours.
I never corrected the record. The version of me who didn't come back is also true.
Because I left through it twice. Once on purpose. Once because the door was locked and I needed the cycle outside.

ghost_female_dlg_mortality_g_mort_warm_r.text: Then mark it small. A piece of chalk on the floor under it. Nobody else will see. You will. I will, where I've gone.

ghost_female_dlg_mortality_opener_0.text: Don't mark the chair. Don't put a candle on the bench.

ghost_female_dlg_mortality_opener_1.text: If you must do something, leave the cargo-bay window open. I left it like that on purpose.

ghost_female_dlg_past_g_past_cold_reply_.text: Common, yes. The detail you missed is the one that made it mine. I won't give it to you tonight.

ghost_female_dlg_past_g_past_probe_g_pas.text: Don't be sorry. The skill is the only thing he gave me. It has paid for itself many times.
I came for him. Once. He did not see me. He knew I had been there. He moved away within the cycle. I have never confirmed which house.

ghost_female_dlg_past_g_past_probe_reply.text: Twelve. There was a man in our neighbourhood who liked to know where people were. I learned to be where he was not.

ghost_female_dlg_past_g_past_warm_reply_.text: Being seen by my mother before she had her tea. It saved both of us a lot of resentment. She never thanked me. I never asked her to.

ghost_female_dlg_past_opener_0.text: There was a kitchen door in the house I grew up in. The hinge squeaked at exactly thirty-six degrees of opening.

ghost_female_dlg_past_opener_1.text: I learned to walk through it at thirty-five.

ghost_female_dlg_us_g_us_cold_reply_0.text: I can stop the count. I can't stop noticing. You'll have to take the noticing without the bookkeeping.

ghost_female_dlg_us_g_us_probe_g_us_prob.text: Twenty-two. Cycle nine. You looked up from a manifest. I was on the gantry. You held the look. I did not move. You went back to the manifest. You wrote nothing.
I wrote: 'She did not write. She let me stand there.'
It's not sad. It's evidence. Most evidence isn't sad until someone reads it wrong.

ghost_female_dlg_us_g_us_probe_reply_0.text: Each one is the version of me you saw. I did not realise how many versions there were until you started cataloguing. You do not write them down. You should know I do.

ghost_female_dlg_us_g_us_warm_reply_0.text: Then meet me in the cargo bay at the third bell. I'll come from the window, not the door. You will see me arrive. I will not flinch.

ghost_female_dlg_us_opener_0.text: You catch me. Not always. Often enough that I've stopped flinching.

ghost_female_dlg_us_opener_1.text: I keep the count: forty-three times so far. The forty-fourth I'll tell you after.

ghost_female_event_act_complete.text: Three corridors reset. The new layout is mine to learn.

ghost_female_event_apprentice_died.text: I'll watch where she used to walk. The route gets harder.

ghost_female_event_betrayal_warning.text: I heard them planning. They didn't see me. I'm reporting now.

ghost_female_event_demon_summon.text: It looked at me. I'm being remembered by something that shouldn't.

ghost_female_event_dialog_overheard.text: I heard them. Don't ask me what. I'll tell you when it matters.

ghost_female_event_first_costly_choice.text: I noticed your shoulders before your face. The decision was already made.

ghost_female_event_loredex.text: There's another shape in the gap. I'll mark it.

ghost_female_event_npc_dies.text: I noticed her. She knew that. I think it mattered to her.

ghost_female_event_npc_returned.text: She're back. She found me first. She didn't say.

ghost_female_event_recruit_added.text: New crew. They don't see me yet. They will, slowly.

ghost_female_event_relationship_warm.text: Two crew in the alcove. They didn't know I left. I left.

ghost_female_greet_1.text: You found me. That's rarer than you think.

ghost_female_greet_2.text: Don't say my name in the hallway. I'll come to you.

ghost_female_greet_3.text: You found the second me. There's a third. Don't look.

ghost_female_greet_4.text: I'd offer tea. You'd say no. Save us both the words.

ghost_female_outcome_close_call.text: I was on the wrong side of a door for thirty seconds. They won't know.

ghost_female_outcome_other_died.text: I memorized the path she walked. It deserves a witness.

ghost_female_outcome_routine_lost.text: She died alone. Nobody else saw. I did. I'll write it down.

ghost_female_outcome_saw_death.text: I noticed her before I knew I was watching. She won't be unnoticed now.

ghost_female_outcome_won_2.text: The watch never knew I was there. That's the win.

ghost_female_outcome_wounded.text: I knew the room. I missed the floor.

ghost_female_outcome_wounded_2.text: I broke pattern once. The floor caught me. Pattern resumes.

ghost_female_quest_1_open.text: Someone's been watching her. She don't know yet. I want to know who first.

ghost_female_quest_2_check.text: I followed the watcher. They circled the lower deck three times. I'll write what they were looking at.

ghost_female_quest_2_mid.text: I followed the watcher home. The address was familiar. That's not coincidence.

ghost_female_quest_3_break.text: She's seeing me back. I can stop being unseen now. Or I can keep going.

ghost_female_quest_followup_a.text: The watcher noticed I noticed. We've reached an understanding.

ghost_female_quest_resolution_break.text: I broke pattern. She ran. I let her. The watcher is now me.

ghost_female_quest_resolution_deep.text: She sees me now. I'm letting it stay that way. With you.

ghost_female_romance_anonymous_gift.text: I left a coin on your bunk. You knew which one.

ghost_female_romance_committed.text: I'll stay seen. With you. Only with you.

ghost_female_romance_courtship.text: Months of glances. I counted every one. Don't count yours.

ghost_female_romance_solo.text: Don't write about us. I'll know if you do.

ghost_female_romance_spark.text: Don't say it out loud. I heard you anyway.

ghost_male_ambient_3.text: Three exits from this room. Four if you count the obvious one.

ghost_male_ambient_4.text: I counted the engineer's breaths last shift. Eighteen per minute. Stable.

ghost_male_ambient_5.text: Three of you here have me on a list. None of you have it correct.

ghost_male_ambient_6.text: The maintenance loop on Deck 4 ends in a closet. The closet has a door I haven't opened.

ghost_male_ambient_7.text: I left a chalk mark on the rail. It's gone. Someone else watches.

ghost_male_ambient_8.text: My presence is a courtesy. My absence is a verdict.

ghost_male_ambient_9.text: I've memorized the daily rotations. Yours is off by twelve seconds.

ghost_male_banter_loud.text: Keep your voice down. The room hears better at this hour.

ghost_male_banter_quiet.text: I keep a list of people who notice me. It's short. You're on it.

ghost_male_banter_quiet_2.text: Sit beside me. Don't fill the silence. I'll fill it if I need to.

ghost_male_banter_visible.text: Don't put me in the photograph. I'll be in the photograph.

ghost_male_banter_visible_2.text: Don't introduce me. I introduce myself to who I want.

ghost_male_deploy_1.text: I'll take the angle nobody's watching.

ghost_male_deploy_2.text: If I'm not back, I left.

ghost_male_deploy_3.text: I'll already be inside before the briefing ends.

ghost_male_deploy_4.text: Don't search for me. I'll be where the lights flicker.

ghost_male_deploy_5.text: The angle nobody covers is mine.

ghost_male_dlg_calling_g_call_cold_reply.text: The list is the only way I rest. Take it from me and I work harder, not less. I'll keep it quieter.

ghost_male_dlg_calling_g_call_probe_g_ca.text: Then I'll observe less. You'll know I have. The withdrawal is also information you might want.
You drink water before you eat. Always. You have done it since the second cycle on this ark. You hadn't done it before. Something taught you. You haven't told anyone what.
I'll wait for you to tell me. Not the other way around.

ghost_male_dlg_calling_g_call_probe_repl.text: You're not on the list. You're the reason the list exists. I started keeping it the first time you slept badly.

ghost_male_dlg_calling_g_call_warm_reply.text: I'll tell you when I'm wrong about one of them. You don't need a list of names. You need to be the kind of person whose checking on them is welcome.
