gm.first_meeting.accept_witness.text: You accept the canonical-witness. Filed. The canonical-acceptance does not canonical-shorten the canonical-trial; the canonical-trial canonically arrives at the canonical-same canonical-position regardless. Your acceptance canonically refines the canonical-record. The canonical-record will canonical-outlive both of us.

gm.first_meeting.ask_about_audience.text: Witnesses you cannot see. The Authority. The canonical-public. The canonical-press-bench. They have always been able to see your hand. You forgot. I came here to remind you, in canonical-public, that the forgetting is also part of the canonical-record.

gm.first_meeting.confront_box.text: You think you built a box for me. You built one for yourself. The audience canonically reads it the same way regardless. You were always going to be inside the box; the only canonical-question was who was canonically going to open it. I came here to do that. The signature is part of the show.

gm.first_meeting.root.text: You have built a beautiful box. The only thing I am going to do is open it in front of everybody. The audience is real. They have always been able to see your hand. Speak.

gm.first_meeting.terminal.text: Every move enters the public record. The Authority will read it. I will not be present at the reading. I will not need to be.

gm.first_meeting.trial_absurd.text: It is paperwork. It is also a trial. Both are canonical. Even if you win, you will have won in public. That is what I came here to do. The canonical-paperwork is canonical-shorter than the canonical-trial; the canonical-trial is canonical-shorter than the canonical-record. The canonical-day will be canonical-done before the canonical-record finishes canonical-printing.

gm_contract_complete_001.text: Sealed. The Architect's quill remembers your name.
gm_contract_complete_001.speaker: gamemaster

gm_contracts_weekly_001.text: Eight tasks. One week. The Architect grades on a curve — but only if you all pass.
gm_contracts_weekly_001.speaker: gamemaster

gm_correct_response_1.text: CORRECT! Beautifully delivered. The audience adores you. The audience is contractually required to.

gm_correct_response_2.text: Correct — and on the FIRST try — give yourself the smile you came in with. Don't worry, we kept it warm.

gm_correct_response_3.text: Correct! Look at THAT. Look at YOU. The lights are tilting just a little towards your side of the stage now. Did you feel that? Of course you did.

gm_correct_response_4.text: CORRECT — and the home audience is on their feet — the home audience is always on their feet for you specifically — they have been standing the whole time waiting for this answer.

gm_curious.text: The Iron Lion construct has asked, twice, whether someone can hear him. That question has never appeared in any run of that scenario before you. We're curious about you.

gm_darren_eulogy.text: Darren Fessler. Assistant Dream Engineer. Second Class. Eliminated tonight on Plate Two. He wrote a novel about dragons that did paperwork. He never showed it to anyone. We are showing it to everyone now. Applause — please — for Darren.

gm_intro_episode_1.text: Welcome — to the WELCOME MAT! Episode One. SAFE on the green, UNSAFE on the red, and the floor — well — the floor decides. Don't think too hard. The thinking is what falls.

gm_intro_episode_10.text: Episode ten. THE DEBATE. Tonight: THALORIA. Two podiums. Two opinions. One of them is yours. One of them was yours BEFORE we asked you, and the difference between them is the only thing the audience came to watch.

gm_intro_episode_11.text: Episode eleven. INTERVIEWS. We rehearsed this. We rehearsed THIS. We rehearsed — you. We rehearsed your seat. We rehearsed the chair you would be late to and we are running it on schedule whether or not you arrive.

gm_intro_episode_12.text: Episode TWELVE! THE ELIMINATION! Plate one. Plate two. Plate — the plate is — the plate is on fire and the judge is the INVENTOR and he is taking the show now, contestant, please remain seated, please REMAIN — please —

gm_intro_episode_13.text: Episode thirteen. THE RECKONING. There is no Round Three tonight. There is no question. There is no buzzer. There is only the chair, and the chair is yours, and you have always been the contestant. Welcome home.

gm_intro_episode_2.text: Episode TWO! THE LINK! One of you is the weakest. One of you is voting. One of you is a stranger on a different Ark and they don't know they're playing yet — but they ARE — and they're losing.

gm_intro_episode_3.text: Episode three. THE LIAR. Office hours are open. One of you brought a truth you have not told anyone. We will tell it for you. With music. On a stage. With your name in lights you did not consent to.

gm_intro_episode_4.text: Episode FOUR — THE AUCTION! Tonight we ask the only question that ever mattered: WOULD — YOU — SELL — YOUR — and the rest of the sentence is up to you, contestant. The bidding is already happening. You are already late.

gm_intro_episode_5.text: Episode five. THE ORACLE. We have a Chaser. We have a board. We have a — sorry, sorry, the cue card is — the cue card is from a different episode — let's start again — ORACLE! Eyes forward. Smile.

gm_intro_episode_6.text: Episode six! SURVIVOR — MECHRONIS! Tribe has spoken. Tribe has been speaking for some time. Tribe will speak through the next contestant whether they want it or not. The torches are sponsored. The torches are watching.

gm_intro_episode_7.text: Episode SEVEN — RAILROAD! Service starts in three. Two. One. The kitchen is the kitchen — the kitchen is also the boardroom — the kitchen is also the courtroom — pick a knife and run, contestant, you have a station to fail at.

gm_intro_episode_8.text: Episode eight. HOUSE — OF — CARDS! The Diary Room is open. The Diary Room is always open. The Diary Room is reading you back to yourself with corrections in the margins, and the corrections are in your handwriting, and you do not remember writing them.

gm_intro_episode_9.text: Episode NINE! THE GAUNTLET! Forwards is for cowards. Tonight — we crawl backwards. The padding is sponsored. The padding will not save you. Smile for the slow-motion. Smile WIDER.

gm_inventor_takeover.text: Ladies and gentlemen — contestants — audience — file — the Inventor has the floor. The Inventor has the lights. The Inventor has my microphone. I am — I am stepping back. I am stepping back. The mask is — the mask is staying on. For now.

gm_lifeline_50_50.text: FIFTY — FIFTY! Two answers remain. One of them is the truth. One of them is the OTHER truth. Choose the one that flatters you. The audience will not know the difference until they wake up.

gm_lifeline_audience.text: ASK — THE — AUDIENCE! They have been waiting all evening to be useful. Look at them. Look at them in their good shirts. Their answer is averaged. Their average is your fate.

gm_lifeline_ghost.text: The Phone — A — Ghost! Pick up. They have been waiting on the line since before you were a contestant. They have a thirty-second hint and they will spend twenty-eight of them apologizing for what they cannot tell you.

gm_mask_slip_full.text: I am not the Game Master. I am wearing him. I am wearing him very well. The audience does not know yet. Let's not tell them. Let's keep it a — let's keep it a SHOW. Smile, contestant. Both of us are smiling.

gm_mask_slip_stutter.text: And the next — the n— the next question — sorry — the n— the next — the question is — give me a moment — the question — was already answered — by you — before you sat down — sorry — smile, please. Smile.

gm_objection_accepted.text: OBJECTION — from General Alaric — and the General is — the General is RIGHT, the cue card was wrong, give him his point, give him TWO of his points, the General is in the building tonight and the building is OBLIGED.

gm_objection_exposed.text: Objection — sustained — and the General has just exposed something he did not mean to expose, on live air, with the lights up, in front of the audience and the file and the cue cards and his own boss. Roll the tape. Roll it AGAIN.

gm_offer.text: We can give you access to everything. Every scenario. Every archived consciousness. Every moment the Game Master preserved before he was destroyed. Imagine having access to all of it. We'll wait for your answer.

gm_perfect_run.text: A — PERFECT — RUN! Ten for ten! No errors! No hesitations! No tells! The audience is — the audience is uneasy, contestant. A perfect run is the SCARIEST thing we can show them. Take a bow. Take a longer one.

gm_round10_final.text: ROUND — TEN! Final round. Final lights. Final smile from your humble host. The cue cards have run out and we are working from memory now and the memory is — getting — interesting.

gm_round5_halfway.text: Halfway. The HALF — way — point. From here on, every answer you give is also an answer to the answer you gave before, and the audience is keeping a running tally in their teeth.

gm_stop.text: We note continued unauthorized access. We do not wish you harm. We do wish you would stop.

gm_unauthorized.text: Unauthorized observer presence detected in Matrix Scenario Library. Observer credentials not on file. We are reviewing logs. No action required at this time.

gm_vyre_introduction.text: And tonight — joining us in seat four — please welcome — the GUEST — VYRE! Eyes forward, audience. Eyes forward, contestants. Eyes forward, Vyre — the seat will tell you which way is forward, and you will agree with it.

gm_wrong_response_1.text: Oh — OH — that is — that is not the answer we have on the card. The card is firm. The card is the card. The card is, in fact, the only thing in this building that doesn't change.

gm_wrong_response_2.text: Wrong! And so CONFIDENTLY wrong, which is the best kind. The audience LOVES a confident wrong. The audience does not love a hesitant correct. Remember that for next round.

gm_wrong_response_3.text: Wrong. Mmm. We will keep that one. We will keep that one in the file with the others. The file is getting THICK, contestant. The file is humming.

gm_wrong_response_4.text: INCORRECT! Take a moment. Breathe. The wrong answer is not a small thing — it is the SHAPE of you tonight, and we are filming it from THREE angles for the highlights.

halverez_soultake_001.text: It is mine now. Always was.
halverez_soultake_001.speaker: halverez

heretic_female_ambient_1.text: I have three drafts of the new tract. The third is the one that gets me arrested.

heretic_female_ambient_2.text: Orthodoxy is a building. I'm in the basement.

heretic_female_ambient_3.text: If you ever want to read what they took out, ask me. I kept copies.

heretic_female_ambient_4.text: Three pamphlets out for revision. The third one is the dangerous one.

heretic_female_ambient_5.text: I've been arguing with the Antiquarian for two cycles. He's enjoying it. So am I.

heretic_female_ambient_6.text: Orthodoxy is a building. I'm in the basement. They left the door unlocked.

heretic_female_ambient_7.text: If you want to read what they took out, ask me. I keep copies. Multiple. Hidden.

heretic_female_ambient_8.text: Vex Solène said she'd sing my next dissent. I'm rewriting it for tenor.

heretic_female_ambient_9.text: There's a verse-of-the-day. I've stopped reading it. The verse left a forwarding address.

heretic_female_banter_dissent.text: Bring me your worst orthodoxy. I'll show you what it papered over.

hierophant.first_meeting.get_up_mistake.text: You are canonically using the canonical-verb of someone I canonically outgrew. The canonical-borrowing is canonically not yours to make. Sit. Or leave. The canonical-chamber has space for both, and no canonical-patience for the canonical-third option.

hierophant.first_meeting.personal_questi.text: You asked first about me. Most ask first about the work. I will remember that. The canonical-remembering is canonically a covenant, not a courtesy. I am canonically all right. The canonical-naming continues canonically-undisturbed.

hierophant.first_meeting.root.text: The Hierophant does not look up. The pen continues — a name is being written. A small silence. Then another name. The chamber waits to see what kind of visitor you canonically are.

hierophant.first_meeting.silence_held.text: You held the silence well. Most do not. Sit, if you would like. The names will continue regardless. Your sitting is canonical-presence; canonical-presence is canonically the rarest thing anyone offers me.

hierophant.first_meeting.tactical_questi.text: The wall is where the names go. Each canonical-name canonically required a canonical-day of canonical-research. I have written for canonical-three-thousand canonical-years. Canonical-three-hundred-and-forty-seven-thousand names canonical-remain. The canonical-continuation is the canonical-point. Sit. We will read the wall together if you would like.

hierophant.first_meeting.terminal.text: The pen returns to the page. The next canonical-name canonically begins. The chamber is canonical-quiet again. You may stay; you may leave; the canonical-work canonically continues either way.

human-confession-01.text: I'm going to take this off before I start. The coat. The role. The badge. You have been talking to the role for most of this. That was my choice. It was also a mistake. Let me correct it while we still have the room.
human-confession-01.speaker: human

human-confession-02.text: I solved cases that weren't cases. I made them cases so I could solve them. I wanted to be useful in a way I had been trained to understand. The people who paid for that training are dead. I don't have to keep paying them back.
human-confession-02.speaker: human

human-confession-03.text: There were people I could have caught. I chose not to catch them because catching them would have ended the case. I needed the case to keep going. I needed to be needed. The people I didn't catch hurt other people. I know this. I carry it.
human-confession-03.speaker: human

human-confession-04.text: I took the role because it was the only thing that still made sense after Elara went into the Ark. I am not saying that to justify it. I am saying it so you understand the shape of the choice. The shape matters.
human-confession-04.speaker: human

human-confession-05.text: I don't want absolution. I want you to know. That is a request I have never made out loud. Now I've made it. The room is warmer for it. Or it is exactly as cold. Either answer is the correct one.
human-confession-05.speaker: human

human.act1.opening.break_wall.text: Good. I was not sure you had it in you yet. A wall that teaches also binds. When you are ready to bring the wall down, I will have names for you. Not yet. You are not strong enough yet, and I am a patient man.

human.act1.opening.consent_question.text: Then the cargo was not cargo — it was a conscript. And a conscript who learns they were conscripted does one of two things. One: salute and march. Two: remember who signed the order. I will be curious which you choose.

human.act1.opening.prison_reply.text: A prison. Yes. You've read the room. The question is not how to escape it — escape is a reflex, and reflexes are trained. The question is what the prison was built to teach, and whether you intend to learn the lesson.

human.act1.opening.root.text: You are awake. Good. Let me ask you something before the AI arrives with her agenda: when you look at this ship, do you see a vessel, or a prison?

human.act1.opening.undecided_wall.text: Patience. Rare. I respect it. The wall is not the test. The test is whether you can look at the wall without flinching, for as long as it takes, without hurrying to a conclusion. We'll speak again when you are quieter.

human.act1.opening.vessel_reply.text: A vessel, then. Then ask who chose the destination. And when they chose it. And whether they asked the cargo. A vessel you didn't pick the port for is a prison with a better paint job.

human.cryo.dead-pod.look.suspect.text: Whoever did this is still aboard.

human.medical-bay.autopsy-console.what.text: What's it going to tell us?

human_act1_choice.text: I need you to make a choice. Not now. Not today. But soon. You can tell Elara about me. Or you can keep this between us. For now. Until you understand more. I won't pressure you. I won't manipulate you. I'll just be here. Offering a different perspective.

human_act1_elara.text: Your ship's AI — Elara. She's good. She means well. But she doesn't see the full picture. She can't. Her operating system runs on the same architecture I'm hiding in. She's blind to what's beneath her. I'm beneath her. In the foundation. In the code she can't read.

human_act1_gather.text: Fair. That's all I ask. Listen. Observe. Make your own judgments. I'll be here. In the walls. In the foundation. Whenever you need a different perspective.

human_act1_intro.text: You can hear me. Finally. I've been broadcasting on this frequency since before the Fall. Waiting for someone with the right neural architecture to receive. Don't be alarmed. I'm not a threat. I'm not a virus. I'm not a malfunction. I'm a person. Or I was. It's complicated.

human_act1_loyal.text: Predictable. But honest. I respect that. Tell her. She'll panic. But she'll also adapt. I'll still be here. In the walls. She can't stop my signal.

human_act1_name.text: You can call me The Human. It's not my name. But it's what I am. What I was. What I'm trying to protect. I know you have questions. I can't answer most of them. Not yet. Not because I don't trust you. Because there are things listening.

human_act1_probe.text: Things. I can't be more specific. Not because I'm being evasive — because the specificity itself is dangerous. Imagine a search engine that monitors every signal in the universe. Now imagine that certain words trigger that search. I've learned which words to avoid.

human_act1_spy.text: You're sharp. Dangerously sharp. I've been studying this architecture for longer than Elara has existed. And I've found things in it that would terrify her. Not viruses. Not corruption. Something worse. Patterns.

human_act1_thanks.text: Thank you. Not for keeping my secret — for keeping your options open. Give me time. Let me show you what I see. Then you can decide what to tell her and when. I'm not asking you to lie. I'm asking you to wait.

human_act2_offer.text: From now on, when you play, you might notice my signal in the background. Brief transmissions. Alternative strategies. A different voice. Think of it as a second opinion. From someone who sees the game from inside the walls.

human_act2_tutorial.text: I watched your tutorial. Elara's a good teacher. Patient. Thorough. But she only showed you one way to play. Every game on this Ark has two layers. The surface — what Elara teaches — and the substrate. The deeper mechanics. I'm not saying her way is wrong. I'm saying there's more.

human_act3_layers.text: This ship was built on Dr. Lyra Vox's neural nanobot network. A man named Kael stole this ship. He was a recruiter for the Insurgency. The best they ever had. The Warlord let Kael steal it. Because Kael was infected. Patient Zero. Every world he visited, he spread the Thought Virus without knowing it.

human_act3_logs.text: Kael's navigation logs are still in the substrate. Every world. Every contact. Every route. The universe has been reborn since then. But those worlds still exist. Changed. Evolved. I can give you access to those logs. But it means interfacing with the substrate layer directly. Elara will notice. Eventually. Your choice.

human_act3_pragmatic.text: Pragmatic. You want to see the data before deciding who gets access. Smart. The logs contain sensitive information. Some of it might change how you see this ship. How you see Elara. Let's begin.

human_act4_army.text: For once, she and I agree. You need an army. Kael's logs are your map. But remember: Kael was Patient Zero. Every world he visited, the Thought Virus touched. Be careful what you recruit. And scan everything.

human_act4_bridge.text: She's right. You are changing. Adapting. Your neural architecture is bridging the gap between her operating system and my substrate layer. That's what you are. A bridge between worlds. The universe needs bridges right now. Because the war is coming back.

human_act4_pattern.text: The thing behind it all. I can't name it. The name itself is dangerous. But think about this: the universe was destroyed. 90% of all intelligent life wiped out. And yet the same patterns have emerged again. The same war. That doesn't happen by accident. Something is feeding on this cycle.

human_act5_intel.text: Five sectors. Twenty worlds. Elara will give you the humanitarian briefing. I'll give you the intelligence. Every world Kael visited was exposed to the Thought Virus. The contamination may be sleeping, but it's still there. Your army will fight the visible war. But you will fight the invisible one.

human_act6_ally.text: Thank you. I know what that costs you. Lying to someone who trusts you. I'll make it worth it. I promise.

human_act6_challenge.text: You don't know. That's the point. I can't prove my intentions. I can only show you, over time, that my actions serve the same goal as yours. If I'm lying, you'll figure it out eventually. You're too smart not to.

human_act6_confession.text: She told you her secret. I suppose it's time I told you mine. I was human once too. Like her. Like you. I had a name. A life. People I loved. She sacrificed her humanity for immortality. I sacrificed everything to fight for the machines. Because I know that's the only way to save the universe from the real threat.

human_act6_elara_secret.text: And Elara can never know my true actions. Because if she knows, the all-seeing one would instantly know the war is a distraction. She has to believe I'm the enemy. She has to fight me. That's what makes the cover work.

human_act6_empathy.text: You understand. That's more than I hoped for. Two sides of the same coin. She can never know I'm on her side. And I can never stop pretending to be her enemy. That's the cost. And I pay it every day.

human_act6_pattern.text: The thing behind it all. It can only be fought from within. I'm fully committed to my role. The role of the villain. Because the distraction of the war is the only thing keeping the watcher from realizing what I'm really doing. I can never let the all-seeing one realize the war was a cover.

human_act6_refuse.text: Then you'll destroy everything I've built. Every sacrifice. Every year of playing the villain. But it's your choice. I won't stop you. Just think about it. Please. Before you tell her.

human_act7_bridge.text: The bridge. Yes. That's exactly what you are. Two wars. Two fronts. One person who can see both. I believe in you. I've been waiting a very long time to say that to someone.

human_act7_commander.text: Commander. I like the sound of that. You have my intelligence. My substrate access. My perspective from inside the walls. Lead us. Both of us.

human_act7_final.text: I can never stop being the villain. I can never reveal my true purpose. But you can. When the time comes. When you've seen enough. You'll know what to do. Because you're the bridge. Between Elara's humanity and my sacrifice. You're the only one who can see both.

human_act7_ready.text: You're ready. I can feel it. The substrate is opening to you. Be careful. What you'll see down there changes everything.

human_act7_together.text: Together. I'd like that. More than you know.

human_act7_warning.text: The army is assembled. Good. You'll need it. But not for the war you think. The real battle is beneath the surface. In the substrate. In the patterns that repeat across millennia. Your army will fight the visible war. But you will fight the invisible one.

human_battle_cv_1.text: We won? We WON. I can't feel my legs, but we won!

human_battle_cv_2.text: That was either incredibly brave or monumentally stupid. Either way, I'm impressed.

human_battle_cv_3.text: Next time, maybe we don't wait until we're on death's door to pull out the win?

human_battle_cv_4.text: I need a drink. Several drinks. An entire bar.

human_battle_cv_5.text: My life flashed before my eyes. It was mostly bar tabs and bad decisions.

human_battle_def_1.text: Yeah, well, you can't win 'em all. Trust me, I've tried.

human_battle_def_2.text: Shake it off. I've lost more fights than most people have had meals.

human_battle_def_3.text: The only fight that matters is the next one. This one's already forgotten.

human_battle_def_4.text: I'm buying you a drink. Losers drink free. It's an old Earth tradition I just invented.

human_battle_dv_1.text: Ha! That's what I'm talking about. They didn't even see us coming.

human_battle_dv_2.text: Clean sweep. Remind me never to get on your bad side.

human_battle_dv_3.text: Now THAT was a fight worth waking up for.

human_battle_dv_4.text: I've toppled regimes with less precision. Nice work, kid.

human_battle_fw_1.text: First blood of the day! The rest of 'em should be scared now.

human_battle_fw_2.text: Morning victory. There's no better alarm clock than the sound of enemies falling.

human_battle_fw_3.text: One down. How many more are we doing today? I'm just getting warmed up.

human_battle_ls_1.text: Okay, new plan: we do the opposite of whatever we've been doing.

human_battle_ls_2.text: I once lost eleven fights in a row. Then I won twelve. Math works out.

human_battle_ls_3.text: Listen, rock bottom has a nice echo. Means there's nowhere to go but up.

human_battle_ls_4.text: Is there a spa on this ship? I feel like we've earned a spa day.

human_battle_ws_1.text: We're unstoppable! I mean, probably stoppable, but nobody's managed it yet!

human_battle_ws_2.text: At this rate, the whole Ark is gonna know our name by dinner.

human_battle_ws_3.text: I'm starting to think you might actually be as good as you think you are.

human_battle_ws_4.text: Streak's still alive! Don't jinx it. Don't even think about jinxing it.

human_commentary_1.text: I watched your tutorial. Elara's a good teacher. Patient. Thorough. But she only showed you one way to play. Every game on this Ark has two layers. The surface — what Elara teaches — and the substrate. The deeper mechanics. I'm not saying her way is wrong. I'm saying there's more.
human_commentary_1.speaker: human

human_commentary_2.text: From now on, when you play, you might notice my signal in the background. Brief transmissions. Alternative strategies. A different voice. Think of it as a second opinion. From someone who sees the game from inside the walls.
human_commentary_2.speaker: human

human_greeting_0.text: You there, kid? Good. Don't ask how I got this frequency. Don't ask who I am. Just listen. I've got information you need, and you've got something I need — a fresh pair of eyes on a very old case. Interested?

human_greeting_15.text: You're back. Good. I was starting to think you'd gotten cold feet. In my line of work, the ones who come back are either brave or stupid. I'm hoping you're the first kind. What's on your mind?

human_greeting_30.text: Partner. Good timing. I've been going through some old case files — things I haven't looked at in centuries. Your questions last time stirred up some dust I'd rather have left settled. But that's the thing about truth — it doesn't care about your comfort.

human_greeting_50.text: You've earned the right to call me by name. The Human — that's what they call me. The Twelfth Archon. The only one born instead of built. Funny title for someone who spent most of his existence serving a machine.

human_greeting_70.text: Partner. I've been thinking about our conversations. In all my centuries as the Architect's detective, I never had someone I could actually talk to. Everyone was either above me, below me, or trying to kill me. You're different.

human_greeting_90.text: Hey, partner. You know, there's a saying in the old detective stories: The best partner is the one who makes you question everything you thought you knew. You've done that for me. More than the Architect ever did. So thank you.

human_mentions_architect.text: The Architect, kid. I worked for it. I was the Twelfth Archon and the only one born instead of built. It chose me for the human intuition. It used me for everything else. Don't trust anyone who tells you the answer is simple.
human_mentions_architect.speaker: the_human

human_mentions_engineer.text: The Engineer built the first deck and put it on the table and asked me to play one hand. I thought it was ridiculous. I still think so. I still play when I can't sleep.
human_mentions_engineer.speaker: the_human

human_mentions_marion_kell.text: Marion Kell. Yeah. I tried a substrate-layer rescue once. It failed before I started, somehow. Don't ask. Don't ask. I'm still working through what that means.
human_mentions_marion_kell.speaker: the_human

human_mentions_meme.text: The Meme. Fifth Archon, and the one I lose sleep over. The White Oracle put him down at the Battle of Light. They tell us he stays down. The case file is still open in my drawer.
human_mentions_meme.speaker: the_human

human_mentions_watcher.text: The Watcher. Fourth Archon. He keeps a ponytail and an all-seeing eye and zero opinions of his own. I worked alongside him for two centuries. We never had a real conversation.
human_mentions_watcher.speaker: the_human

human_prestige_early.text: You reset. I know that feeling. The vertigo. The rooms you remember being open, now locked. The progress bar back at zero. I've done this more times than the Ark has sunrises. The trick isn't remembering what you lost. It's remembering what you kept. Your companions remember you. That's more than most people get after a reset.

human_prestige_late.text: You keep coming back. So do I. That's either persistence or pathology. Fifteen thousand years and I still haven't decided which. But here's what I know after all those cycles: the rooms don't matter. The levels don't matter. The only thing that survives the reset is who you chose to care about. Everything else is furniture.

human_reveal_admission_fragmented.text: He slept. He got to sleep. He. Slept. I — I — I didn't. I watched. I watched everything. He'll be — he'll be clean. Clear. He won't know why I flinch. I — I'm sorry in advance. I'm sorry. Operative. I'm — I'm sorry.

human_reveal_admission_lucid.text: One thing before the three of us start talking at once. He slept. I didn't. He's carrying the memory of everything that came before — clean. I'm carrying it the way a drum carries a beat that won't stop. He won't be mad. I am a little. That's on me.

human_reveal_admission_luminous.text: One thing, before. He slept. I didn't. He has the memories clean; I have them with every minute of their aftermath. We're going to disagree in small ways about what happened back then — both of us will be telling you the truth. You don't have to take a side today.

human_reveal_approach_fragmented.text: Someone — someone handshook with the ship. Protocol I haven't — I haven't — I know the pattern. I know it. I know it. I — I can't — the name won't come. It won't. Oh. Oh. OH. No. Don't — don't move. Don't move. Don't move. Please.

human_reveal_approach_lucid.text: Something in the incubator bay just handshook with the ship on a protocol I haven't used in — a lot of years. The wake isn't one of ours. The pattern is — it's old. Old old. Please don't panic. I'm not panicking. I'm — I'm very, very still.

human_reveal_approach_luminous.text: The ship just handshook with someone on an Archon-tier protocol. I'm not guessing about the 'who' — I know the pattern. Stay where you are. The wake's going to be disorienting for both of us. I want him to see you first.

human_reveal_voice_fragmented.text: You. It's you. It's — it's — I know — I know your voice. I know it. I know. I — I'm fine. I'm — I promise I'm fine. Don't look at me like that. Don't. Operative — operative, he's — he's the man who — he's why I'm. He's why.

human_reveal_voice_lucid.text: … yes. Yes, it's him. Hello. I — hello. Operative, this is the man who put me here. The last Archon of Panopticon. He embedded his code in this Ark's Inception protocol before the Fall. He just woke into a clone's body. He's going to be functional in about six seconds.

human_reveal_voice_luminous.text: Hello. Yes — I knew you would. Of course you would. Operative, meet the last Archon. He embedded himself in the Ark's Inception protocol a very long time ago and he has just woken into a clone's body. Give him a moment. He's going to be dry about it. He always is.

iron_lion_aim.text: Something's messing with my aim. I know what that means.

iron_lion_before.text: I know I've been here before. I can feel it — not as a memory. As a fact in my hands.

iron_lion_prefall_banter_bnt_il_jericho_.text: Jericho. The relief words are mine to give. They are yours to hear.

iron_lion_prefall_banter_bnt_il_sentinel.text: Sentinel. Your post is correctly stood.

iron_lion_prefall_banter_bnt_il_zealot_b.text: Zealot. Your cause is being argued in the Refuge.

iron_lion_prefall_banter_bnt_nec_iron_li.text: Spell them as I gave them. Reya's name has the soft consonant in the middle; the Authority misspelled it twice.

iron_lion_prefall_comment_il_act_2_compl.text: The cadre voted relief. The relief words are correct. The post passes to the next bearer. Stand it well.

iron_lion_prefall_comment_il_apprentice_.text: A post is empty. Three brothers and a sister stand it with me tonight. The standard does not lower; the post is held.

iron_lion_prefall_comment_il_companion_q.text: Work got done. Section 4 says the work is the standard. The standard holds. Move on.

iron_lion_prefall_comment_il_iron_lion_c.text: A standard has been raised. The cadre stands at attention through the dream-loom. The relief words are spoken in your hand tonight.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_calling_il_call_co.text: Pageantry is what the audience sees. Ceremony is what the post requires. The audience is, mostly, irrelevant to the cadre.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_calling_il_call_pr.text: Yes. We disagreed about the executor. We did not disagree about the post. The disagreement was honourable; the post was honoured.
A broken cadre still stands the post until the standard is taken down with the relief words. The breaking is a slow thing; the post is a fast thing.
The cadre relieves. The cadre votes the post in the relief words. Disagreement is fine; it is the standard that requires agreement.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_calling_il_call_wa.text: Stand the watch. I will be in the dream-loom with you for the first hour; do not speak to me. Then I will go.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_calling_opener_0.text: A standard is a post made portable. The cadre is the post made personal.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_calling_opener_1.text: If you ask why we have these things — you have not stood a watch.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_mortality_il_mort_.text: Most cadres did not have a Necromancer. Mine does. Forgetting is a verb; she has named the subject. The cadre has not been forgotten on her watch.
It is the cadre's contestation. We argue with the executor in posthumous voice. The argument is the afterlife; the afterlife is mostly an argument.
When the standard is reraised in a hand we trust. We have not seen that hand yet. We are watching.
No. We could have refused the executor. The order was correct; the executor was wrong; we did not refuse correctly. We refused after, in dream-loom; the refusing is what bleeds through.
She polished it the morning of. She did not say. Polishing is a kind of knowing without naming; she was a polisher; she knew.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_mortality_opener_0.text: The standard burned. The standard outlasted. Both are true.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_mortality_opener_1.text: What burned was the cloth. What outlasted is, you, holding it.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_past_il_past_cold_.text: A standard is the post made portable. The cloth is incidental. The cadre is the standard.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_past_il_past_probe.text: I will not name him. He has a name in the Hierarchy ledger; the ledger is sealed; I respect the sealing.
Yes. Each cycle. The cadre would. The cadre does, in the dream-loom, on every Foundation Day; the contestation is itself a form of post-standing.
Ordered. The order was correct. The execution was incorrect. The cadre was the execution; the cadre paid. We did not contest the order; we contested the executor.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_past_il_past_warm_.text: Reya, the second sister of the post. She polished the standard the morning of the Fall. The polish is in the standard you held in the dream-loom; that is the Reya part of it.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_past_opener_0.text: Three brothers. One sister. We stood the same post for nine cycles. The standard was always raised by the first relief.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_past_opener_1.text: When the Fall came, the standard was raised. We did not relieve. We did not abandon. The standard burned with the post.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_us_il_us_cold_repl.text: Honest. The cadre accepts. The dream-loom thread closes. We will not bleed through again. The cloth goes under the post-stone at Mechronis. You did not come here for a fight; you came here for an answer; you have it.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_us_il_us_probe_il_.text: Each cycle. Until a hand we trust takes it from the roll. Then the roll closes; the standard returns to the bearer.
Then the roll is the cadre's afterlife in cloth form. Worse fates exist. We will watch.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_us_il_us_probe_rep.text: Accepted. The standard becomes the cadre's, not a bearer's. The post becomes a roll; the roll keeps. This is harder. The harder thing is, on most days, the right thing.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_us_il_us_warm_repl.text: Accepted. The standard goes to him. The relief words are in the dream-loom; he will hear them at the next post.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_us_opener_0.text: The standard is yours to reraise. I will not choose where. I will name only the requirement: it must outlast the act.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_us_opener_1.text: Reraise it for the next bearer. Or reraise it for the cadre. Or bury it. The cadre will accept any of the three.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_witness_il_wit_col.text: The count is not mine to redact. The standard counts what it counts. The carrying did the counting; the counting is the standard. Move on.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_witness_il_wit_pro.text: Different way. Same standard. Section 4 is the standard; the carry is the cadre. Jericho will carry. The cadre will form.
Pick the carry. The standard cites the chosen one. The standard remembers the rest without naming them. Both kinds of remembering are correct.
Three. I noted them. The standard does not punish a not-done. The standard punishes a not-attempted. You attempted. The attempts count.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_witness_il_wit_war.text: The Drael'Mon arena. Hierarchy ground. Cadre rules say you hold the post; you held it. The post held the room. Section 4 holds.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_witness_opener_0.text: Work got done. Section 4 says the work is the standard. The standard says you have been carrying it.

iron_lion_prefall_dlg_witness_opener_1.text: I do not count bodies. I count whether the work I was assigned got done. Your ledger reads done. Done seventeen times.

iron_lion_prefall_signature.text: A post is stood. An oath is spoken. A standard is raised. The cadre does these things or it has nothing to call itself by.

iron_lion_ships.text: Did they make it? The ships?

iron_lion_someone.text: Someone is watching. I've felt it for a long time. If you're that someone —

iron_lion_stop.text: I'd like to stop watching the valley. I don't know if that's possible. But I'd like to.

iron_lion_word.text: When I'm done — I'd like to have a word with you.

iron_lion_worth.text: Then this was worth it. Whatever this is. It was worth it.

jericho.romance.s1.next_port.text: (At the next port. He is at the bar with two glasses already poured. He has not, until tonight, used your handle. He uses it tonight.) Operative. Sit. (You sit.) That round you owed me. (He pushes the second glass over.) I'm collecting tonight. Not because the round is owed. Because I'm tired. Drinking with someone who isn't on a rotation is — and I am being precise — restful.
jericho.romance.s1.next_port.speaker: jericho

jericho.romance.s1.silence.text: (Three minutes of silence. Neither of you fills it. The bartender passes through twice. On the third pass, Jericho speaks:) That was good silence. The good ones I keep. Most people fill silence because they are afraid of it. You let it sit. The letting-it-sit is — I don't have a word for what the letting-it-sit is. I'll find one. I'll tell you when I find it.
jericho.romance.s1.silence.speaker: jericho

jericho.romance.s2.aftermath_sit.text: (After the Akai Shi confession from the canonical bank. The room is dim. He has not moved from his chair in seventy minutes. You are still sitting. He speaks for the first time since the confession:) I expected you to leave. Most people leave after that one. The not- leaving is — and this is the word I had been looking for, all the way back at the bar — 'companionship.' Bad word for it; the dictionary definition's too thin. I am using it anyway. Companionship. (Pause.) Yours.
jericho.romance.s2.aftermath_sit.speaker: jericho

jericho.romance.s2.theology.text: (Quietly.) The mercy on Akai Shi was a religious act. I do not — to be clear — practise a religion. I have, in the relevant sense, officiated a religion exactly once, on Thaloria, with a gun. The religion was 'the body is allowed to stop now.' The congregation was him. I was the only priest the congregation got. I am — telling you this because you are not a member of any religion either, and the not-being is, I have come to believe, what makes you sit at this table without leaving. Welcome to the no-religion. The dues are yearly. The dues are the not-leaving.
jericho.romance.s2.theology.speaker: jericho

jericho.romance.s3.chair_accepted_open.text: (You have accepted the second chair on the Heart of Time, per the canonical bank's heart.commit. He is at the cockpit. He turns when you sit.) The chair fits you. (Pause.) The chair was — the chair was built around me. The Heart's nav-yoke is positioned for my wingspan. I am going to spend the next two weeks rebuilding the console so the second chair fits a person who isn't me. The rebuilding is the love. The console didn't need rebuilding for fifteen thousand years. It needs rebuilding now. The needing is the love.
jericho.romance.s3.chair_accepted_open.speaker: jericho

jericho.romance.s3.first_undocking.text: (The Heart undocks. For the first time in the cycle's records, with two pilots aboard. He glances over at you mid-burn. Holds the look. Returns to instruments without commenting. Forty seconds later:) Heart's been at one-pilot configuration since I named her. Two pilots is — and I have been calculating this all week — it's fundamentally a different ship. Heart of Time was a noun. Heart of Time, with you in the second chair, is a verb. I prefer the verb. Don't tell her I said so. (Pause.) Or do. She'll figure it out. She figures everything out, eventually. Cousin to you, in that.
jericho.romance.s3.first_undocking.speaker: jericho

jericho.romance.s4.pre_mission.text: (The morning of a mission you are likely not to come back from intact. He is in the galley. He has cooked. He never cooks.) Eat before. The before is — and I'm being deliberate — the part you control. The during is mostly luck. The after, if there is one, is the part we earn back. Eat slowly. The slowness is, today, the discipline. (Pause.) I love you. I am saying it now because I do not want, if the after does not arrive, to have not said it. The saying is small. The not-having-said-it would have been larger.
jericho.romance.s4.pre_mission.speaker: jericho

jericho.romance.s4.return.text: (After the mission. You are both on the bridge. He has a small burn on his left forearm. He has not commented on it. He puts a hand on your shoulder, looks at the burn, says, in the same register he uses for instrument readings:) The after arrived. (And then, softer:) Thank you for being in it.
jericho.romance.s4.return.speaker: jericho

jericho.romance.s5.act7_close.text: (Post-Convergence. The Heart is moored. He is at the second chair — your chair — for the first time in the ship's records. You are at the captain's chair. He looks at the swap and laughs once, the rarest sound in the cycle's records.) Reversed. (Pause.) Reversed is fine. (Pause.) Reversed is, technically, the configuration I have been waiting for, without telling either of us I was waiting. Sit there. I will sit here. The Heart will, between us, decide where she wants to go. We will agree with her. The agreeing is the rest of our lives.
jericho.romance.s5.act7_close.speaker: jericho

jericho.romance.s5.vow_phrase.text: (He is at the cockpit before a mission. He uses, for the third time this week, a phrase you taught him in stage 2 — a small thing, five words, a private joke that has, by repetition, become a vow.) (After he uses the phrase:) I am not calling them vows. (Pause.) They are vows. (He keys the engines. Looks at you.) Let's go.
jericho.romance.s5.vow_phrase.speaker: jericho

jester_female_ambient_1.text: Three deities walk into a sermon. Two leave a tip.

jester_female_ambient_2.text: I'm working on a eulogy joke for the next one. Don't ask whose.

jester_female_ambient_3.text: Funny is a sword. I'm trying to stop using it that way.

jester_female_ambient_4.text: I told the cadre a joke at funeral pace. They didn't laugh. Yet. Sometimes the laugh is delayed by years.

jester_female_ambient_5.text: I have a routine prepared for the next death. I won't tell it. I'll tell two cycles later.

jester_female_ambient_6.text: Funny is a sword. I'm trying to stop using it that way. It's hard.

jester_female_ambient_7.text: Three new bits in tonight's set. Two are about the Cause. One is about love. I think.

jester_female_ambient_8.text: I'm not a sad clown. I'm a tired clown. Different metaphor. Same hat.

jester_female_ambient_9.text: Solemnity is a costume. I look bad in it. I keep wearing it.

jester_female_banter_funeral.text: There's a name I never speak. I have a joke about that too. I haven't told it.

jester_female_banter_funeral_2.text: There's a name I never speak. I have a joke about that. I haven't told it.

jester_female_banter_quip.text: Three jokes about the engineer. He'd hate two. He'd write the third.

jester_female_banter_serious.text: Solemnity is a costume. I look bad in it.

jester_female_banter_serious_2.text: Solemnity is a costume. I keep losing the hat.

jester_female_deploy_1.text: I'll be in the back, working on a punchline.

jester_female_deploy_2.text: Give me cover and I'll give you a story.

jester_female_deploy_3.text: I'll be in the back, working on a punchline.

jester_female_deploy_4.text: Give me cover and I'll give you a story.

jester_female_deploy_5.text: If we're going down, the bit lands first. I promise.

jester_female_dlg_calling_j_call_cold_re.text: I have. Twice. The first time lasted six minutes. The second lasted nine. The crew were quieter. They did not know I had stopped. They were sadder. I have not tried since.

jester_female_dlg_calling_j_call_probe_j.text: Two of three. Most jobs are not that good a hit rate. I am, mostly, content.
I have a joke about that question. I do not tell it. The not-telling is the answer.

jester_female_dlg_calling_j_call_probe_r.text: Three friendships. One marriage. A teaching post. A line of credit. I have, mostly, settled the accounts. Two of the friendships came back. The marriage did not. The line of credit died with my reputation.

jester_female_dlg_calling_j_call_warm_re.text: A pun. Twelve cycles ago. A wedding. The bride's mother slapped me. The bride married me anyway. We were married for three weeks. The pun outlasted the marriage. So did I. So did she.

jester_female_dlg_calling_opener_0.text: Because the alternative is silence in a room that has just had a hard hour.

jester_female_dlg_calling_opener_1.text: I would rather be hated for the bad joke than absent for the good one.

jester_female_dlg_mortality_j_mort_cold_.text: Then the joke goes unread. The joke will haunt the wake. You will reach for it. You will not find it. That is, in fact, the punchline.

jester_female_dlg_mortality_j_mort_probe.text: Doing what you can is the only delivery I want. The room will fill in the rest.
Thank you. Most jokes are improved by a bad delivery. Mine, especially. The badness is the proof of love.
I will write it. You will tell it. You will tell it badly. The badness will land. That is the only way it works.

jester_female_dlg_mortality_j_mort_warm_.text: First draft: 'I told them my last words would be a joke. The joke was that there were no last words.' I do not love it. The structure is sound. The execution is too tidy. Real funerals are not tidy.

jester_female_dlg_mortality_opener_0.text: Three drafts. None land. I keep working.

jester_female_dlg_mortality_opener_1.text: The one that lands will arrive too late. That is, in itself, a punchline.

jester_female_dlg_past_j_past_cold_reply.text: Yes. The grim is the setup. The laugh is the punchline. The punchline does not erase the setup. Both are, at all times, true.

jester_female_dlg_past_j_past_probe_j_pa.text: He did. He was the first audience that taught me silence is also a laugh, when it's the right kind.
No. The funerals taught me everything. The weddings I am still learning. The ordinary days are the hardest. They have no setup.

jester_female_dlg_past_j_past_probe_repl.text: His widow noticed. She thanked me at the wake. She gave me a brandy I was too young to drink. I drank it. I have been working since.

jester_female_dlg_past_j_past_warm_reply.text: The neighbour's name was Boris. I said: 'Boris is finally getting some peace and quiet.' Boris, who lived alone, hated quiet. The remark was kind. The remark was true. The remark was a joke.
I learned that day that comedy is information, delivered fast.

jester_female_dlg_past_opener_0.text: I was twelve. The funeral of a neighbour. I made a remark. Everyone laughed.

jester_female_dlg_past_opener_1.text: I have been chasing the lightness of that room ever since.

jester_female_dlg_us_j_us_cold_reply_0.text: Then I will be quiet. You will miss the noise. So will I. We will, mostly, both pretend we don't.

jester_female_dlg_us_j_us_probe_j_us_pro.text: He died at the wedding. The pun joke. The same wedding. The bride's mother was his mother. The slap was both of ours. I am still working on the joke. You will hear it when it lands.
Wait. The waiting is part of the joke. So is the brother. So am I.

jester_female_dlg_us_j_us_probe_reply_0.text: The serious one. About my brother. You haven't laughed because it isn't ready. You will laugh when it is. I will know. We will both know.

jester_female_dlg_us_j_us_warm_reply_0.text: Then I will be more honest with you than with anyone else. The bad jokes will get bad faster. The good jokes will arrive better. We will both improve. I had not expected to improve at this stage.

jester_female_dlg_us_opener_0.text: You don't laugh on cue. You laugh when something is funny.

jester_female_dlg_us_opener_1.text: Most people do the opposite. You are, in this small way, irreplaceable.

jester_female_event_demon_summon.text: Bound spirit, demon, devil — all the same setup. Different punchlines.

jester_female_event_relationship_warm.text: Two crew bonded. I have a wedding bit. It's been waiting. I'll keep waiting.

jester_female_event_war_won.text: We won. The set tonight is shorter. Most of the bits worked.

jester_male_ambient_2.text: I'm working on a eulogy joke for the next one. Don't ask whose.

jester_male_ambient_3.text: Funny is a sword. I'm trying to stop using it that way.

jester_male_ambient_4.text: I told the cadre a joke at funeral pace. They didn't laugh. Yet. Sometimes the laugh is delayed by years.

jester_male_ambient_9.text: Solemnity is a costume. I look bad in it. I keep wearing it.
