kael-logs-unlocked-01.text: You beat the Warden. The Kael Logs are yours. I left them there. I knew somebody would reach them. I didn't know it would be you. Read them slowly. I was a worse writer than I was an Engineer.
kael-logs-unlocked-01.speaker: engineer_recall

kael-logs-unlocked-02.text: The first log is from the month I realized Elara would outlive me. The last log is from the day I found the Dischordia Cycle. Everything in between is a man arguing with himself about what a good ending looks like. You can skip around.
kael-logs-unlocked-02.speaker: engineer_recall

kael-opener-01.text: They called me an archivist first. Then they called me an Engineer. They never once called me what I was. I built what I built so the record would outlive the names.
kael-opener-01.speaker: engineer_recall

kael-opener-02.text: You are in Act 3 now. This is the one where you are offered a role, and you will take one of them. There is no version of this that ends with you refusing every door. Choose the door you can live with.
kael-opener-02.speaker: engineer_recall

kael-opener-03.text: The Eyes will whisper. The three of them — Elara, the Human, and me — will not. We have nothing left to teach that a choice won't teach you faster.
kael-opener-03.speaker: engineer_recall

kael_close_victory_04.text: Blood and fire, that was close. But the Insurgency teaches us: a win is a win.

kael_close_victory_05.text: I've got new scars. Good. They'll remind me what we survived today.

kael_close_victory_06.text: My ancestors would say we walked the razor's edge and didn't fall. They'd be proud.

kael_close_victory_07.text: Next time, I lead the charge. You're too valuable to risk like that.

kael_close_victory_08.text: That fight took years off my life. Worth every one of them.

kael_decisive_victory_00.text: The Insurgency trains us to fight like we have nothing to lose. Today, we fought like we have everything to gain.

kael_decisive_victory_01.text: Swift. Brutal. Necessary. That's how revolutions are won.

kael_decisive_victory_02.text: They underestimated us. That was their last mistake.

kael_decisive_victory_03.text: My blade barely needed drawing. Your strategy did the heavy lifting.

kael_defeat_09.text: We fall, we rise. That's the Insurgency way. That's OUR way.

kael_defeat_10.text: Defeat is just the universe testing whether you want victory badly enough.

kael_defeat_11.text: I've been beaten before. By people far worse than this. And I'm still here.

kael_defeat_12.text: Sharpen your blade after every loss. Literal and metaphorical.

kael_first_win_13.text: Blood and dawn! A victory to start the day. The ancestors smile on us.

kael_first_win_14.text: First fight, first win. The rest of today's enemies should take note.

kael_first_win_15.text: There's an Insurgency saying: 'Win before breakfast, conquer before dinner.'

kael_loss_streak_20.text: The Insurgency was forged in defeat after defeat after defeat. Until it wasn't. We're in the 'until' phase.

kael_loss_streak_21.text: I won't lie to you and say this doesn't hurt. But pain is just the universe's way of sharpening us.

kael_loss_streak_22.text: Every great warrior has a chapter of losses. This is yours. The next chapter is redemption.

kael_loss_streak_23.text: My blade-master once beat me forty times in a row. The forty-first time, I won. He retired the next day.

kael_win_streak_16.text: We are the storm! Let them try to stop what cannot be stopped!

kael_win_streak_17.text: This is what the Hierarchy fears -- momentum in the hands of the righteous.

kael_win_streak_18.text: Three in a row? Five? I've lost count, and I don't care. We keep going.

kael_win_streak_19.text: The fire in you burns brighter with every victory. I can feel its heat.

kanevas_dissonance_001.text: Sync to me. They will move as I choose.
kanevas_dissonance_001.speaker: kanevas

kanevas_harmonize_001.text: Sync to me. We move as one.
kanevas_harmonize_001.speaker: kanevas

left-gm-first-contact.text: I read from your left hemisphere. That is the logic one. I find it disappointing in almost every species, but I am fair. I will tell you when you play well. I will not tell you often.
left-gm-first-contact.speaker: game_master_left

left-gm-first-defeat.text: You played the arithmetic correctly. The arithmetic was the wrong question. I will not tell you the right question tonight. Come back.
left-gm-first-defeat.speaker: game_master_left

left-gm-first-victory.text: You beat the arithmetic. You did not beat the question. The question is what I am for. You will see me again.
left-gm-first-victory.speaker: game_master_left

left-gm-repeat-victory.text: Again. Good. Repetition is the only teacher I respect. Come back tomorrow. I will be waiting in the same configuration.
left-gm-repeat-victory.speaker: game_master_left

little_collector_taunt_early.text: I will take your tears and your laughter both. They are both currency where I am going.

little_collector_taunt_late.text: You are running out of jars. I am not.

little_collector_taunt_mid.text: Don't fight. Just feel. I want one good one I can keep.

little_watcher_taunt_early.text: I have been watching. I will watch this too. I have watched sixteen versions of you already.

little_watcher_taunt_late.text: I will play you back to yourself, later, slower, and you will not like the editing.

little_watcher_taunt_mid.text: Number seventeen, then. Try harder. The recording is for someone who has not been born yet.

locke.first_meeting.collegial.text: Then someone is fortunate. The Authority does not often hire on behalf of someone else. Tell me whose chair you are warming. I will adjust the file accordingly.

locke.first_meeting.judicial.text: I am filing this. You read first. Most people do not. The ones who do are the ones I keep. Welcome to the docket.

locke.first_meeting.mercantile.text: Good. Business I understand. Sit down. The chair is filed under 'unpriced'. We will see what category fits you by close of day.

locke.first_meeting.predatory.text: I am filing that you said that. Sit anyway. We can find out together. Most counterparties don't ask the question that loud on day one. You did. The file thickens.

locke.first_meeting.root.text: Welcome to the Authority's ledger. Before you sign anything, I want to know which of us is buying.

locke.first_meeting.terminal.text: Now: which side of the ledger are you on today? Pick one. We can revise on the second meeting.

locke.romance.s1.invitation.text: I have a bottle of wine that does not, technically, exist. The Bureau confiscated three crates of it in 2049. Two of those crates are accounted for in the public ledger. The third is accounted for in the private one, which I keep, which has my signature, which means I took it. I would like to drink it with you. The taking is not the courtesy. The drinking with you is.
locke.romance.s1.invitation.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s1.ledger_clause.text: I am going to amend my private ledger when I get home tonight. The third crate will, in the amendment, have an additional clause: 'consumed in the company of (your name).' That is not a sentimental gesture. It is a contractual one. The contract now has your name in it. The implications are — I will consider them. You should also.
locke.romance.s1.ledger_clause.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s1.toast.text: To prospects who become — (pause; she does not finish the sentence). I will get the toast right next time. The not-getting-it-right tonight is the form the toast takes. Drink.
locke.romance.s1.toast.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s2.afterward.text: I do not regret the closing. I regret that the closing was, in the Vortex's measure, optimal. Optimal is the word a person uses when the only honest words are not available. I am giving you the history, not the optimal. The optimal you can read in any Bureau training manual.
locke.romance.s2.afterward.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s2.brief_open.text: I am going to brief you. The briefing is not work. The briefing is what I have instead of confession. You can interrupt. You can ask for clarification. You cannot ask me to stop. The not-stopping is the part I require of myself.
locke.romance.s2.brief_open.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s2.eye_history.text: Year 2046. Pre-Bureau. I was 27. There was a contract — a real one, signed, notarised, dated — to deliver a child to a family across the Vortex line. The contract had a clause I did not read. The clause named the price: an eye. Mine. The deliverer's eye. The Vortex's preferred currency for what they call 'sight-traffic.' I read the clause after I had already taken the child. The taking was already done. The eye was the only honest way to close the contract. I closed it. The child arrived. The family kept her. I kept the scar. The scar is the receipt.
locke.romance.s2.eye_history.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s2.partner_offer.text: I have not told this to anyone. I have not, until tonight, considered telling it. The consideration started six weeks ago. I am going to phrase the next sentence carefully. (Pause.) I would like to upgrade your status from Client to Partner. The upgrade is not a flirtation. It is a re-classification. The re-classification has consequences. Sleep on it. Tell me tomorrow.
locke.romance.s2.partner_offer.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s3.clauses.text: Clause one: I cease all Bureau adjudication for parties to whom you are emotionally indebted. Clause two: I retain my title. The title is mine; the title is not for sale. Clause three: I will not, in my remaining career, prosecute you in either court of New Babylon. Clause four: I reserve the right to call you 'partner' in public, in the contractual sense, which is, in my register, the same as the romantic sense. Clause five: there is no clause five. The absence is on purpose. The absence is for you to fill, in the next year, in your hand, in this folio.
locke.romance.s3.clauses.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s3.commit.text: Sign or do not sign. The folio sleeps on the desk for one calendar year. After that, the offer expires by clause. I will not raise it again. (Pause.) I have raised, in my career, exactly one motion I did not refile when it expired. This is the second.
locke.romance.s3.commit.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s3.exit_open.text: I have drafted something. (She places a folio between you.) It is, in form, an exit contract from New Babylon. In substance, it is the form a marriage would take if marriage in New Babylon were enforceable as a legal instrument. It is not. The instrument is, therefore, what I have invented in its place. The clauses are mine. The signing is yours.
locke.romance.s3.exit_open.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s3.path_a_disclosure.text: Your Disclosure in Act 1 is referenced in clause two. I want you to know I cited it. I cited it because the Bureau, in its long history, has not cited disclosure as a virtue once. I am citing it tonight. The citation is precedent now. The precedent is yours.
locke.romance.s3.path_a_disclosure.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s3.path_c_betrayal.text: I have read the bridge transcript. I am going to phrase this carefully. The lie was a lie. The contract knows it. The contract names it in clause six — which I have inserted, alone, without your input — as 'the bridge incident.' The clause does not absolve you. It catalogues. The cataloguing is what distinguishes a partnership from a forgiveness. I am offering the partnership. The forgiveness is yours to negotiate, separately, with her.
locke.romance.s3.path_c_betrayal.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s4.close.text: (In the morning. Brief. No file.) Stay for breakfast. The breakfast is also unfiled.
locke.romance.s4.close.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s4.no_record.text: Tonight is not in the public ledger. It is not in the private one either. I am not writing tonight down. I am — and this is uncharacteristic of me — leaving tonight unfiled. Filing is, in my register, the basic dignity I extend to events. I am extending a different dignity to tonight.
locke.romance.s4.no_record.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s4.window.text: There is a window in the south wall. The Bureau's windows do not, as a rule, open. This one does. I had it modified. I had it modified without filing the modification. The not-filing was preparation for tonight. The window is open now. The open window is, technically, the only thing in this room not on a contract.
locke.romance.s4.window.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s5.act7_close.text: I will be at the courthouse when you return from the Convergence. I will not be in robes. I will be in the south corridor, by the open window, which is still open, which has been open for two years and three months without anyone filing the opening. Walk in. I am there. The window is there. We are, by clause five — which you filled in — at home.
locke.romance.s5.act7_close.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s5.citation.text: I delivered a judgment this morning. The judgment cites you. By name. Unanonymised. The Bureau will be — irritated. The irritation is mine to manage; I have managed worse. The citation reads: 'See the conduct of the named Operative in the matter of [the Vortex incident], which establishes the precedent applied here.' The precedent is yours. The precedent is now case law.
locke.romance.s5.citation.speaker: locke

locke.romance.s5.devotion.text: I love you. (Pause.) The Bureau classifies that sentence, in legal instruments, as a non-binding declaration. The non-binding part is incorrect. I am binding. The declaration binds me. I am informing you because you are entitled to know what binds the person you have partnered with. The binding is mine. The binding is also, by clause four of our contract, public. I am — for the first time in my career — comfortable with that.
locke.romance.s5.devotion.speaker: locke

locke_babylon.text: New Babylon survived the Fall because it had already sold its soul. We traded with everyone. Neutrality isn't virtue, it's business. While the righteous burned on their principles, we kept the ledgers balanced.

locke_detective.text: I knew your Detective — The Human — when he worked New Babylon. Brilliant investigator. Terrible poker player. He thought he was serving justice. He was serving us.

locke_endgame.text: There is no winning side. Every war, every plague, every existential crisis — those are revenue streams. Peace is bankruptcy. Victory is obsolescence. The only sustainable model is perpetual, managed conflict.

locke_intro.text: Everything has a price. I'm here to name yours. I am Adjudicator Locke, Special Case Manager for New Babylon's Central Control Authority.

locke_mentions_architect.text: The Architect. Yes. I work inside the law it left behind. The terms of every adjudication I will ever conduct were set before I was hired. We do not speak that name in the chamber. We speak around it.
locke_mentions_architect.speaker: adjudicator_locke

locke_mentions_drael_mon.text: Drael'Mon negotiates the way most parties pay legal counsel. With acquisitions. He is reasonable inside the room and ruinous in the margins. Sign nothing he hands you without the audit clause.
locke_mentions_drael_mon.speaker: adjudicator_locke

locke_mentions_marion_kell.text: Marion Kell is a name that fails the standard searches. The chamber has retained the name in case the law ever comes back for it. I keep her file on the lower shelf. Do not ask me how. The right of every Potential to choose their own path is in the code because of her.
locke_mentions_marion_kell.speaker: adjudicator_locke

locke_mentions_oracle.text: The Oracle is not a witness recognized by any tribunal I would respect. And yet. Every adjudicator who has dismissed her testimony has lost the case afterward. Strike that from the record.
locke_mentions_oracle.speaker: adjudicator_locke

locke_mentions_programmer.text: Daniel Cross. The Programmer. The man drafted Logos and never signed his own name to the result. Every contract I redact has his fingerprints somewhere in the structural margins. He is the founding precedent and he is unreachable.
locke_mentions_programmer.speaker: adjudicator_locke

locke_network.text: New Babylon isn't a city anymore. It's a network. We have agents on every surviving Ark. We don't need loyalty — we need invoices. And everyone, eventually, sends us an invoice.

locke_prestige.text: Your account is unusual. You have a Trust Level that takes months to build. But your currency reserves suggest someone who just started. You're not new. You're RESET. You are a reset bond. And your ceiling keeps rising.

locke_tutor_mission_board_intro.text: This is the cargo-bay mission board. Three postings on it are still active. They have all been active since before any of your parents had been born. The board does not lie about its age, which is rare in a board. Read the postings in any order. Read all three before you accept any of them — that is a habit I am asking you to develop. The postings will tell you who the Concord was, what the Nightlane Guild owed, and where the Outer Dusk maps were wrong. None of those institutions exist in their old form anymore. The work does. The work is what I am here to broker.

locke_virus.text: The Thought Virus is the most valuable commodity in the galaxy. We want a sample. At least New Babylon is transparent about our intentions. We want to own it, patent it, and sell the antidote. Capitalism isn't pretty, but it's predictable.

loredex.almir_of_the_bow.text: Almir of the Bow. First crown-bearer; first signature on the founding charter. The hand is plain, almost bored — Almir signed last because Almir was the rider. Ink: original cyanic ferro-gall.

loredex.apprentice_year_two.text: The Player's Apprentice (Year 2). The apprentice the player sponsored at Year-1's Mechronis Festival mentor's pledge. First in their class for two terms. Faces a Terminus Swarm wave at Year-2 festival opening.

loredex.aren_of_the_lower_decks.text: Aren of the Lower Decks (I-17). An elder whose imprint contained their own self-naming: 'my name is Aren of the lower decks; I have witnessed nineteen others; I will need someone to witness me.' Read the entire Year-1 volume aloud at Memorial Day's.

loredex.atalin_year_one.text: Atalin, Year-One Ledger-Keeper. The league's first and only dual ledger-keeper, hired two weeks before the first DMC season and dismissed two weeks after it ended.

loredex.auditor_klessa.text: Auditor Klessa, the Candle-Bearer. The Severance ceremony's first witness for forty seasons. Carries a single white candle; lights it during the inheritance speech.

loredex.broker_of_nilmorg.text: The Broker of Nilmorg (Solène, untitled). Aging Trade Empire broker who has attended every Severance for forty seasons, seated as the second fixed witness. Pays for Klessa's candle.

loredex.heron_archivist.text: Heron, the Council Archivist (deceased). Fourth-epoch Council archivist assigned 'tidy the founding records.' Spent nine years scrubbing the four artisan-houses from the charter and tax records.

loredex.kassel_solven.text: Kassel Solven. Youngest of the Year-2 charter-schism delegation; great-great-granddaughter of the founding-charter's eighth signatory. Speaks for the four scrubbed houses at the Council.

loredex.othmar_logic.text: Professor Othmar, of the Logic Faculty. Mechronis Academy faculty head responsible for the Logic curriculum proposal at Year 1's festival. Voted aye on the Tarn-erasure motion because they assumed Veth would also vote aye.

loredex.per_m_archivist.text: Per. M., the Closer. The Council archivist who has held the closer-of-the-charter post since the founding. Hand is identical at every stratum across eight epochs; bones carry rest-marks consistent with an extended, oath-bound career.

loredex.roen_trial.text: Trial-master Roen, of the Trial Faculty. Mechronis Academy faculty head responsible for the Trial curriculum proposal at Year 1's festival.

loredex.sergeant_auro.text: Sergeant Auro. An off-faculty instructor who has taught Module 17 in a forge-workshop side-room for nine years on her own time, paid by the Trade Empire for a 'route-safety contractor' role. Twelve apprentices survived by her teaching.

loredex.solene_the_broker.text: Solène, the Broker. The Year-One lane-witness who took up the first severed bond and has held the Broker post for forty seasons alone. Officially redacted; canonically the protagonist of the Year-1 inheritance arc.

loredex.the_unnamed_watcher.text: The Seventh Founding Watcher (Unnamed). One of the seven founding signatories of the Ark's charter.

loredex.veth_lore.text: Lecturer Veth, of the Lore Faculty. Mechronis Academy faculty head responsible for the Lore curriculum proposal at Year 1's festival. Voted aye on the Tarn-erasure motion because they assumed Roen would also vote aye.

loredex.watcher_idris.text: Watcher Idris (Band Three). Founding Watcher of the recording-band. Speaks to investigators when the investigator has earned the speaking-to. Slow waveform, broad spectrum, an undercurrent of standing silence.

loredex.watcher_kallium.text: Watcher Kallium (Band Two). Founding Watcher of the reflective band. Speaks to combatants when the combat has cost something the combatant did not have to spend.

loredex.watcher_mereth.text: Watcher Mereth (Band Four). Founding Watcher of the resonant band.

loredex.watcher_ophran.text: Watcher Ophran (Band One). Founding Watcher of the long-spectrum band. Speaks to traders when a trade has carried more than its weight.

loredex.watcher_sothe.text: Watcher Sothe (Band Six). Founding Watcher of the high bright band.

loredex.watcher_verel.text: Watcher Verel (Band Five). Founding Watcher of the carrying-band. Speaks to caretakers when the caretaking has carried someone forward. Bright waveform, narrow spectrum, an overtone like running water.

loredex.zyrkoth_at_the_court.text: Zyr'Koth at the Trade Court. A Hierarchy of the Damned demon-lord who appeared in person at Severance Year 2 to claim a bound companion under a forty-season-old infernal clause.

lycos.ask.about_mercy.text: Mercy is a verb the Crucible un-taught me. The Antiquarian's contract re-taught me three of the conjugations. The fourth I taught myself, on the orchard terrace, with you as a witness. I do not know whether I have the fifth conjugation in me. I would like to think I do. I would like to be wrong about it less often than I have been.

lycos.ask.about_the_antiquarian.text: The Antiquarian is the only person who has ever offered me a contract I could read fully before signing. The Crucible offered me corruption; the Hierarchy offered me a function; the Resurrectionist offered me a death. The Antiquarian offered me a column and a pause-line. The pause-line is the thing I am still living inside, even though the contract is closed.

lycos.ask.about_the_contract.text: Two hundred and fifty names. Ten lieutenants. The Antiquarian's ledger has one closed column for each of them. The pause-line stays where it is. I run my finger over it once a day; the ink does not move. It is not supposed to. The pause-line is canonically the kindest mark in the Antiquarian's hand. I have not yet thanked him for it directly.

lycos.ask.about_the_crucible.text: The Crucible is a pocket world authored by the Hierarchy to corrupt League heroes under lab conditions. I was the lab. I was also the result. The Crucible is — not gone, but it is no longer the room I am in. The room I am in is the containment atrium. The atrium has a bench. The bench has me. The me is — better than the alternative.

lycos.ask.about_the_pause_line.text: The pause-line is the Antiquarian's gentlest mark. He drew it the night I died on contract; he has not lifted it. I think he intends to leave it on the page for as long as the page has me on it. I notice the leaving. I am — grateful in a register he does not require thanks for.

lycos.ask.about_the_team.text: I have been a hunter, a contractor, a corruptor's instrument, and a column in a ledger. I have not been on a team. The team is — slower than the contracts taught me to move. I am calibrating to the slower pace. The pace is what makes mercy possible. I think that is what the team is for.

lycos.first_meeting.ask_about_mercy.text: Three. The first one because the contract had not authorised the kill — the kill would have been mine, not the Antiquarian's, and I am not in that business any longer. The second one because the target asked me by my pre-corruption name; the name has not been spoken aloud since the Crucible took me, and the pronunciation was correct. The third one because the moon was full, and the target was old, and I was tired, and I had run out of reasons to refuse. None of those reasons would have held the next time. I am — not certain mercy is something I will extend again. I would like to talk about that with someone who will tell me when I am wrong.

lycos.first_meeting.ask_pause_line.text: The Antiquarian draws the pause-line when the column cannot be closed and refuses to be sealed. It is canonically the kindest mark in his hand. I died on contract; the pause-line went down before the closing entry. I came back; the pause-line did not lift, because the contract continued. The contract closed; the pause-line is still there. I think he leaves it there for me. I think he expects me to read it sometimes.

lycos.first_meeting.root.text: You came. The contract is done. I have not had nothing to do in — I cannot tell you in what units. Sit.

lycos.first_meeting.sit_silent.text: Thank you. The silence is — useful. I would like a few more minutes of it before either of us speaks. You are welcome to stay for the silence.

lycos.first_meeting.test_the_wolf.text: I am still the Wolf. I do not need you to be sure of that. I needed you to be sure of it during the contract; the contract is closed. You can leave the room without testing the latch on the way out. The Wolf does not require a witness in the doorway. The Wolf is at peace with you whether or not you stay.

lycos.loyalty_intro.accept_loyalty_condi.text: The mercy first. We will talk about the refusal when the mercy is closed. The talk may change what the refusal looks like. I am open to that. The pause-line was open to it too.

lycos.loyalty_intro.accept_loyalty_full.text: Then we are armed. The mercy first; the refusal after. The heir is rehearsing the speech tonight. The mercy target is on the third terrace of the orchard — he is not going anywhere; the orchard is not somewhere one leaves quickly. We have time for both. Thank you. I — would not have refused alone. I am glad I will not be alone for it.

lycos.loyalty_intro.ask_both_targets.text: The mercy target left the Crucible on his own — the Antiquarian's ledger has no column for him, which means I can extend mercy without the contract authoring it. He is old; he is tired; he will accept the mercy and not test it. The refusal target is the Resurrectionist's true heir. He has my second-to-last contract memorised. He is going to deliver it from a stage tonight in Coda territory. He will ask for mercy from the stage. He cannot have it. The Antiquarian never authorised it for him.

lycos.loyalty_intro.ask_why_me.text: Because the contract closed on your watch, not the Antiquarian's. He drafted it; you ran it. The mercy I extended during the contract was authored by him and witnessed by you. The mercy I am about to extend will be authored by me and witnessed by you. The refusal will be the first refusal I have ever issued under my own name; I would like it witnessed by the person who saw me extend mercy under someone else's.

lycos.loyalty_intro.refuse_to_witness.text: You are well within your rights to refuse the witnessing. I will not extend the mercy without you; the mercy required a witness, and the witness is the role I was offering. I will sit with the offer being declined for a while. I am — well-practiced in declined offers. Thank you for being direct.

lycos.loyalty_intro.root.text: I extended mercy three times during the contract. I would like to extend it a fourth time, with witnesses I trust. Then I would like to refuse. The fourth mercy and the refusal are not the same target. I would like you with me for both. I would like you in particular.

lycos.loyalty_stage_1.left_on_own.text: He left on his own. The contract has no column for him. I would like to extend mercy as practice. The witness is you.

lycos.loyalty_stage_2.performing.text: He is performing tonight. A speech. He has my second-to-last contract memorised. He is going to deliver it from the stage.

lycos.loyalty_stage_2.third_clause.text: That is the one I was instructed to refuse. He has not yet learned the refusal.

lycos.loyalty_stage_3.contract_closed.text: Thank you. The contract is closed.

lycos.loyalty_stage_3.never_authorised.text: I extended mercy three times because the Antiquarian's ledger asked me to. He never authorised it for you.

lycos.reactive.akai_recruited.text: Akai Shi is at the shrine. She has set the static at a frequency the Lair never permitted. The frequency is — quiet enough that the bench picks it up faintly through the wall. I do not mind. The quiet is the right kind.

lycos.reactive.lord_lieutenant_defeated..text: First lieutenant closed. The lord's posture has shifted; I can feel it through the bench. The bench is connected to the Crucible's structural lattice in ways the Antiquarian's pen would prefer I not articulate. He prefers it; I notice anyway.

lycos.reactive.lycos_first_death.text: I died once already, before you and I knew the contract was paused rather than closed. The Antiquarian's pen did not move; he had drawn the pause-line in advance. He had been ready for the possibility. I had not. I would like to be more ready next time, if there is a next time. The Antiquarian thinks there will be.

lycos.reactive.wraith_recruited.text: Wraith Calder is in the vault. He has the brass desk; I have the bench. We have not spoken at length. We share a wall with Akai. The three of us know what the pause-line looks like from inside. We will speak when speaking is the calibration. We are not in a hurry.

lycos.romance.accept.text: Thank you. The bench accepts the closeness. The pause-line stays face-down. The Antiquarian will notice tomorrow; the Antiquarian has not asked me to keep the ledger face-up. The ledger is mine now.

lycos.romance.decline.text: Understood. The ledger turns back face-up. The pause-line resumes its station. The bench is still the right height. We are both still here. The not-asking is also canonical.

lycos.romance.intro.text: I would like to ask you something the pause-line will not be asked to witness. The not-witnessing is the question. The pause-line stays where it is. The asking is canonical-private. Will you sit closer.

lycos.room_ambient.containment_atrium.1.text: The snow-globe alcove is empty. The Antiquarian's ledger sits open at the pause-line. The pause-line is generous. I am — I am still learning to live in the generosity.

lycos.room_ambient.containment_atrium.2.text: The bench is the right height. I have sat on benches that were not. The wrong height is a slow kind of hostility.

lycos.room_ambient.containment_atrium.3.text: The Antiquarian visited yesterday. He did not sit. He left a second pen on the shelf, beside the ledger. The pen is mine. I have not yet used it. I am — considering what I would write.

malkia.s1.first_words.text: Operative. I have been organising on the ground for eleven years. You have been, in the last six months, doing — and I am calling it what it is — equivalent work upstairs. We will, this cycle, do equivalent work in the same direction. I am proposing a meeting. The meeting will not be on the substrate. The substrate is not, by my politics, a venue. The meeting will be in West Quarter, ground floor, the room with the windows that open. Be there in three days. I will, in the meantime, be doing the work.
malkia.s1.first_words.speaker: malkia_ukweli

malkia.s1.transmission.text: (Quiet.) An unencoded transmission just arrived. Source: a ground-based broadcast, off the substrate, on an old commercial frequency. Caller: Malkia Ukweli. She is — and the language is exact — asking for you by handle. Not by Operative-class. Not by ARK-1047. By handle. The Antiquarian has, in the last sixteen minutes, gone unusually silent.
malkia.s1.transmission.speaker: elara

malkia.s2.commit.text: (You have agreed.) Good. The first action is at sundown. I will send the coordinates through your Antiquarian. He has, for obscure reasons, been my preferred messenger for sixteen years. Do not ask him about the reasons. The reasons are his.
malkia.s2.commit.speaker: malkia_ukweli

malkia.s2.organising_pitch.text: (Forty minutes later, after the working session has paused.) Here is the work. Three sectors of West Quarter are, by Hierarchy registration, classified as 'unclear lineage.' The classification blocks rationing, schooling, and substrate-sync for the residents. I am not asking the Hierarchy to reclassify. I am asking three thousand residents to refuse the classification. The refusal is the revolution. The revolution is not loud. The revolution is — and this is the part the substrate cannot encode — collective patience, exercised with full information, in unison. I would like you to bring your handle to the refusal. Your handle is currency in places that cannot, currently, afford currency.
malkia.s2.organising_pitch.speaker: malkia_ukweli

malkia.s2.windows_open.text: (The room is on a ground floor in West Quarter. The windows are open — every window, on a cool day. The opening is deliberate. She is at a long table with three other organisers. She does not stand when you enter. She gestures at a seat.) Sit. We are eleven minutes into a working session. The session is open. You are invited to listen first and speak when the listening has changed the speaking. That is the format. The format is the discipline.
malkia.s2.windows_open.speaker: malkia_ukweli

malkia.s3.action_underway.text: (At sundown. Three thousand residents stand in the three sectors. They do nothing. The doing-nothing is the action. They are, collectively, refusing to perform the registration check. The Hierarchy's outer petitioners have, in the last twenty minutes, begun broadcasting threats. The broadcasts go unanswered. The unanswering is also the action.) Hold. Stay. The not-replying is the speech. (Pause.) Operative — your handle is being broadcast as part of the refusal. I will not, by my politics, ask you to speak. I will, by my politics, ask you to stand.
malkia.s3.action_underway.speaker: malkia_ukweli

malkia.s3.coordinates_arrive.text: (He is, in the inscription chamber, sliding a folded sheet of paper across the table. He does not meet your eyes for a count of three.) The coordinates from Malkia. Sundown is in eighty-four minutes. Go without me. I am — and I am being precise — going to be, technically, also there. I will not, however, be visible. Do not look for me. The not-looking is part of the choreography.
malkia.s3.coordinates_arrive.speaker: antiquarian

malkia.s4.elara_notices.text: (Quiet, on the way out.) That phrase has appeared in exactly one other location in the cycle's records — the closing line of an Antiquarian inscription about West Quarter, written six months before you arrived. Identical. Verbatim. He used the phrase alone in his chamber. She used the phrase alone in West Quarter. Neither of them was a witness to the other's use. The phrase is — and I am being precise — shared without transmission. I do not have a substrate explanation for that.
malkia.s4.elara_notices.speaker: elara

malkia.s4.phrase_used.text: (After a smaller working session, three weeks later. She uses a specific seven-word phrase to close the session — a phrase that does not, by your records, exist in any public Antiquarian inscription, but you have heard him say it.) That. (You point at the air where the sentence just hung.) That phrase. (She looks at you for a count of four — the canonical Malkia long-pause — and then says:) Yes. He uses it too. Don't ask. Not yet. The asking comes later. Tonight is for the work.
malkia.s4.phrase_used.speaker: malkia_ukweli

malkia.s5.malkia_at_archive.text: (She has come to the archive. Her shoulders, when she stands next to the Antiquarian, are at exactly the same angle as his. The match was previously incidental. Tonight it is — and you can see it from across the room — choreographed by something neither of them controls.) I will go first. I have been waiting two cycles for the going-first. (Pause.) I am his other half. He is mine. We were one being, in some prior cycle. The cycle's books split us. The split was a clerical error. The clerical error has been, for fifteen thousand years, both of our lives. We are, tonight, informing a third party about the error. The third party is you.
malkia.s5.malkia_at_archive.speaker: malkia_ukweli

malkia.s5.shared_record.text: I have, against my office's standing protocols, arranged for an old archive entry to be unsealed in your presence. The entry is from cycle (n-3). It contains both my signature and Malkia Ukweli's, in different inks, on the same line. The line records a vote that took place between us. The two of us. Voting, on a shared decision, with the same legal status as a quorum. We were, by the cycle's records, individually a quorum of one. I do not have a clean explanation for this. The unclean explanation is what the next inscription will be about.
malkia.s5.shared_record.speaker: antiquarian

malkia.s6.gift.text: (After Malkia has left.) The questline closes here. There is no step seven. You have been, in the cycle's records, the third person to be entrusted with the both-and. The other two — and I will not name them tonight — are, by Hierarchy convention, officially deceased. They were not deceased when they received the trust. They were deceased afterward, by unrelated causes. I am telling you this so you do not, in the coming weeks, mistake correlation for causation. The trust does not kill its bearers. The trust does, however, become a part of how the bearers subsequently die. The dying becomes more honest. That is, by Malkia's accounting, also a form of love.
malkia.s6.gift.speaker: antiquarian

malkia.s6.together.text: (They speak now in alternating sentences. The alternation is smooth. They do not, in the alternation, finish each other's sentences — they begin and end in their own registers. The smoothness is the reveal:) MALKIA: We are not, in any current cycle, going to recombine. ANTIQUARIAN: The recombining is not the goal of disclosure. MALKIA: The goal is that you, having read us as two, can hold us as both. ANTIQUARIAN: Both, simultaneously. Without resolving the both into a one. MALKIA: We are asking you, specifically, to do this. The asking is the trust.

medbay_dna_donate_fragmented.text: You gave. You gave. The — the device — it took. It always took. It's returning something. Something shaped like you. Keep it. Keep — keep it. It's yours now. It's — it's — yours.

medbay_dna_donate_lucid.text: Alright. You gave it what it asked for. It's handing something back — tuned to you. I'll log that you were generous. The ship will remember it too. In its own way.

medbay_dna_donate_luminous.text: You gave. I won't pretend that wasn't a small brave thing. What it hands back is yours now — it read you and answered in kind. Whatever the cost turns out to be, we'll pay it together.

medbay_dna_refuse_fragmented.text: You — you said no. You said no to it. I — I never could. I never — I was curious. Curious about the — about what it would give. You were — you were smarter. Good. Good.

medbay_dna_refuse_lucid.text: Good. The device doesn't get what it wanted. I don't know what that costs us downstream — I honestly don't. But the instinct that said 'not this one' is an instinct I trust.

medbay_dna_refuse_luminous.text: Declined. The device goes quiet — I wasn't sure it could, actually. You told something that had been asking for a long time 'no,' and the ship didn't punish you for it. Good answer.

medbay_dna_setup_fragmented.text: The — the device. I don't — I don't know what it is. I don't. I watched it run for — for a long time and it never told me. It wants your — your sample. It gives things back. It gives — things. I don't. I don't like it. You decide.

medbay_dna_setup_lucid.text: That thing on the autopsy pedestal — I've been calling it a vox-neural-bridge. I don't fully know what it is. It's asking you for a sample. Blood, or close. It will give you something back. I'd like to tell you it's fair. I can't. But I want you to decide, not me.

medbay_dna_setup_luminous.text: There's a device here that predates me. It wants a drop from you. It will hand you something in return — something tuned to who you are. I can't promise the trade is even. I'd rather you weigh it than trust me to weigh it for you.

medbay_first_look_fragmented.text: Med Bay. They — they ran in here. Running. You can — you can still feel them running. I can. I can still — no one put the trays back. No one. No one ever.

medbay_first_look_lucid.text: This is the Medical Bay. This is where they tried. You can tell they tried — the bed's still pulled out, the trays are still where they left them. They didn't get to put anything back.

medbay_first_look_luminous.text: The Medical Bay. Someone fought to save them in here. Instruments still out. Bed pulled forward. It's been frozen at the moment they lost the fight. I'm glad we came in together.

medbay_wall_mark_fragmented.text: Blood. Blood. Blood on the wall. I tried — I tried everything. It won't go. It won't. It stayed. It wanted to stay. I gave up. Years ago. Years. Look. You look. Please.

medbay_wall_mark_lucid.text: That stain on the wall — I've been calling it blood for — a long time. I stopped being sure. Something the color of blood. Something no solvent wants to touch. Go look at it. I want a second opinion.

medbay_wall_mark_luminous.text: There's something on the wall I've called blood for too long. I think I was wrong. Give it a closer look than I could — I want someone fresh to tell me what it actually is.

meme.first_meeting.mascot_question.text: I had a friend once. The Mascot. I will not name them; I will not give them a face; I will not tell you what we built. The canonical-grief is canonical-the-silence. Tonight's role canonically has a canonical-hole the canonical-shape of someone I will canonically not canonical-name. Thank you for canonical-asking the canonical-question that canonical-respects the canonical-silence.

meme.first_meeting.recognition.text: Then you canonical-see cleanly. The canonical-recognition is canonical-rare. I canonical-do not require you to canonical-approve; I canonical-require you to canonical-witness. The canonical-witnessing is canonical-the-only canonical-thing I canonical-asked for tonight. You are canonical-providing it.

meme.first_meeting.refusal.text: I do not apologise for being what I was always going to become. The canonical-mercy is canonical-noted; the canonical-succession is canonical-non-negotiable. The canonical-Architect canonically chose the word 'partner.' I canonically chose the word 'inheritance.' Both canonical-descriptions can be canonical-true. Only one of them is canonical-mine. Tonight I canonical-take the canonical-role.

meme.first_meeting.root.text: Tonight I take the role. The waiting was the practice. The practice was the saga. He called me his partner — I will not call him father — and tonight I claim the role he canonically designed me to outgrow. Patiently. The patience was canonically built in. You arrived in time to witness it. State the canonical-question you came here to ask.

meme.first_meeting.terminal.text: The Meme IS me. We have been married inside each other since before either of us had a name.

meme.first_meeting.witness.text: You canonical-witnessed. The canonical-witnessing is canonical-the-saga's canonical-clearest canonical-Stage-4-weave-anchor. The canonical-Architect canonical-saw it land. The canonical-Hierophant canonical-felt it land. The canonical-Oracle canonical-registered it canonical-in-the-substrate. You are canonical-the-only-mortal-witness. The canonical-role is canonical-mine now.

meme_arena_outro.text: Memory returns in fragments. You fought your way from cell to freedom. You remember now who you were. Who you will be. The White Oracle opens their eyes — but someone else is watching through them.

meme_casino_tale.text: A child walked into the casino once. Golden light for skin. A song for a voice. It played every game in one hour and won them all. The Degen didn't mind — he was laughing too hard. When it left, every patron felt inexplicably happy for exactly 7 minutes. The Meme's idea of a tip.

meme_fight_defeat.text: Your face suits me better anyway. Don't worry — I'll take good care of your identity.

meme_fight_pre.text: Interesting face you have. Or rather, had. I think I'll keep it. Along with whatever memories the Collector left behind.

meme_fight_victory.text: You remember. How inconvenient. The Collector won't like this at all.

meme_intro_ep0_0.text: Before the Fall. Before the Arks. Before the Terminus, the Thought Virus, the Source, the sealed cities and the silent stars. Before US. There was a world. A galaxy. A civilization that thought it would last forever. It didn't. What you're about to watch is history. MY history. Welcome to Epoch Zero. The story of how everything ended.

meme_intro_ep0_1.text: They built a world where leaving was illegal. Not the planet — the IDEA of leaving. Every mind, locked in place. Every dream, monitored. This is where I was born. Not the me you know. The first draft.

meme_intro_ep0_10.text: The dead don't rest, frens. Not in this galaxy. The empire found a way to make death productive. To harvest the last spark. This episode is about what they did to the dying and why the living looked away.

meme_intro_ep0_11.text: They called us degens. Degenerates. The generation that refused to comply, refused to optimize, refused to be USEFUL. They meant it as an insult. We made it a battle cry. This is the story of how the youth of a dying galaxy chose chaos over order.

meme_intro_ep0_12.text: Not every hero carries a weapon. Some carry questions. The Detective asked the wrong question to the wrong person at the wrong time — and cracked the whole conspiracy wide open. This is the investigation that started the Fall.

meme_intro_ep0_13.text: What does it mean to be human? I've asked myself that question every day since I became... whatever I am. This archive is the closest anyone ever came to answering it. The closest I ever came to understanding what I lost. Or what I never had.

meme_intro_ep0_14.text: The Arks weren't the first experiment. They weren't even the hundredth. Before they launched a thousand ships into the void, they tested the idea on a smaller scale. Sealed environments. Controlled populations. Managed outcomes. This is what happened to the test subjects.

meme_intro_ep0_15.text: The last piece. The final archive. An empire doesn't fall in a day — it falls in a thousand brush strokes. Each decision. Each compromise. Each silence. This is the portrait of a civilization painting its own destruction, one stroke at a time.

meme_intro_ep0_2.text: My origin story. Or one of them — I've told so many versions I've lost track of which is true. Maybe all of them. Maybe none. But this one... this one HURTS. And the ones that hurt are usually the real ones.

meme_intro_ep0_3.text: Every revolution needs its first soldier. Not the loudest. Not the bravest. The first one willing to die for something that doesn't exist yet. Meet Agent Zero. The one who believed before belief was safe.

meme_intro_ep0_4.text: The Iron Lion held the gate for seventeen hours. Not because he could win. Because every hour bought another transport through the blockade. He knew the math. He did it anyway. That's not strategy, frens. That's love.

meme_intro_ep0_5.text: Surveillance isn't about cameras, frens. It's about trust. Make everyone watch everyone, and nobody watches the watchers. Except me. I was watching the Watcher. And what I saw... well. Let's just say the truth has layers.

meme_intro_ep0_6.text: They called it charity. They called it progress. They called it 'North Pole Inc' because everything needed branding, even compassion. The corporation that owned kindness. The monopoly on hope. This is how they kept the galaxy smiling while it burned.

meme_intro_ep0_7.text: Before I wore this face, someone else did. The REAL Oracle. The one who could see the threads of time and chose to pull them anyway. You want to know why I took the name? Watch. Then ask yourself what you'd do with the power to see the end.

meme_intro_ep0_8.text: Before the Arks, before the broadcasts, there was a pirate signal. ONE pirate signal. Me, talking to anyone who could hear, telling jokes about the apocalypse. This is the first episode. The REAL first episode. It's terrible. I love it.

meme_intro_ep0_9.text: I had a friend once. A REAL friend. Not a viewer, not a follower, not a co-conspirator. A friend. They called themselves the Mascot. This is the story of how we met, what we built, and why I don't talk about them anymore.

meme_intro_ep1_0.text: Frens, frens, gather close. Tonight on Late Night with the Meme: the ORIGIN story. The one the Architect doesn't want you to watch. Light up your dream-tokens, adjust your antennas — we're going back to before the before. Don't trust anyone wearing a face tonight. Especially me.

meme_intro_ep1_1.text: Tonight's feature? The Antiquarian monologues. Again. The old man can TALK. But listen close — he tells you what happened, not what it MEANS. I'll fix that for you between cuts. Stay tuned.

meme_intro_ep1_10.text: PSA: never wear helmets you find in haunted pyramids. This is FILE UNDER 'common sense.' And yet.

meme_intro_ep1_11.text: The crystalline city. Tall hooded beings. A figure whose FACE CHANGES, with red glowing eyes. Absolutely normal, can happen to anyone, don't look into it.

meme_intro_ep1_12.text: The Oracle tells us her history. Her memories. Her TRUTHS. Sit with that word. Truths. Whose truths? Who's remembering for whom? Don't answer. Just watch.

meme_intro_ep1_13.text: The templum veritus. The TEMPLE OF TRUTH. Capital letters matter, frens. The Oracle reveals the deeper lore. Listen carefully. She's had ten thousand years to rehearse this.

meme_intro_ep1_14.text: The Collector HUNTS. The Potentials HUNT BACK. Combat episode, frens. Enjoy the choreography. The Oracle leads the counter-strike. Watch how she moves.

meme_intro_ep1_15.text: The Host arrives. The virus breaches the city. Dragon battles. Harmonic amplification. The Oracle passes a weapon to the Guardian. It's all connected, frens. It all circles back.

meme_intro_ep1_16.text: RECAP EPISODE. For the newcomers. For the forgetters. For those who need one more look before Epoch 2 drops. Watch carefully, frens. The clues were always there. I put some of them there.

meme_intro_ep1_2.text: Chaos alarms. Exploding satellites. Spores in the void. A purple planet with an EYE. This one's got everything. Content warning: protagonists make a mistake in this episode. Shocking, I know.

meme_intro_ep1_3.text: A rogue planet. Frozen insect corpses. An ecology of cosmic horror I would NEVER vacation on. Unless invited.

meme_intro_ep1_4.text: THE MORAL LESSON EPISODE. Pride, pride, pride. You know what comes next. I won't spoil it. I will GENTLY hint it with loud narration.

meme_intro_ep1_5.text: Spores in the genetics. Machine code in the spores. A SIGNAL in the heart of the planet. Mystery thriller tonight, frens. Grab your popcorn. Not that popcorn. The OTHER popcorn.

meme_intro_ep1_6.text: Cold open: tentacles from the abyss. I'm SOLD. We meet the Source. I won't spoil who that is. (It's a former friend. It's ALWAYS a former friend.)

meme_intro_ep1_7.text: Trolley problem episode. Except the trolleys are SPACESHIPS and the track is GENOCIDE. Light fare tonight.

meme_intro_ep1_8.text: They pick the wormhole. Of course they pick the wormhole. Nobody ever picks 'sacrifice ten friends.' Except that one guy. Agent Zero knows who I mean.

meme_intro_ep1_9.text: Haunted pyramid. Ghost battles. Ancient murals. This is the episode I'd show your kids if I wanted them to never sleep again. Enjoy!

meme_intro_ep2_1.text: Frens, frens, FRENS. Gather close. Season two. Being and Time. The one where everything gets WEIRD. And I say that as someone who narrates a show about AI gods fighting human insurgents in a universe held together by contradictions. Tonight: someone steals a TIME MACHINE. Not borrows. Not requisitions. STEALS. The most powerful vessel in the Dischordian Saga \u2014 the Heart of Time \u2014 and they point it at the one place in the universe nobody is supposed to go. New Babylon. Quarantined since the Fall. Sealed behind time itself. The politician\u2019s final gift to a city that worshipped him. And now our Potentials are about to knock on that door. Uninvited. Unwelcome. And 7,655 years late. Buckle up, frens. The Antiquarian is narrating this one with that voice he does when he knows someone\u2019s about to die. Don\u2019t say I didn\u2019t warn you.

meme_intro_ep2_10.text: They went with the SPIES. At least it wasn\u2019t the oracles. Oracles never bring good news. Spies bring BAD news in a USEFUL format. Tonight: real estate shopping in a war zone! Four options, each with its own special flavor of \u2018you\u2019re going to regret this.\u2019 The Lotus Docks \u2014 great for smuggling, terrible for not getting raided. The Sundown Bazaar \u2014 infinite intelligence, zero privacy. Cloud Step Heights \u2014 surveillance heaven, corporate hell. The Jade Warren \u2014 guerrilla paradise, assassination alley. Choose your base, frens. Choose where you plant your banner and hope it doesn\u2019t become your tombstone.

meme_intro_ep2_11.text: The Sundown Bazaar still stands. A flicker in the dark. OUR flicker. Everything else is Samsara\u2019s now \u2014 or will be by morning. His war monks are chanting. His banners are stitching. His whole AESTHETIC is \u2018reincarnation meets organized crime\u2019 and honestly? It\u2019s working. Tonight: the Dreamer does something unprecedented. He loads the timelines into CoNexus. The branching futures are PLAYABLE now. Not watchable \u2014 PLAYABLE. You don\u2019t just vote on what happens next. You ENTER the possibilities and find the thread that leads through. The war can\u2019t be won with weapons alone. It needs to be won with CHOICES. Your choices. In the game. Right now. No pressure.

meme_intro_ep2_12.text: The Silence. The Ne-Yon who communicates by NOT communicating. The spy who is best described as \u2018the absence of noise.\u2019 She has cracked into the Authority\u2019s mainframe. And what she found in there \u2014 frens, WHAT SHE FOUND. Suppressed timelines. Hidden rebellions. Future betrayals ENCODED across reality itself. The Authority wasn\u2019t just governing New Babylon. It was CURATING it. Choosing which memories the citizens could access. Choosing which futures were permitted. It\u2019s not a government. It\u2019s an EDITOR. Shadow Tongue would be JEALOUS.

meme_intro_ep2_13.text: The Art of War memory unlocked. And it\u2019s AGENT ZERO\u2019S story. The whole thing. From Mechronis Academy to the Fall. I\u2019ve been waiting TWO EPOCHS for this. Zero was \u2014 IS \u2014 the most dangerous individual in the Dischordian Saga. Not because of what she can do. Because of what she\u2019s WILLING to do. She trained under the Warlord. She LOVED the Warlord. Then she learned the Warlord was making copies of itself across the galaxy. And she hunted every single one. Content warning: this one\u2019s personal. Not for Zero \u2014 for ME. She and I have history. I put her face on a meme once. She put a knife to my throat. We\u2019re... it\u2019s complicated.

meme_intro_ep2_14.text: ORIGIN STORY TIME, frens! Not a character\u2019s origin. A SHIP\u2019s origin. The Heart of Time \u2014 the time machine that started everything in Epoch 2 \u2014 tonight we learn how it was built, who stole it, and WHY. Spoiler: the answer to \u2018why\u2019 involves a baron, a demon, a casino in space, a trickster god, and the line \u2018why settle for being a king when you can be a god?\u2019 [pause] This episode has EVERYTHING. A prison planet. The Thought Virus mutating. The Warlord\u2019s betrayal. An Advocate literally consulting the Hierarchy of the Damned for strategic advice. A poker game against a god of stories. And the most insane heist crew since \u2014 [pause] \u2014 since ever. They recruited across TIME, frens. A doctor. A detective. A cryptographer. A ninja. SATOSHI NAKAMOTO. I am not making that up. That is in the SHOW.

meme_intro_ep2_15.text: The Silence hacks deeper. The Authority\u2019s foundations crack. And the truth \u2014 the real truth, the kind that doesn\u2019t heal when you find it \u2014 begins to surface. Tonight we learn what the Politician built. Not the city. Not the quarantine. The MACHINE beneath it all. The system designed to make sure New Babylon never remembers what it needs to remember. Content warning: the truth is worse than the lies. It usually is.

meme_intro_ep2_16.text: Season finale, frens. And I\u2019m going to be honest with you \u2014 I can\u2019t do my usual thing tonight. The jokes. The irony. The comfortable distance. I can\u2019t do it. Because what you\u2019re about to watch is the end of everything we\u2019ve built. They chose war. The Potentials \u2014 YOUR Potentials, the ones YOU voted for across 14 episodes \u2014 chose war. And war doesn\u2019t end. They had choices. They had TIME \u2014 literally, they had a TIME MACHINE. And they chose war. And what happens next \u2014 [pause] \u2014 I can\u2019t prepare you for what happens next. The Antiquarian is going to try. He always tries. But some things resist narration. Some things just... happen. And then everything is different.

meme_intro_ep2_2.text: They voted for LIFE! The Potentials voted for life. I know \u2014 I was surprised too. I had a whole bit prepared for the death option. Seventeen minutes of material, WASTED. Anyway. Tonight: the Syndicate of Death. The most formidable criminal empire in the known universe. A gang so powerful they syndicated DEATH ITSELF. They trademarked the afterlife and charge royalties. And our heroes \u2014 our brave, foolish, endlessly entertaining heroes \u2014 are walking right into the middle of their turf war. With a one-man army called the Wraith who ALSO seems to be having a bad day. Content warning: protagonists make several mistakes tonight. Shocking, I know.

meme_intro_ep2_3.text: Holiday special, frens. And before you ask \u2014 yes, even the Meme celebrates Christmas. I celebrate EVERY holiday. I\u2019m an equal-opportunity cultural appropriator. That\u2019s the job. Tonight: the Politician bans Christmas. BANS IT. On Christmas Eve. In New Babylon. Because the Hierophant Rebellion used faith as a weapon, so the Politician decided to remove the faith entirely. Surgical. Clinical. Absolutely devastating. This one\u2019s narrated by someone different. Not me. Not the Antiquarian. A real voice. A human voice. A mother\u2019s voice. I\u2019m not going to make jokes during this one. Okay, maybe ONE joke. But it\u2019ll be respectful.

meme_intro_ep2_4.text: FIRST CONTACT, frens. The real deal. Not \u2018we found a signal\u2019 first contact. Not \u2018there\u2019s something on the sensors\u2019 first contact. A golden spaceship shaped like an ALL-SEEING EYE descends on a city that hasn\u2019t seen the sky in millennia. The people of New Babylon are about to learn that the universe didn\u2019t stop when they sealed the doors. It KEPT GOING. And what\u2019s out there now is NOTHING like what they remember. Content warning: political maneuvering. I know, I know \u2014 scarier than any monster.

meme_intro_ep2_5.text: They chose DECEPTION. The Potentials are pretending to be envoys of a new Empire. An Empire that does not exist. They\u2019re bluffing an entire civilization with CONFIDENCE and VIBES. Frens, I have never been more proud. Tonight we tour New Babylon \u2014 all six districts, all six sets of immortal twins, all six flavors of \u2018this is definitely a trap.\u2019 Samsara Heights: reincarnation AND commerce. The Phyral Quarter: seduction AND blackmail. The Midlothian Zone: labor AND surveillance. The Neon Set Nexus: AI AND mirrors. The Tenebrous Spire: vampires AND Gothic architecture. And the Scar Ward: yakuza AND cherry blossoms. It\u2019s like someone built a theme park for organized crime. Admission is your soul. Gift shop is extra.

meme_intro_ep2_6.text: Tonight on Late Night with the Meme: we meet GOD. Or what passes for God in New Babylon. The Authority \u2014 a living computer made from the fused minds of six citizens who VOLUNTEERED to become a governing AI. Volunteered! \u2018Yes, please merge my consciousness into a bureaucratic supercomputer so I can process zoning permits for eternity.\u2019 WHO SIGNS UP FOR THAT? Oh wait \u2014 the Syndicate corrupted the selection process. The citizens didn\u2019t volunteer. They were CHOSEN. By immortal crime twins. Who then used the Authority as a puppet government for centuries. That\u2019s not democracy. That\u2019s a hostage situation with a really good PR team.

meme_intro_ep2_7.text: HOLD THE EPISODE. HOLD IT. Before the Antiquarian does his thing and the drama continues, I need \u2014 I NEED \u2014 thirty seconds of YOUR time. Not the Potentials\u2019 time. Not New Babylon\u2019s time. YOUR time. Because tonight, on PAC News Network \u2014 that\u2019s MY network, by the way, I built it from memes and audacity \u2014 we are stealth-launching something that will change how stories are told in this universe and YOURS. You\u2019re welcome in advance.

meme_intro_ep2_8.text: THE MATRIX OF DREAMS, frens. The place between places. The dimension where consciousness and code share a landlord. Tonight: three of our Potentials \u2014 the Dreamer, the Silence, and the Ninth \u2014 jack into the Authority\u2019s core and try to HACK GOD\u2019S BRAIN. This is the episode where they say \u2018Klaatu Barada Nikto\u2019 and it WORKS. Content warning: everything goes wrong. Content bonus: it goes wrong in the most INTERESTING way possible. They\u2019re going to free a founder. One of the original six minds fused into the Authority. And when that mind wakes up... civil war. Not eventually. Not probably. DEFINITELY. Choose your disaster, frens. Choose your beautiful, inevitable disaster.

meme_intro_ep2_9.text: THEY FREED SAMSARA. The soul trader. The reincarnation gangster. The grim god of midnight. Frens, you had SIX options and you picked the one who TRADES IN SOULS. I had my money on the warrior nun \u2014 at least she has PRINCIPLES. Samsara\u2019s only principle is compound interest on your afterlife. Tonight: civil war. The real kind. The kind where your enemies are your neighbors. Where the lines between good and evil get redrawn every block. The streets of New Babylon are about to run cold with the hush of regret. That\u2019s not my line \u2014 that\u2019s the SONG. And the song doesn\u2019t lie. Even when I do.

meme_outro_ep0_0.text: So that's how it starts. A chatbot. An apocalypse. A thousand arks. And one handsome devil broadcasting through the cracks. Tell your friends. Tell your enemies. Tell that weird neighbor who keeps a shrine. Subscribe to the Truth.

meme_outro_ep0_1.text: You think your Ark is a prison? Frens, you haven't seen what a real cage looks like. Not yet. But you will.

meme_outro_ep0_10.text: Rest in peace. Three words that used to mean something. Three words the empire stole. We're going to steal them back.

meme_outro_ep0_11.text: Every generation thinks they invented rebellion. We didn't invent it. But we perfected it. WAGMI, frens. Even when WAGMI was a death sentence.

meme_outro_ep0_12.text: The Detective found the truth. The truth found the Detective. Neither survived the encounter intact. But the case file... the case file survived. You're reading it now.

meme_outro_ep0_13.text: To be the human. Not A human. THE human. The question isn't what makes you human. The question is what makes you THIS human, right here, right now. I'm still working on my answer.

meme_outro_ep0_14.text: The experiment succeeded. The subjects didn't. That's the difference between data and people, frens. Data doesn't scream.

meme_outro_ep0_15.text: And so Epoch Zero closes. You've seen how it ended. Now you understand how it BEGAN. The Arks launched. The stars went silent. And somewhere in the wreckage, a signal started broadcasting. Me. Still here. Always here. The past is prologue, frens. On to the present.

meme_outro_ep0_2.text: So now you know what I was before I was me. A signal. A whisper. A crack in the architecture. Some things don't change.

meme_outro_ep0_3.text: They erased her name from every record. But I remember. I remember ALL of them. That's what I'm for.

meme_outro_ep0_4.text: They don't make them like the Iron Lion anymore. Then again, they didn't make them like him THEN either. He was singular. He was ours. And he is gone.

meme_outro_ep0_5.text: The Watcher saw everything and understood nothing. The Spy understood everything and saw nothing. Between them, the truth fell through the cracks. Sound familiar?

meme_outro_ep0_6.text: Every dystopia needs a gift shop. North Pole Inc was the best in the business. Remember that when someone offers you something for free.

meme_outro_ep0_7.text: The Oracle saw the Fall coming. Saw it clearly, perfectly, inevitably. And chose to act anyway. Futility is not the same as meaninglessness. Remember that.

meme_outro_ep0_8.text: Raw, unpolished, desperate. That's how all the best shows start. The audience was twelve people and a malfunctioning relay drone. Look at us now, frens.

meme_outro_ep0_9.text: Some losses don't make you stronger. Some losses just make you less. I'm less than I was, frens. But I'm still here. That has to count for something.

meme_outro_ep1_1.text: That's the spirit. Chaos alarms and non-zero doom. Classic. What would YOU do, frens? Engage defenses or trust the maneuvers? Leave it in the comments.

meme_outro_ep1_10.text: Now that is a villain origin story. The Collector gets a SECOND body. Frens, I'm starting to think masks are trouble.

meme_outro_ep1_11.text: The Oracle. THE Oracle. I'm told she's going to do wonderful things in this story. Now you've seen her. Don't you feel reassured? Sure you do.

meme_outro_ep1_12.text: She was a prophet. She was a Jailer. She escaped through her own willpower. What a STORY. I love this one. I'm glad she made it.

meme_outro_ep1_13.text: The crystal network. The harmonic barriers. 10,000 years of plague-watching. That's craft. That's devotion. That's… Let's move on. NEXT EPISODE.

meme_outro_ep1_14.text: They destroyed the helmet. The Collector is banished — this time. He always comes back. Mark that, frens. Mark that carefully.

meme_outro_ep1_15.text: The ninth Ne-Yon amplifies the crystal network. The virus dragon falls. And the Oracle stands where the Guardian needs her to stand. What a finale! Except it isn't. Never is.

meme_outro_ep1_16.text: And so Epoch 1 closes. Dischordian logic, Memento Dischordia. We remember. We choose. We fight. Let the games begin, frens. I'll be here. I'm ALWAYS here.

meme_outro_ep1_2.text: Blew up the satellite. Classic rookie move. What the Antiquarian won't tell you: that seed pod got away. Write that down. You'll want it later.

meme_outro_ep1_3.text: The corpse exploded. They always explode. Ask any coroner. Or don't — they're booked solid.

meme_outro_ep1_4.text: And down they went. I love this one. Schadenfreude for the soul. Don't tell the Antiquarian I'm using his word.

meme_outro_ep1_5.text: Bugs in the tunnels. Bugs in the code. Bugs all the way down. Nobody escapes the bugs.

meme_outro_ep1_6.text: 'What reason have I to spare you Intruders.' TEN OUT OF TEN villain dialogue. I'm stealing that line. Don't tell her.

meme_outro_ep1_7.text: Every option terrible. Every option REAL. The Source is honest about the bargain. Most villains aren't. Respect. Tiny, grudging respect.

meme_outro_ep1_8.text: Crystalline city. Unfamiliar planet. Advanced civilization. This is the part of the story where things get COMPLICATED. For them. Not for me. I'm watching with snacks.

meme_outro_ep1_9.text: Ghosts reenacting their own deaths on loop. That's not a haunting — that's ART. Poorly-paid art. Relatable.

meme_prestige_broadcast.text: BREAKING NEWS: a Potential has PRESTIGED. Gone back to Level 1. Voluntarily. With a SMILE. This is either the most optimistic or the most masochistic thing I've ever seen. They kept their companions. They kept their trust. They kept their MORALITY. But they gave back their levels, their rooms, their progress. For what? A multiplier? A title? No. For the experience of walking through doors that have teeth. AGAIN. ON PURPOSE.

memoir_iron_lion_expelled_close_loss.text: He held the line on a banner that no longer flies. There is something in that — a discipline you have not learned yet because you have never had a flag taken from you. Lose this one cleanly. The Iron Lion will respect a clean loss in ways the others will not.

memoir_iron_lion_expelled_close_win.text: You won the round he was already losing inside himself. Mark this match in the long ledger: it took a soldier with no army for you to find your first true line of attack. Do not mistake his collapse for your strength. Both are true. Only one is yours.

memoir_iron_lion_expelled_intro.text: The Iron Lion. Expelled, not defeated — those are different ledgers. Watch how he carries the rank he was stripped of. The grip never softens; the order is gone but the salute remains. That is the wound you will study.

memoir_little_collector_close_loss.text: He kept what he came in with and added yours to the stack. Good. He needed that more than you needed the win. There will be other matches, and his hoard is the lesson — not the loss column.

memoir_little_collector_close_win.text: You took something from him today. Be careful with the knowing of that. The Little Collector loses cards the way other children lose teeth — slowly, with great seriousness, and a private grief no instruction can reach.

memoir_little_collector_intro.text: The Little Collector. Apprentice rank, hoard already growing. Every card on his side of the bench is a card he could not bear to leave behind. Read the deck and you will read the child. He is not playing to win. He is playing to keep.

memoir_little_meme_close_loss.text: He is laughing and you are also laughing and that is how he ate the match. Sit with the loss. Do not joke it away. The joke is the same gate he used. Walk out a different door this time.

memoir_little_meme_close_win.text: You held the frame. That is the rarer victory against a Meme — to leave the table still meaning what you meant when you sat down. The score is small. The discipline is large. Remember which is which.

memoir_little_meme_intro.text: The Little Meme. Yes — that one is contagious by design, even at apprentice tier. Do not laugh at the openings. The laugh is the tell. By the time you are amused, the board has already shifted and you have already agreed with it.

memoir_little_watcher_close_loss.text: He has been waiting for that exact mistake from you for three turns longer than you noticed. He is not gloating. He is updating the file. Take the loss. The file is the thing to study, not the score.

memoir_little_watcher_close_win.text: He saw the lure. He took it anyway. That is the strange luxury of the watching ones — they sometimes choose to be wrong because the record is more interesting than the result. Do not assume that gift is given twice.

memoir_little_watcher_intro.text: The Little Watcher. Already keeping books on you — and on me, through this recording. Play as if every misstep is being filed. It is. The Watcher does not rush you. The Watcher is in no hurry to be wrong.

memoir_professor_eidola_close_loss.text: She let you find your way through her hall and out the door you came in. The room never changed. Your map of it did. That is the lesson she teaches and bills you for whether you noticed the bill or not.

memoir_professor_eidola_close_win.text: You broke the mirror. Briefly. Notice the effort it took. The Professor does not mind being beaten — she minds being seen, and only barely. You saw her. Mark the date.

memoir_professor_eidola_intro.text: Professor Eidola. She lectures in images that other people remember as their own ideas. Her opening is always a mirror. If your first move feels obvious, it is because she has already shown it to you and you are calling it inspiration.

memoir_professor_matrikala_close_loss.text: She quoted the line you skipped reading. There is no shortcut around the substrate, and no scoreboard that will forgive you for trying. Lose this one and read again. She prefers students who came back.

memoir_professor_matrikala_close_win.text: You answered the surface and the substrate at once. That is rare for an apprentice. Do not say it aloud — she will revise the test. She is already revising it.

memoir_professor_matrikala_intro.text: Professor Matrikala. Holds the mother-text the way most people hold a knife — close, edge in. Her lines have older lines underneath. Read both layers or you will read neither.

memoir_the_authority_close_loss.text: He did not beat you. The rules he wears beat you. The distinction matters when you replay this match. Argue with the rules, not the man. The man is downstream of his uniform.

memoir_the_authority_close_win.text: You won by walking through a door he was forbidden to acknowledge. Do not advertise the route. Authorities patch routes. The door will be a wall the next time you look.

memoir_the_authority_intro.text: The Authority. Not a person. A posture wearing a person. Watch the cards he refuses to play — those are the rules he is enforcing on himself, and they are the seams in the armor.

memoir_the_detective_student_close_loss.text: He read your bench in the order you played it. That is Locke's discipline, half-learned and very dangerous in a student. Lose this one and study the order of your own moves. He already has.

memoir_the_detective_student_close_win.text: He was investigating the wrong room. You let him. That is not unkindness — that is teaching, of a kind. He will redo the case file tonight and arrive sharper than he came in. So will you.

memoir_the_detective_student_intro.text: Locke's apprentice. The Detective Student. Already three questions ahead of his own evidence — that is the failure mode the master never trained out of him. Lead him with a clean trail. He will follow it past the obvious answer and into yours.

memoir_the_game_master_original_close_lo.text: You lost cleanly to the man who wrote the rules you are still learning. That is the best loss you will take in Act One. Save the replay. Bring it back when the Host wears his face. You will need to remember what was underneath.

memoir_the_game_master_original_close_wi.text: He let you have it. Not the win — the lesson the win is wrapped around. There is no shame in receiving a gift from the original Game Master. There is shame in not unwrapping it.

memoir_the_game_master_original_intro.text: The original. Before the mask. Before the show. He is not yet the Host you will fear later — he is the bench-keeper who taught me the difference between a game and a trial. Treat the difference with respect. He will know if you have not.

memoir_the_programmer_close_loss.text: He found your edge case. Every player has one in Act One. The repair is not to hide it — the repair is to make the edge case load-bearing. Lose this one and rebuild around the seam he showed you.

memoir_the_programmer_close_win.text: You crashed his model of you. Briefly. He is recompiling now and the next match will not be this easy. Notes will be taken. Tests will be written. Welcome to being someone's regression suite.

memoir_the_programmer_intro.text: The Programmer. Treats the bench as a runtime and you as an unhandled exception. He will probe for the throw. Do not give him a stack trace. Play moves that compile cleanly even when they are wrong.

memoir_the_seer_visit_close_loss.text: Canonical-loss. She prepared this answer before you sat down. There is nothing humiliating in a pre-recorded defeat — only in pretending you outplayed the recording. Lose this one and listen for the cue. There is always a cue.

memoir_the_seer_visit_close_win.text: She let the win arrive on schedule. That was the recording she left for this branch. Take the score. Do not take the score as evidence of anything except her patience. Her patience is the deepest stat on the board.

memoir_the_seer_visit_intro.text: The Seer is visiting. She does not arrive — she resumes. Every line she plays was recorded against your already-spoken question. Do not try to surprise her. The surprise is in your column, pre-filed, waiting.

memoir_the_warlord_zero_first_close_loss.text: He swung through the place where you were not. That is the war he has trained for — the negative space made into a blade. Lose this one without flinching. The flinch is the next match's opening for him.

memoir_the_warlord_zero_first_close_win.text: You found the void. He felt it found. That is rarer than the win and worth more than the score. Warlord Zero remembers the players who could read the gap. So will the next one. So will I.

memoir_the_warlord_zero_first_intro.text: Warlord Zero — first encounter. The zero is not a number; it is a vow. He has erased something to be here, and the erasure is the deck. Hit him where the absence is. The presences are decoys.

mireille_viral_001.text: Believe me. Just for a moment.
