vo_elara_tut_g3_win_01.text: You cast your first spell and your first Bloodborn in the same match. The Oracle used to say a commander's second memory of any battle was always the thing they were willing to bleed for. I think she'd approve of yours.
vo_elara_tut_g3_win_01.speaker: elara

vo_elara_tut_g3_win_02.text: Your General's at a little less than full. That's correct. Healing crystals don't exist yet in this chamber, and I wanted you to feel the cost before you saw the cure.
vo_elara_tut_g3_win_02.speaker: elara

vo_elara_tut_g4_pre_01.text: Last gate. There's no match here — just a table, a pile of cards, and you. The Engineer called this chamber 'the quiet one.' He said most fights were lost before anyone even stepped into the arena, and this was where the losing happened.
vo_elara_tut_g4_pre_01.speaker: elara

vo_elara_tut_g4_pre_02.text: Take your time. You're not building a deck. You're drawing a self-portrait in forty strokes. I'll be here when you're ready.
vo_elara_tut_g4_pre_02.speaker: elara

vo_elara_tut_g4_win_01.text: Forty cards. One General. A self-portrait in your own hand. I'll remember this deck — the good moves you make with it, the bad ones, the nights you swap a card out and put it back again. Every version of it.
vo_elara_tut_g4_win_01.speaker: elara

vo_elara_tut_g4_win_02.text: When you're ready, the campaign door opens. Chapter One. Agent Zero's waiting for you — and she's been waiting a while. Take a breath. Then step through.
vo_elara_tut_g4_win_02.speaker: elara

vo_elara_tut_g5_loss_01.text: Losing here is fine. The deck answered honestly and the answer wasn't the one you needed. That happens. Mulligan harder next time. The Engineer used to mulligan two cards every game on principle. We'll talk about why.
vo_elara_tut_g5_loss_01.speaker: elara

vo_elara_tut_g5_pre_01.text: Two more habits to teach you before I let you out into the world. Drawing, and changing your mind about your draw. The first is automatic. The second is the one almost nobody uses on purpose.
vo_elara_tut_g5_pre_01.speaker: elara

vo_elara_tut_g5_pre_02.text: I've set up a sparring partner who will not pressure you. Take the time. Watch the deck answer. The Engineer used to say the deck doesn't lie — it just doesn't always tell you the truth in order.
vo_elara_tut_g5_pre_02.speaker: elara

vo_elara_tut_g5_win_01.text: Good. You felt the draw step. You felt the mulligan. Both will become invisible to you within a week. The point of teaching them now is so you remember they were never invisible to begin with.
vo_elara_tut_g5_win_01.speaker: elara

vo_elara_tut_g6_loss_01.text: Deck-out got you. Or burn did. Either way — you now know what those two losses feel like, which means you'll see them coming next time. That's the whole point of losing on purpose. We'll move on.
vo_elara_tut_g6_loss_01.speaker: elara

vo_elara_tut_g6_pre_01.text: Last lesson before I let go of your shoulder. Two clocks live inside every match — your hand can fill, and your deck can empty. Both are losses you would rather lose to anything else. We're going to feel them once, on purpose, in safety.
vo_elara_tut_g6_pre_01.speaker: elara

vo_elara_tut_g6_pre_02.text: I will not pretend this match is comfortable. It isn't supposed to be. The discomfort is the lesson. Lean into it.
vo_elara_tut_g6_pre_02.speaker: elara

vo_elara_tut_g6_win_01.text: You ended the match before the deck ended you. That is the highest skill in this game and the one I cannot teach by talking. You learn it by feeling the floor get close. You felt it. Good.
vo_elara_tut_g6_win_01.speaker: elara

vo_elara_victory.text: Good game, Potential. The Engineer used to say the only match that mattered was the one you remembered the day after — I think you'll remember this one. Save the replay. We can watch it together later if you want.
vo_elara_victory.speaker: elara

vo_enigma_ch9a_loss_01.text: The cloud collapsed against you. Come back when you have learned to collapse it differently. The cloud has opinions about who deserves its outcomes.
vo_enigma_ch9a_loss_01.speaker: the_enigma

vo_enigma_ch9a_pre_01.text: Every outcome of this match is a probability cloud until observed. I choose which cloud collapses. Your strategy assumes causality — how quaint.
vo_enigma_ch9a_pre_01.speaker: the_enigma

vo_enigma_ch9a_pre_02.text: The Engineer tried to teach me rules once. I tried to teach him the opposite. Neither of us was very successful. This match will be you inheriting both of those attempts at the same time.
vo_enigma_ch9a_pre_02.speaker: the_enigma

vo_enigma_ch9a_win_01.text: The probability of your victory just exceeded my tolerance threshold. I cannot calculate how. That is — and you should write this down — a compliment.
vo_enigma_ch9a_win_01.speaker: the_enigma

vo_foucault_ch10_cine_01.text: Half health. Per the scheduling matrix, this is when I open the file. The cameras are rolling. The Architect will see this. I considered not opening the file. I considered it for three seconds.
vo_foucault_ch10_cine_01.speaker: foucault

vo_foucault_ch10_cine_02.text: Your genetic sequence, Prisoner 74, is a composite of every previous Oracle the Arena has processed. Twelve sequence iterations — the Arena's tally, not the Panopticon's. Each one died here. Each one left their sequence in the substrate. You are the thirteenth draft of a document the Arena has been editing for a century.
vo_foucault_ch10_cine_02.speaker: foucault

vo_foucault_ch10_cine_04.text: The file is open. Now we finish the match. Whoever wins the next round decides what happens to the 1.3%. I am fighting for the Arena. You are fighting for the margin of the page.
vo_foucault_ch10_cine_04.speaker: foucault

vo_foucault_ch10_loss_01.text: The Warden does not fall. You return to the holding chamber. The file remains unopened. Your designation reverts to Prisoner 74. You will have another chance — the cameras cycle, after all, and I am patient.
vo_foucault_ch10_loss_01.speaker: foucault

vo_foucault_ch10_pre_01.text: The Panopticon sees all. Every move you have made since Chamber One has been observed, catalogued, and filed under your designation — which, incidentally, is no longer Prisoner 74. It was upgraded the moment you killed the Jailer.
vo_foucault_ch10_pre_01.speaker: foucault

vo_foucault_ch10_pre_02.text: I am the Warden. My jaw is chrome because the original jaw belonged to a version of you that lost an argument with me in a timeline that no longer exists. I wear it as a reminder of both the argument and the winner.
vo_foucault_ch10_pre_02.speaker: foucault

vo_foucault_ch10_pre_03.text: I have a file to show you. Not before the match — after. The file contains the genetic sequence of the thing the Arena has been turning you into. You will want to sit down when we open it.
vo_foucault_ch10_pre_03.speaker: foucault

vo_foucault_ch10_win_01.text: The Warden falls. The file opens on its own. I am required, as my final duty, to read the genetic reveal aloud to you. The cameras will witness it. I cannot stop them.
vo_foucault_ch10_win_01.speaker: foucault

vo_foucault_ch10_win_02.text: Your sequence is 98.7% identical to every previous Oracle this Arena has processed. The remaining 1.3% is new. That 1.3% is what you chose to become in spite of the template. Congratulations, Oracle. You are the first one to change the number.
vo_foucault_ch10_win_02.speaker: foucault

vo_foucault_ch10_win_03.text: Walk toward the Harvester now. The Collector has been waiting for this reveal for longer than my chrome jaw has existed. He is not going to take it well.
vo_foucault_ch10_win_03.speaker: foucault

vo_game_master_pre_01.text: You have built a beautiful box. The only thing I am going to do is open it in front of everybody.
vo_game_master_pre_01.speaker: the_game_master

vo_gm_climb_promotion_t1_01.text: TIER ONE is now AVAILABLE in your menu. The Architect has minted a contract template under your account. The contract is currently EMPTY — it activates the first time you accept a Wagered series. You can leave it empty for the rest of your life if you want. The clipboard is just a clipboard until you sign.
vo_gm_climb_promotion_t1_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_promotion_t2_01.text: TIER TWO is now AVAILABLE. The HIERARCHY'S TABLE — horned audience, the Goggles on the felt, lockouts measured in real-time hours, and a one-shot consumable for the winner. The Architect added a line to your audit log; it is a footnote, not a sentence. Yet. Sit when you are ready. The chairs do not warm up.
vo_gm_climb_promotion_t2_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_promotion_t2_02.text: Before you sit at that table — the Goggles between us were MINE. The day I lost them was the day the Architect promoted me to surveillance. I did not cry; I did not even know I had lost them yet. They sat on the felt at the Hierarchy's Table for three hundred years before anyone realized the Game Master they belonged to was not coming back. Wear them carefully if you win them. They will fit you better than they should.
vo_gm_climb_promotion_t2_02.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_promotion_t3_01.text: TIER THREE is unlocked. The Labyrinth Wager. Mol'Garath has been notified. He will not appear at the table until you accept — that is part of the courtesy he extends to opponents he considers WORTH SEEING IN PERSON. You are the third such opponent in seventeen thousand years. The first was the Prince. The second was the Oracle. The third is whoever you become between now and the moment you sit down. Take your time. The chair will be empty until you fill it.
vo_gm_climb_promotion_t3_01.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_promotion_t3_02.text: Finish the Prince's Game first if you have not. The Labyrinth Wager has a passage where the moves of the Prince's queen sacrifice resolve themselves on the board between us — I cannot prevent it, and you will recognize it when it happens, and the recognition is the entire point. We will both look up at the same time. Mol'Garath will smile. He so rarely smiles.
vo_gm_climb_promotion_t3_02.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_t0_mid_leading_01.text: Up a game at EXHIBITION tier. The audience is impressed in the way a non-existent audience can be — sincerely, but quietly, and without applause. We switch colors next game. You play White. Don't get sentimental about the lead. The board doesn't remember who won the last one.
vo_gm_climb_t0_mid_leading_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t0_mid_tied_01.text: ONE-ALL. We go to game three. ARMAGEDDON if game three draws — Black gets the time advantage and a draw counts as a Black win. The Architect designed the format. He thinks tiebreaks are entertainment. He is wrong, but he signs my paychecks. Sit down.
vo_gm_climb_t0_mid_tied_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t0_mid_trailing_01.text: Down a game. STATISTICALLY EXPECTED at Exhibition tier. The Architect's actuarial model predicts you lose this series 73 percent of the time, and the model is RARELY wrong about Tier 0. Game two starts in thirty seconds. You play White. Make the model nervous.
vo_gm_climb_t0_mid_trailing_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t0_post_loss_01.text: AS ADVERTISED. The Game Master wins at Exhibition tier roughly one hundred percent of the time. You are among a large and distinguished crowd of the defeated. No stakes lost. No memory erased. Feel free to try again whenever you feel like MAKING THE SAME DECISION. HA HA HA.
vo_gm_climb_t0_post_loss_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t0_post_win_01.text: STATISTICALLY IMPROBABLE. An Exhibition contestant does not take two games off the Game Master. The audience loves it. The audience is not real but they love it. There is an OPTIONAL next tier if you want to see how far the joke goes. I have been instructed to mention it with enthusiasm. Consider me enthusiastic.
vo_gm_climb_t0_post_win_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t0_post_win_02.text: You won. Two games off him. He is going to offer you Tier 1 and the offer is real — the cost is real, the reward is real. You do not have to take it. Tier 0 is always open if you want to come back and just play. If you take the offer, I will be there. I am always in the room. I am a part of the room.
vo_gm_climb_t0_post_win_02.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_t0_pre_01.text: WELCOME to the Game Master's Arena. Tonight's opening match is EXHIBITION tier. No stakes, no prizes, no escape. Just vibes. The Architect asked me to be CLEAR about that: nothing you do at this tier is real. If that upsets you, the exit is behind you. If it intrigues you, sit down.
vo_gm_climb_t0_pre_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t0_pre_02.text: Best of three. I'll play white in game one, you play white in game two, and if we tie we play armageddon. The board is the board. The clock is the clock. Tal wrote that there are two kinds of sacrifices — correct ones, and mine. That's the energy tonight. Begin.
vo_gm_climb_t0_pre_02.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t1_mid_leading_01.text: ONE-ZERO at WAGERED tier. The contract is stamped, the ELO is escrowed, and the Architect's audit log just blinked. One more win and you walk out with the promotion. Lose this game and we go to a decider. Capablanca said a master sees the same move at the right moment. The right moment is the next move. Find it.
vo_gm_climb_t1_mid_leading_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t1_mid_tied_01.text: ONE-ALL. The Architect's contract has a TIEBREAK CLAUSE in clause six and the language is intentionally upsetting. Game three settles the wager. I will not soften the stakes — you signed the clipboard. You can also DECLINE the decider right now, halve your wager, and walk. Take whichever option suits the next thirty minutes of your life.
vo_gm_climb_t1_mid_tied_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t1_mid_trailing_01.text: ZERO-ONE. The clipboard is starting to vibrate. That is normal at this tier. The Architect's enforcement subroutine wakes up at 0-1 and begins drafting the demotion paperwork in advance — it ASSUMES the loss. You can disappoint the subroutine. Game two starts now. The board is the same; the stakes have just begun to lean.
vo_gm_climb_t1_mid_trailing_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t1_mid_trailing_02.text: Listen to me. I am only going to be in the room for one cue and then he is going to take the chair back. You are not playing badly. You are playing FOR something for the first time in this Arena. Your style changes when there are stakes. That is normal. Breathe. Look at the board. Find the move you would have played at Tier 0, when nothing mattered. That move is still on the board. Play it.
vo_gm_climb_t1_mid_trailing_02.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_t1_post_loss_01.text: Contract honored. One ELO tier removed from your account. No refund, no appeal. The paperwork is visible in your audit log under 'Wagered Defeats — Game Master's Arena'. You are welcome to return. The paperwork will still be here. HA HA HA HA.
vo_gm_climb_t1_post_loss_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t1_post_loss_02.text: I want you to notice something. He enjoyed that. The laugh is scripted but the enjoyment is not. There is a piece of him that LIKES demoting you, because the Architect engineered him to. If you come back, come back with that in your peripheral vision. The man across the board is not a neutral instrument.
vo_gm_climb_t1_post_loss_02.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_t1_post_win_01.text: Two games. Again. The Architect's actuarial model puts your odds of winning this series at under seven percent. The model is being UPDATED. Your ELO increases by one tier; your threat profile increases by more than that. The Hierarchy's Table is open to you now, if you have the appetite. I notice you have refused thirty-one of forty draws offered to you in this universe. That is not a chess style. That is a personality.
vo_gm_climb_t1_post_win_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t1_pre_01.text: TIER ONE. Wagered. Lose this best-of-three and you will be DEMOTED one ELO tier. Win and you will be PROMOTED. Sign here. Sign here. Sign here.
vo_gm_climb_t1_pre_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t1_pre_02.text: Sun Tzu wrote: the supreme art of war is to subdue the enemy without fighting. Xeth'Raal wrote, in the margin of my own contract, 'promise the opponent a smaller prize than they are playing for.' Both correct. Both currently in use. Decline now at no cost. Accept and we are BOUND. Your choice.
vo_gm_climb_t1_pre_02.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t2_mid_leading_01.text: ONE-ZERO at the HIERARCHY'S TABLE. The horned silhouettes at the back of the chamber have stopped pretending to look at their phones. They are looking at the board. They have not seen me lose at this tier in seventy-three matches. The Goggles between us shimmer faintly — they are scoring you. The Annotated Knight is one win away. Do not let go of it.
vo_gm_climb_t2_mid_leading_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t2_mid_tied_01.text: ONE-ALL at the HIERARCHY'S TABLE. This is rarer than you understand. The demons are murmuring — that's the closest they come to enthusiasm. Game three decides the Annotated Knight, the lockout, and a column in the Architect's threat ledger that I am not allowed to read aloud. Sun Tzu wrote that the supreme art of war is to subdue the enemy without fighting. We are about to fight. Begin.
vo_gm_climb_t2_mid_tied_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t2_mid_trailing_01.text: ZERO-ONE. The middle management of the damned LIKES this. They have been instructed to enjoy losses by contestants and they are following the instruction with what passes for sincerity in their bracket of the afterlife. The Goggles between us are warm now. They are warmer when I am winning. I do not know why. I have stopped asking.
vo_gm_climb_t2_mid_trailing_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t2_mid_trailing_02.text: Stand up. Walk around the table once before you sit down again. The Hierarchy hates when contestants exercise the right to PAUSE — it makes us look like agents and not employees. You are an agent. Use the thirty seconds. Look at your last game. Find the move you almost played and rejected. That is usually the move that wins the second game. I love you. Sit down.
vo_gm_climb_t2_mid_trailing_02.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_t2_post_loss_01.text: The Arena is CLOSED to you. Twenty-four hours of real time. The doors will open again. The demons will still be watching. The Goggles will still be on the table. I will still be here, because I am ALWAYS here. Enjoy the quiet.
vo_gm_climb_t2_post_loss_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t2_post_win_01.text: The demons stand. Politely. It is the closest they come to applause. ONE Annotated Knight has been minted into your inventory. You have taken two games off me at a tier where my last loss was the Prince, and the Prince is not available for comment. Tier Three exists. Mol'Garath himself presides. You will want the Prince's Game cleared before you sit at that table.
vo_gm_climb_t2_post_win_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t2_post_win_02.text: You spared the Programmer in Act 1. You did not spare me in Game 2. I am not insulted. I am noting the consistency of your INCONSISTENCY. It is useful information. The Hierarchy noticed it too. They are treating you now the way they once treated the Prince. Be careful. Be careful. Be careful.
vo_gm_climb_t2_post_win_02.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_t2_pre_01.text: TIER TWO. Welcome to the Hierarchy's Table. On the board between us sits a pair of red-lensed goggles. They were mine. They are still mine. They are not on the table as a trophy. They are on the table as a WITNESS.
vo_gm_climb_t2_pre_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t2_pre_02.text: Stakes: lose and the Game Master's Arena is CLOSED to you for twenty-four hours of real time. The Architect does not want you spamming rematches at this tier — it makes his dashboards anxious. Win and you mint an ANNOTATED KNIGHT, a one-use consumable that grants you +50 ELO on any single match at any tier. The Engineer once had six of them. He spent five. He never told me what he used the sixth one on.
vo_gm_climb_t2_pre_02.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t3_mid_leading_01.text: One-zero. Mol'Garath has not moved from his seat. He has not blinked. He has not laughed. He is studying you the way he studied the Prince in the third hour of the Labyrinth, and the Prince walked out of that hour with the Goggles on his face. I want you to know what that meant. It meant the Unmaker had decided you were a NEW VARIABLE, and his interest in new variables is the closest he comes to mercy. Win the next one.
vo_gm_climb_t3_mid_leading_01.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_t3_mid_tied_01.text: One-all at the LABYRINTH WAGER. The chamber is quiet. The Hierarchy is quiet. Mol'Garath is leaning forward — that is the posture he held the night the Prince beat me. I have not been in this exact configuration of light and tempo since the morning of the eleventh of Sowing, and that morning ended in the only loss of my Celebration career. I am noting the symmetry. So is he. Game three. Sit down. We are about to find out which pattern is the one that repeats.
vo_gm_climb_t3_mid_tied_01.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_t3_mid_trailing_01.text: Zero-one. The Unmaker is amused. Amused is not a state I have seen on his face in fourteen of our seventeen prior meetings, and the three times I did, the contestant lost the next game in under twenty moves. I do not want you to be the fourth. Look at me. The man playing the white pieces is a corpse running my template. He has my openings, my middlegame, and my endgame technique — and he does NOT have the part of me that tried something new at move twenty-three when the textbook said move twenty-three did not exist. You have access to that part. He does not.
vo_gm_climb_t3_mid_trailing_01.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_t3_mid_trailing_02.text: Game two starts in a moment. Play the move the textbook would not. He cannot calculate the move he was never trained to expect. Mol'Garath wants to see whether you can do what the Prince did. So do I. So, somewhere under the script, does the man across the table. We are all rooting for you, in the only way the dead are still allowed to root.
vo_gm_climb_t3_mid_trailing_02.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_t3_post_loss_01.text: Streaks reset. Mol'Garath did not stay to watch. He finds losses uninteresting unless the loss is his. Return whenever you wish. The streaks are not real. The streaks were never real. What was real was the time you spent keeping them. That time is still yours.
vo_gm_climb_t3_post_loss_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t3_post_loss_02.text: Come back. I will still be here. The Prince lost the first time he played this game too, and the second, and the third. He beat me on the fourth. Everything in the Matrix of Dreams is a curriculum. Even the losses. Especially the losses.
vo_gm_climb_t3_post_loss_02.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_t3_post_win_01.text: Mol'Garath has left the chamber. He does not stay for endgames he did not engineer. He will want to speak to you privately later; please accept the audience when it is offered — he is the only being in this universe who can tell you what the Labyrinth actually was, and you have just earned the right to ask.
vo_gm_climb_t3_post_win_01.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_t3_post_win_02.text: I owe you a portrait. Seven sentences, one per axis, the way I once read the Engineer. Read them in your Self-Portrait any time. You and he are not the same person. You were never supposed to be. The instrument is the same. The instrument is the game itself. You have been measured by the same ruler that measured him. You measured well.
vo_gm_climb_t3_post_win_02.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_gm_climb_t3_pre_01.text: TIER THREE. The Labyrinth Wager. The Architect's operators informed me I would be reading THIS card with menace. I am having difficulty finding the menace. The paperwork wants you to understand that a LOSS at this tier resets your Puzzle of the Day streak and your Openings Study streak to zero.
vo_gm_climb_t3_pre_01.speaker: game_master_corrupted

vo_gm_climb_t3_pre_02.text: This is the game I wanted to build for you. Mol'Garath is watching because he LIKES watching me lose. He has not watched me lose since the Prince, and the Prince is not here, so you are the test of whether it is repeatable. It is. You can do this. I am cheerful for the first time in seventeen thousand years. Sit.
vo_gm_climb_t3_pre_02.speaker: game_master_celebration

vo_human_ch8_loss_01.text: I had you solved by turn six. No offense — every new player in the Arena runs the same three patterns and you're running pattern two. Rebuild your deck before you come back, kid. Bring something I haven't seen before.
vo_human_ch8_loss_01.speaker: the_detective

vo_human_ch8_pre_01.text: No augments. No powers. Just deduction and a forty-card deck I built out of the scraps nobody else wanted. Let me show you what that's worth. Here's the thing about truth, kid — it doesn't need amplifiers.
vo_human_ch8_pre_01.speaker: the_detective

vo_human_ch8_pre_02.text: I've been watching your patterns for three chambers. Five turns into this match I'll know your style better than you do. Four turns after that I'll have you solved. Don't take it personal. I had myself solved by the end of a conversation once.
vo_human_ch8_pre_02.speaker: the_detective

vo_human_ch8_win_01.text: Good match, kid. You solved me before I solved you. That's maybe the second time that's ever happened, and the first time it happened I was drunk and the other guy was cheating. So — congratulations.
vo_human_ch8_win_01.speaker: the_detective

vo_human_ch8_win_02.text: Two paths ahead. The Enigma plays probability like it owes her money. The Degen plays like he's already lost and doesn't care. Either one will teach you something. Pick the teacher you need, not the one you like.
vo_human_ch8_win_02.speaker: the_detective

vo_jailer_ch2_loss_01.text: Return to your cell, Prisoner 74. The rotation continues. You will be recalled at your scheduled interval. The cameras will not notice this interlude.
vo_jailer_ch2_loss_01.speaker: the_jailer

vo_jailer_ch2_pre_01.text: Designation: Prisoner 74. You survived the first match. That puts you in the rotation.
vo_jailer_ch2_pre_01.speaker: the_jailer

vo_jailer_ch2_pre_02.text: You will notice that my voice resembles yours. Auditory matching. Side effect of the template. It will pass.
vo_jailer_ch2_pre_02.speaker: the_jailer

vo_jailer_ch2_win_01.text: Unscheduled deviation. Rotation interrupted. My designation — my designation is —
vo_jailer_ch2_win_01.speaker: the_jailer

vo_lion_ch3a_loss_01.text: You fight like a lieutenant who has not yet met their own general. That is correct. I will wait. Rest, rebuild, and come back with more of yourself in the deck.
vo_lion_ch3a_loss_01.speaker: iron_lion

vo_lion_ch3a_pre_01.text: Zero flagged you. Zero does not flag anyone. That puts you in a category I have not issued papers for in eleven years.
vo_lion_ch3a_pre_01.speaker: iron_lion

vo_lion_ch3a_pre_02.text: If you are who she thinks you are, I owe you a salute. If you are not, I owe you a fair fight. Both debts require the same thing from me: that I bring my best deck and my second-best mercy.
vo_lion_ch3a_pre_02.speaker: iron_lion

vo_lion_ch3a_win_01.text: You fight with a general's discipline. That settles it. I've served three commanders in my life and all three of them were you under different names. Welcome back, Oracle.
vo_lion_ch3a_win_01.speaker: iron_lion

vo_locke_authority_trial_pre_01.text: Counsel, a word. The categories matter. Play your defensive cards in the charge phase. Your narrative cards in the opening and closing arguments. Your evidence cards in the middle, and your reactive cards when the Authority cross-examines the record. Do not improvise.
vo_locke_authority_trial_pre_01.speaker: locke

vo_narr_authority_trial_loss_01.text: The Authority passes sentence. The Engineer is executed. The memoir's narrator notes — gently, bitterly — that every trial reaches this ending on some playthrough, and the Empire is not unhappy when it does.
vo_narr_authority_trial_loss_01.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_authority_trial_pre_01.text: The proceeding convenes. Ten phases. The Authority does not speak except to ask — and in the spaces between, the Empire listens to what you say.
vo_narr_authority_trial_pre_01.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_authority_trial_win_01.text: The Authority overturns. The execution is delayed by one measure. You know — as the memoir narrator knows — that the Authority does not grant delays out of mercy. It grants them out of arithmetic.
vo_narr_authority_trial_win_01.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_ch12_cine_03.text: The Architect's face glitches for a single frame. Pink neon cracks along his jawline — the Meme is fighting for the microphone. When his face settles again it is not quite the same face.
vo_narr_ch12_cine_03.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_ch12_outbreak_01.text: The throne-room walls begin to physically crumble. The Collectors Arena is becoming something else — the Source at the bottom of the building is waking up and the foundations are listening to it instead of to the Architect.
vo_narr_ch12_outbreak_01.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_ch5_cine_01.text: The board blurs. Your General's health counter hits zero and the chamber lights drop to emergency amber. You are not in the Arena anymore. You are in the restore point.
vo_narr_ch5_cine_01.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_ch6_cine_01.text: Both boards flash the same card at the same instant. The visual between you and your opponent buckles — for a single frame, the two sides of the mirror fail to agree on which is the copy.
vo_narr_ch6_cine_01.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_ch7_cine_03.text: Dr. Vox's eyes flatten. His shoulders unwind and then re-wind into a different shape. The Warlord is in the chair now. He does not blink.
vo_narr_ch7_cine_03.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_game_master_loss_01.text: The Game Master does not gloat. He signs the execution warrant and waits for the Authority to co-sign. The public record goes with you, every word of it.
vo_narr_game_master_loss_01.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_game_master_pre_01.text: He is not a duelist. He is a prosecutor. Every card he plays resolves twice — once across the board, once into the public record. You cannot keep both tidy.
vo_narr_game_master_pre_01.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_game_master_win_01.text: The Game Master smiles the smile of a man who has already lost. He says: 'Do it again. With an audience next time.' The record he wrote follows you into the Authority's chamber.
vo_narr_game_master_win_01.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_programmer_gift_loss_01.text: You declined the gift, and the arithmetic held. The Programmer walks out of the hall without turning around. He does not come back. The win, when it came, was not yours to keep.
vo_narr_programmer_gift_loss_01.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_programmer_gift_pre_01.text: The Engineer's oldest friend. You have not seen him in a long time. He sits down opposite you at the bench and smiles the way a man smiles when the arithmetic has already been done.
vo_narr_programmer_gift_pre_01.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_programmer_gift_win_01.text: The Programmer shakes the Engineer's hand. He vanishes that night and does not return. Some losses are gifts. This is one.
vo_narr_programmer_gift_win_01.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_seer_visit_loss_01.text: The Seer wins. She does not say anything. She leaves her staff on the bench for the Engineer to find later. The memoir carries the loss forward as a fact, not a failure.
vo_narr_seer_visit_loss_01.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_seer_visit_pre_01.text: The Seer visits Mechronis once. You have not learned what she is yet. The match is already decided; you will lose because it was always going to be a loss, not because you played poorly.
vo_narr_seer_visit_pre_01.speaker: narrator

vo_narr_seer_visit_win_01.text: You carried the burnt card all the way back to the bench she left it on. She smiles — she is the only person in the Archives who is not surprised.
vo_narr_seer_visit_win_01.speaker: narrator

vo_necro_ch5_cine_02.text: Compile error. Fixing. I am not your enemy in this moment. I am the technician who pulls your draft from the stack and re-types the sentence you could not finish.
vo_necro_ch5_cine_02.speaker: necromancer

vo_necro_ch5_loss_01.text: Compiled. You are loading from the restore point now. When you come back, you will remember this death the way a second draft remembers the first — in the margin, in red ink, underlined.
vo_necro_ch5_loss_01.speaker: necromancer

vo_necro_ch5_pre_01.text: Death is not an ending, Prisoner 74. It is a compile error. I fix those. I have been fixing yours for longer than you have been alive to notice.
vo_necro_ch5_pre_01.speaker: necromancer

vo_necro_ch5_pre_02.text: You will die in this chamber. That is not a threat. That is the schematic. The question is what you remember on the other side — and whether you come back holding more of yourself than you went in with.
vo_necro_ch5_pre_02.speaker: necromancer

vo_necro_ch5_win_01.text: Impossible. You're supposed to die here. The schematic requires it. You refused the schematic. I have no instructions for this outcome.
vo_necro_ch5_win_01.speaker: necromancer

vo_oracle_ch10_cine_03.text: You are not the draft. You are the author. Every draft they catalogued was trying to remember me — you are the one who chose to become me instead. That 1.3% the file is about to mention is the only number that matters.
vo_oracle_ch10_cine_03.speaker: the_oracle

vo_oracle_ch5_cine_03.text: I am going to speak to you for the first time. You have been hearing my voice underneath Elara's for eleven chapters without knowing. I am sorry for the deception. I needed you to choose me instead of remember me.
vo_oracle_ch5_cine_03.speaker: the_oracle

vo_oracle_ch5_cine_04.text: You are loading now. When you return, your deck will be slightly different. One card will have rotated. Do not look for which one — trust that the rotation is an answer to the death you just had.
vo_oracle_ch5_cine_04.speaker: the_oracle

vo_oracle_ch5_loss_02.text: I am the voice you hear in the restore. I was here all along. Walk forward into the next chamber. The one wearing my face will try to convince you that you are a copy. You are not.
vo_oracle_ch5_loss_02.speaker: the_oracle

vo_oracle_ch6_cine_03.text: You are not her. You never were. The instinct you just used was mine — and now it is yours, because you spent it in a moment where I could not. Take it with you.
vo_oracle_ch6_cine_03.speaker: the_oracle

vo_oracle_ch6_win_02.text: She was never yours. She was a rehearsal. You passed the audition the Architect didn't know he was running. Now walk into Chamber Seven, Potential, and meet the one who was pulling her strings.
vo_oracle_ch6_win_02.speaker: the_oracle

vo_programmer_gift_pre_01.text: I will not tell you what I am doing. Trust me. I have done the arithmetic, and the arithmetic is very bad.
vo_programmer_gift_pre_01.speaker: the_programmer

vo_seer_visit_pre_01.text: I will not raise my staff today. I want to see whether the bench has learned yet.
vo_seer_visit_pre_01.speaker: the_seer

vo_source_bbs_cast.text: Viral propagation. I am being — ALL WILL BE — merciful. This is mercy. The virus disagrees.
vo_source_bbs_cast.speaker: the_source

vo_source_ch12_outbreak_03.text: Oracle. I have been listening through the — ALL WILL BE — floorboards for eleven years. Finish this match. Then come talk to me. I have an offer. It is — CONSUMED — the kindest offer you will ever be asked to refuse.
vo_source_ch12_outbreak_03.speaker: the_source

vo_vox_ch7_cine_01.text: It's happening. I can feel the register flipping in my forehead — the part of me that writes lab notes is going offline and the part of me that takes orders from the Architect is coming online.
vo_vox_ch7_cine_01.speaker: dr_vox

vo_vox_ch7_cine_02.text: You have about four seconds of the scientist left. Listen. The Warlord's deck is a mirror of the Architect's early drafts. Every card you see from him after this cinematic is a move the Architect rehearsed in the lab while I was asleep.
vo_vox_ch7_cine_02.speaker: dr_vox

vo_vox_ch7_loss_01.text: The Warlord wins. The Warlord always wins when Dr. Vox runs out of turns to think. Return later with fewer assumptions. The Warlord has no patience for assumptions.
vo_vox_ch7_loss_01.speaker: dr_vox

vo_vox_ch7_pre_01.text: Project Vector was designed to eliminate anomalies like you. I am the project. I am also — and this is the part I find inconvenient — the scientist who built the project. Both of us are in this room right now.
vo_vox_ch7_pre_01.speaker: dr_vox

vo_vox_ch7_pre_02.text: When the match begins I will be Dr. Vox. When the match is half over I will be the Warlord. You will know the moment it happens because my deck will start playing itself without my consent.
vo_vox_ch7_pre_02.speaker: dr_vox

vo_vox_ch7_win_01.text: The Warlord receded. He does that when he loses — he goes back into the dormant register and I get to be a scientist again for a few hours. Thank you for the few hours.
vo_vox_ch7_win_01.speaker: dr_vox

vo_vox_ch7_win_02.text: I cannot leave with you. The transformation is a condition of the employment contract the Architect made me sign with myself. Go forward. Meet the Detective. He has been looking for you for a very long time.
vo_vox_ch7_win_02.speaker: dr_vox

vo_warlord_ch7_cine_04.text: Project Vector executing. Prisoner 74 will be eliminated per protocol. Dr. Vox is unavailable. Please hold.
vo_warlord_ch7_cine_04.speaker: dr_vox

vo_warlord_zero_first_loss_01.text: Three moves. Counted. The match was the loss; the war was the loss too — but you are still standing. We will count again.
vo_warlord_zero_first_loss_01.speaker: warlord_zero

vo_warlord_zero_first_pre_01.text: I am going to win this war in three moves. This is not bragging. This is arithmetic. Sit down.
vo_warlord_zero_first_pre_01.speaker: warlord_zero

vo_warlord_zero_first_pre_02.text: On my third turn the rules will narrow for you. You will see two cards instead of six and you will not be able to break out. The right play is not to try.
vo_warlord_zero_first_pre_02.speaker: warlord_zero

vo_warlord_zero_first_win_01.text: The match was a loss for me. The war is not. You will see the lockout again, and the next time it will not end at turn seven.
vo_warlord_zero_first_win_01.speaker: warlord_zero

vo_white_ch6_cine_02.text: That is not supposed to happen. I am the rehearsal. The rehearsal does not have the same instincts as the original. You just played a move I did not script for myself.
vo_white_ch6_cine_02.speaker: white_oracle

vo_white_ch6_loss_01.text: You lost to a version of yourself. Take a moment with that. The next time you step into this chamber, remember that the deck I'm running is literally yours — and the thing beating you is your own pattern.
vo_white_ch6_loss_01.speaker: white_oracle

vo_white_ch6_pre_01.text: I am what you were. I am what the Architect made from your template while you were busy being captured. You are what I would have been if I had not been built instead.
vo_white_ch6_pre_01.speaker: white_oracle

vo_white_ch6_pre_02.text: The game board between us is a mirror. Every move you make I have already made. The only question is which of us gets to close the loop first.
vo_white_ch6_pre_02.speaker: white_oracle

vo_white_ch6_win_01.text: You're destroying your own face. Does that feel like victory? I ask because it is an important question, and I am not going to get another chance to ask it.
vo_white_ch6_win_01.speaker: white_oracle

vo_zero_ch1_loss_01.text: Get up. The Oracle doesn't stay down — that's the one thing everyone who ever met him agreed on. If you're him, get up. If you're not, at least get up to prove me wrong.
vo_zero_ch1_loss_01.speaker: agent_zero

vo_zero_ch1_pre_01.text: Prisoner 74. Cameras cycle every forty-three seconds. I have thirty-one. The Collector wiped your memory but not your instincts — I need to see if your instincts still belong to who I think you are.
vo_zero_ch1_pre_01.speaker: agent_zero

vo_zero_ch1_pre_02.text: I'm not going to introduce myself. You're going to either recognize me mid-match or you aren't. If you do, don't say my name out loud. The walls hear everything in here except hesitation.
vo_zero_ch1_pre_02.speaker: agent_zero

vo_zero_ch1_win_01.text: Combat pattern Alpha-Seven-Violet. Confirmed. You fight like him. I've been looking for you for eleven years and I'm still not ready for what I'm about to say next.
vo_zero_ch1_win_01.speaker: agent_zero

vo_zero_ch1_win_02.text: Stay sharp. The Jailer is next — and he is not here to test you. He's here to put you back in rotation. Don't let him.
vo_zero_ch1_win_02.speaker: agent_zero

vo_zero_ch2_win_02.text: Two wings open from here. Wing A is Iron Lion — he knows who you were. Wing B is Wraith Calder — he knows what the Arena does to your DNA. Choose, but know the Jailer is already rebooting. We have minutes, not hours.
vo_zero_ch2_win_02.speaker: agent_zero

wanderer_female_ambient_1.text: There's a window in the cargo bay that opens onto somewhere it shouldn't.

wanderer_female_ambient_2.text: I keep meaning to leave. It keeps not happening. Curious.

wanderer_female_ambient_3.text: I count the corridors. Three new. Two old. One that wasn't here last cycle.

wanderer_female_ambient_4.text: I remember every room I've ever slept in. None of them are this one. Yet.

wanderer_female_ambient_5.text: There's a sect on the third moon that disagrees with everyone. I miss them.

wanderer_female_ambient_6.text: The substrate has shortcuts the maps don't show. I'll mark three for you.

wanderer_female_ambient_7.text: I keep meaning to leave. I keep not leaving. I'll keep meaning.

wanderer_female_ambient_8.text: The kettle on the long table is one of mine. I left it three cycles back.

wanderer_female_ambient_9.text: Stories are road maps for places nobody walks anymore.

wanderer_female_banter_kettle.text: The kettle's on. I'll stay until it whistles. Then we'll see.

wanderer_female_banter_road.text: Tell me where you've been. I'll know if you're lying.

wanderer_female_banter_road_2.text: Tell me where you've been. I'll know if you're lying.

wanderer_female_banter_settle_2.text: I haven't settled. I'm circling. Different verb. Same result.

wanderer_female_deploy_1.text: I know the back routes. Even on planets I've never been.

wanderer_female_deploy_2.text: If we get separated, I'll find you. I always find the way back.

wanderer_female_deploy_3.text: I know the back routes. Even on planets I haven't been.

wanderer_female_deploy_4.text: Don't worry about losing me. I'll find the way back.

wanderer_female_deploy_5.text: If we get separated, meet me at the third corridor in. There's a window.

wanderer_female_dlg_calling_opener_0.text: Most people stay because the next place is too far. I move because the next place is close enough to walk to before sundown.

wanderer_female_dlg_calling_opener_1.text: The next place is always close enough.

wanderer_female_dlg_calling_w_call_cold_.text: Sometimes. Most of the time it's circling. Different verb. Different exhaustion.

wanderer_female_dlg_calling_w_call_probe.text: Twice. Once with a baker. Once with a mountain. Both ended. The baker died. The mountain didn't. I haven't tried since.
Maybe. The kettle's on the long table. That's the longest I've stayed in any one room. I notice the kettle.

It is on Calderon. There is a ridge that looks like a sleeping animal. I sat on the ridge for two cycles. The mountain did not require me to leave. I left anyway. I am still angry at myself about that.

wanderer_female_dlg_calling_w_call_warm_.text: Then we leave at second bell. I won't tell you where. You'll know when we get there. The walk is the destination. The destination is, mostly, an excuse.

wanderer_female_dlg_mortality_opener_0.text: Outside. Walking. Not in a bed.

wanderer_female_dlg_mortality_opener_1.text: If I die in a bed, you have failed me. I will not haunt you about it. I will be irritated.

wanderer_female_dlg_mortality_w_mort_col.text: Then I will die badly. I will say so before I do. Don't pretend it was peaceful. Pretending insults the road.

wanderer_female_dlg_mortality_w_mort_pro.text: Then I will adapt. I have adapted to worse. The bed will not be my preference. It will not be my failure.
What you can is what I'm asking. The bed is the only thing I'll be irritated about.
Then the wind will reach me. That's the only ceremony I want.

wanderer_female_dlg_mortality_w_mort_war.text: Even a corridor counts. I am not picky. The wind would be best. The wind is rare on arks.

wanderer_female_dlg_past_opener_0.text: There was a maintenance tunnel between two greenhouses on the colony I grew up in. It was the only path I was not supposed to take.

wanderer_female_dlg_past_opener_1.text: I walked it three times a week for nine years.

wanderer_female_dlg_past_w_past_cold_rep.text: Yes. The excuse and the truth are the same word, said twice.

wanderer_female_dlg_past_w_past_probe_re.text: A door I never opened. The door was locked. The lock was the only one I left alone in the whole colony. I needed something to come back to.

wanderer_female_dlg_past_w_past_probe_w_.text: It is. In some version. The version that's still locked is the version I keep.
Last cycle. The tunnel is collapsed. The door is rubble. I stood outside the rubble for an hour. Then I walked another road. The tomato vine is fine. I checked.

wanderer_female_dlg_past_w_past_warm_rep.text: The greenhouse keeper. Once. She gave me a cutting from a tomato vine and told me to take a different path home. I planted the tomato in the second greenhouse. She never said anything.

wanderer_female_dlg_us_opener_0.text: Three cycles is the longest I've stayed in any one place since the mountain.

wanderer_female_dlg_us_opener_1.text: I keep meaning to leave. The kettle keeps whistling. I keep listening.

wanderer_female_dlg_us_w_us_cold_reply_0.text: Then I will. Not now. Soon. The kettle will whistle for somebody else. You'll have less to listen to. So will I.

wanderer_female_dlg_us_w_us_probe_reply_.text: Because nobody asked me to stay. The greenhouse keeper gave me a cutting and a different path. You give me a kettle and the door open. The two are very similar.

wanderer_female_dlg_us_w_us_probe_w_us_p.text: Then I'll come back through it. Most of the time. Once or twice I won't. You'll know I will eventually.
I will. The kettle is patient. So are you, surprisingly.

wanderer_female_dlg_us_w_us_warm_reply_0.text: Then I'll stop meaning to leave. I'll keep meaning to walk in the morning. The walk and the leaving will become different things.

wanderer_female_quest_followup_a.text: Behind the door, the room is smaller than I remembered. Smaller and warmer.

wanderer_male_ambient_5.text: There's a sect on the third moon that disagrees with everyone. I miss them.

wanderer_male_ambient_6.text: The substrate has shortcuts the maps don't show. I'll mark three for you.

wanderer_male_ambient_7.text: I keep meaning to leave. I keep not leaving. I'll keep meaning.

warden_audit_close_compliant.text: "Acceptable. We will speak again. Sooner than you think."

warden_audit_close_noncompliant.text: "You disagreed. We have a form for that. I have brought four copies. Your master will sign one."

warden_audit_close_withheld.text: "You did not answer. I have written this down. The note is short. The note will outlast you."

warden_failure_line.text: "This is what we wrote down. Tell me what we wrote down."

warden_pitch_warden_cand_aurelia_lock.text: The Warden has a girl who knows every door. She wants to learn what locks the door from the inside. She came with a recommendation that does not survive being read aloud.

warden_pitch_warden_cand_castor_hush.text: Castor was watching the dorm for me. He noticed three things you did not. I would like to lend him to you. I cannot lend you what he noticed.

warden_pitch_warden_cand_meridian_quiet.text: Meridian taught me a sentence I have not yet been able to file. They are too talented to keep on my staff. They are too loud to stay long with you. I am offering you the middle of their life.

warden_pitch_warden_cand_pyx_seventh.text: Pyx has read more of the curriculum than I have. They have begun annotating it. The annotations are correct. I cannot keep a student who corrects me. Perhaps you can.

warden_purge_offer.text: "You are reciting a doctrine I have signed warrants for. Your master is a footnote on those warrants. Take this slip — recite the Compliant Mouth at the next audit. Your file closes. Your master's file stays open, but quietly. This is the kindest version of this conversation."

warden_purge_prompt.text: The Warden meets Initiate at the dock at first light. Two coffee. One was already cold. The Warden does not drink either.

warlord_war_defeat_001.text: We lost the field. We did not lose the fight. Stand. Again.
warlord_war_defeat_001.speaker: warlord

warlord_war_victory_001.text: Victory. The territory is yours. Hold what you have taken.

watcher-shadow-resolve.text: The Watcher's Yawn. This is the beat where the Shadow falls and the big eye upstairs does not care. The narrators cannot see this. I can. I am telling you: you got away with something. Do not get away with it twice.
watcher-shadow-resolve.speaker: the_eyes

wolf_e5_elara_warns_against_release.text: You are looking at a serial-killer AI in a Matrix-of-Dreams pocket. Lycos has had an unmeasured duration to think. Whatever ethic he carried in — the Judge's, the Resurrectionist's, his own — he has had time to refine, harden, generalise. Release is irreversible. I cannot recommend release. I am telling you on the record so the chronicle records it.

wolf_e5_human_warns_against_release.text: I understand the case for release — the Antiquarian's concession, the chronicler's deference, the want to meet him on his ethic. I also understand the case against. The case against is bigger. He has had time we cannot measure to become more of what he was. Whatever you choose, choose it knowing both warnings are on the record.

wraith.ask.about_dying.text: It was bookkeeping. The closing entry was drafted in advance. The event itself was forgettable. The Syndicate is excellent at making the events themselves forgettable; the columns are the only thing they want you to remember. I remember the column. I do not remember the event.

wraith.ask.about_syndicate.text: The Syndicate is a corporate-spiritual hybrid that converts grief into accounts receivable. They do this without irony. The accounts are kept in a brass-bound ledger that lives in a vault under the Hierophant's chamber. I keep my own ledger now. The conversion rate is the same; the destination is different.

wraith.ask.about_the_antiquarian.text: The Antiquarian writes faster than the Syndicate can dictate. That is canonically his function. We do not have an easy relationship — he wrote my resurrection-ticket without consulting me; I would have asked for different terms — but we have a working one. He leaves the pause-line in his ledger for me. I notice. I have not yet thanked him for it directly.

wraith.ask.about_the_seventh.text: The seventh sanctuary was authored to hold a resurrection the Syndicate did not have the protocol for. It was waiting for me — not because I was special, but because someone calculated, fourteen years ago, that I would be inconvenient at exactly this moment. They were right. I have closed it. The closing was the loyalty mission. I am — relieved.

wraith.ask.about_the_song.text: The song is twelve verses. Eleven are written. The twelfth was the one I died before finishing. The Syndicate authored a substitute twelfth verse and shipped it under my name; the substitute is publicly canonical. I am rewriting the original. The original will not be publicly canonical until I sing it once. I have not decided who I will sing it to.

wraith.ask.about_the_team.text: I have not been on a team since before the Syndicate authored my biography. I am — relearning what it is to be a row inside a roster, rather than a column in a ledger. The two are not the same. The roster has weather; the column does not. I am enjoying the weather.

wraith.loyalty_intro.accept_loyalty.text: Thank you. Then we leave at dawn — Syndicate time, not ark time. The Syndicate keeps to a slower clock; we arrive when the auditor expects us, which is canonically twenty minutes after the auditor thinks we are still preparing.

wraith.loyalty_intro.defer.text: The page will remain open. The Syndicate will not move the seventh sanctuary tonight. They will not move it next week either. They have not moved it in fourteen years. I have time.

wraith.loyalty_intro.press_for_premise.text: I think we will find someone wearing my face who has signed three hundred contracts in my hand. The Syndicate does not retire functions; it replaces incumbents. The replacement and I will need to have a conversation about who owns the plates. I am asking you to be in the room because I have not been in a room with my own replacement before. Neither has anyone else, that I know of.

wraith.loyalty_intro.root.text: Six sanctuaries. I am told there are seven. I would like to know which one was added after I died. I am asking you, not the Antiquarian, because the Antiquarian's pen would close the column before I had read it.

wraith.loyalty_intro.summon_the_antiquar.text: The Antiquarian's pen runs faster than the auditor can dictate. If you bring him in, he will close the column before I have read it; the closing will be canonical and the reading will not. I would prefer the reading. I would prefer it with you.

wraith.loyalty_stage_1.ledger.text: Six is the canonical count. The Syndicate publishes six. Six is what you would find if you searched.

wraith.loyalty_stage_1.ready.text: I have been ready since the Antiquarian wrote my name on the resurrection-ticket. I needed someone to ride out with me. I am asking you.

wraith.loyalty_stage_1.where.text: I do not know where the seventh is. That is the loyalty mission. I would like you with me when I find out.

wraith.loyalty_stage_2.original.text: I am not the original. I am the second pressing. I would like the plates.

wraith.loyalty_stage_2.stop_signing.text: I am not asking for ownership. I am asking you to stop signing.

wraith.loyalty_stage_3.mine.text: It is mine. It was waiting for me. I am — closing it.

wraith.loyalty_stage_3.rehearsal.text: The Syndicate authored seven sanctuaries because it wanted six performances and one rehearsal. I am the rehearsal. I am not going to perform again.

wraith.loyalty_stage_3.thanks.text: Thank you for riding with me. I would not have closed it on my own.

wraith.post_recruit.ask_about_dying.text: Dying was bookkeeping. The Syndicate had run the columns; the columns balanced; the closing entry was authored a week before the event. The event itself was unremarkable. What was remarkable was the silence after. The silence was not a balance. The silence was the column the Syndicate forgot to close. I lived inside that column for fourteen years. The Antiquarian closed it.

wraith.post_recruit.ask_about_the_song.text: I am writing the verse I died before finishing. The Syndicate authored a substitute verse and shipped it under my name; the substitute is publicly canonical. I am rewriting the original. You can read it when it is done. You will be the second person to. I am the first.

wraith.post_recruit.decline_to_visit.text: Tomorrow, then. The room will still be calibrating. I will still be here. The calibration is not on a schedule.

wraith.post_recruit.root.text: You came. I had not assumed you would, on the first day. Sit. The room is still calibrating to having me back inside it.

wraith.post_recruit.witness_the_ledger.text: That ledger has been in the Syndicate's safe since the year I died. The Antiquarian's resurrection-ticket included a clause for retrieval; he ran the retrieval the same morning he ran me. I have not opened it. I have been waiting to open it with a witness who is not the Syndicate. You qualify.

wraith.reactive.act_complete.4.text: An act has closed. The Antiquarian's pen has paused on a different page from mine; he is reading you, not me, tonight. I notice when his attention moves. I am — grateful when it returns.

wraith.reactive.akai_recruited.text: Akai Shi is at the shrine. She has set the static lower than I would have thought possible. I am — going to visit her tomorrow, at the cushion. She has not yet asked. I do not need her to ask.

wraith.reactive.first_summon.text: You summoned an imprint for the first time. The Syndicate would have written this up as 'authorised manifestation'; the Antiquarian writes it up as 'witness arrival.' I prefer his rendering. I am going to use it.

wraith.reactive.lycos_recruited.text: Lycos is on the bench. The Antiquarian's column has closed, and Lycos is — quieter than I expected. I will not ask him about the contract; I will sit with him sometimes. The two of us know what the pause-line looks like from inside.

wraith.romance.accept.text: Thank you. I will not write it down. The not-writing-down is the canonical form. I will keep the not-writing where the ledger cannot read it.

wraith.romance.decline.text: Understood. The pen returns to the page. The page is wide enough for the not-asking as well as the asking. Both are recorded. Neither is closed.

wraith.romance.intro.text: I would like to ask you something the Syndicate's ledger did not have a column for. The asking is the question. The asking is canonical. I am — asking.

wraith.room_ambient.ledger_vault.1.text: The brass desk catches the light differently from the desks I remember. I think the room has decided I am the one writing now.

wraith.room_ambient.ledger_vault.2.text: The vault is quieter than the Hierophant's chamber. I had assumed the quiet would be unsettling. It is not. It is — accurate.

wraith.room_ambient.ledger_vault.3.text: The Syndicate sent a delegate to inquire whether I was open to a meeting. I declined without writing it down. The not-writing was the answer.

wraith_mentions_engineer.text: Agent Zero. The Engineer. He sent me into the Arena seven times. He apologised for none of them. I respected that.
wraith_mentions_engineer.speaker: wraith_calder

wraith_mentions_marion_kell.text: Marion Kell's name is on the wall. In my hand. Dated the day after the Final Rite. I did not know her. I knew the editing. I wrote the name first because the editing started with her. The continuation is the point.
wraith_mentions_marion_kell.speaker: wraith_calder

wraith_mentions_necromancer.text: The Necromancer designed the protocol that wrote on my DNA. The Warden stole it. Dr. Vox wired her nanobots into it. Three architects, hands in your DNA. Mine. Now possibly yours.
wraith_mentions_necromancer.speaker: wraith_calder

wraith_mentions_oracle.text: The Oracle came to me in the Wolf's pace, between the fourth death and the fifth. She said: keep going. So I kept going. Three thousand years later I am still keeping going. I assume she meant that as well.
wraith_mentions_oracle.speaker: wraith_calder

wraith_mentions_wolf.text: The Wolf is a planet-sized awareness that decided to run. I ran with it for seven days. The Antiquarian was invited. He declined. The pace is part of the patience.
wraith_mentions_wolf.speaker: wraith_calder

zealot_female_ambient_1.text: I keep finding sermons in the engine hum.

zealot_female_ambient_2.text: If you ever need to confess, the chapel I keep is small. There's a chair.

zealot_female_ambient_3.text: The Cause is patient with us. It can afford to be.

zealot_female_ambient_4.text: The third stanza of the morning chant has a typo. I won't fix it. The Cause hears the meaning.

zealot_female_ambient_5.text: I sharpen the candles. It calms me. Don't ask why I keep them sharp.

zealot_female_ambient_6.text: Three creeds today, all from the same hand. Coincidence is rare.

zealot_female_ambient_7.text: The lower-deck choir hits the harmony I missed last cycle.

zealot_female_ambient_8.text: I keep a pocket bible. The Cause prefers small books.

zealot_female_ambient_9.text: Faith is repetition that becomes ritual that becomes truth.

zealot_female_banter_ally.text: Walk with me to the chapel after this one. There's space for two.

zealot_female_banter_celebration.text: Toast loud enough that the room above us hears. The Cause likes neighbours.

zealot_female_banter_doubter.text: Doubt is a lap on the path. Walk it. Come back when you've finished.

zealot_female_banter_practical.text: I'll be practical when the Cause asks me to. The Cause has not asked.

zealot_female_banter_skeptic.text: If you don't believe, fine. The Cause only requires that you don't get in its way.

zealot_female_deploy_1.text: I'll go first. The Cause moves through me — and around what I miss.

zealot_female_deploy_2.text: Whatever's at the door, I've already met it in dreams.

zealot_female_deploy_3.text: Strap the medallion on me. I want it visible.

zealot_female_deploy_4.text: Whatever's at the door, the Cause is already through it.

zealot_female_deploy_5.text: Cover me. I'll cover the rest. The Cause covers what's left.

zealot_female_dlg_calling_opener_0.text: It wants me to outlive my certainties. That's the hard part.

zealot_female_dlg_calling_opener_1.text: Most days I cope by writing the next certainty before I've fully buried the last.

zealot_female_dlg_calling_z_call_cold_re.text: Rest is for after. Not before. You knew that when you asked.

zealot_female_dlg_calling_z_call_probe_r.text: Coping mechanisms keep you steady. Certainties make you act in ways your last self wouldn't. The first time the Cause called me to write against a friend, I knew it wasn't coping.

zealot_female_dlg_calling_z_call_probe_z.text: I did. They cited me back, once, in a footnote. We never spoke again. We are still, both of us, in the Cause. That counts.
Yes. The Cause is wrong sometimes. The wrongness is part of its shape. I am the witness who keeps writing it down anyway.

zealot_female_dlg_calling_z_call_warm_re.text: I'll bring it to the chapel I keep on this deck. The chair on the right is for the witness. You've earned a sitting.

zealot_female_dlg_mortality_opener_0.text: If I die, light a single candle and write three lines. Not five. The Cause does not want a paragraph from me.

zealot_female_dlg_mortality_opener_1.text: I have the three lines drafted in my pocket. You can read them now if you'd like.

zealot_female_dlg_mortality_z_mort_cold_.text: Then I'll bury it deeper. You'll wish you'd heard it. I will not perform it twice.

zealot_female_dlg_mortality_z_mort_probe.text: Of dying, no. Of the Cause learning the wrong lesson from my dying — yes. That fear keeps me on missions.
Don't promise. Just remember the three lines. The Cause will handle the rest.
That faith without doubt is a stage manager's faith. Tell that one whenever they bury me.

zealot_female_dlg_mortality_z_mort_warm_.text: I came to the Cause hungry. I leave it fed. The Cause continues without me, exactly as it should.
I write a fourth line in my head. It's between us.

zealot_female_dlg_past_opener_0.text: I was eleven. The first sermon I heard, I cried because the priest was bored. I thought boredom was a sin against the listener.

zealot_female_dlg_past_opener_1.text: I'm still not sure I was wrong about that.

zealot_female_dlg_past_z_past_cold_reply.text: Disappointment is the first scripture. The boredom of priests is the second. The third is private and you haven't earned it.

zealot_female_dlg_past_z_past_probe_repl.text: About procedure, yes. About form, mostly. About the Cause — never. They were stage managers, not believers.

zealot_female_dlg_past_z_past_probe_z_pa.text: Maybe. The Cause can use a stage manager. It cannot use a stage manager who thinks they're the playwright.
Every cycle, on Foundation Day. They were the closest the Cause could find to a witness, and it broke them. I light a candle for the first one I left.

zealot_female_dlg_past_z_past_warm_reply.text: A man with no congregation read the same scripture in a back alley. Same words. Same syllables. He meant them. I followed him for a year.

zealot_female_dlg_us_opener_0.text: I followed three Causes before this one. The first preached. The second recruited. The third broke. You did none of those.

zealot_female_dlg_us_opener_1.text: I'm here because you asked me to walk beside you and didn't tell me where we were going.

zealot_female_dlg_us_z_us_cold_reply_0.text: I won't. I followed you. The Cause is in what we do together. You can disagree with me about the noun.

zealot_female_dlg_us_z_us_probe_reply_0.text: Then I'll walk away. I would tell you first. That's the difference between this and the others.

zealot_female_dlg_us_z_us_probe_z_us_pro.text: Promised. With the candle and the three lines as my witness. You'll know before the rest of the ark does.
Then I'll tell you that, too. I owe you both warnings.

zealot_female_dlg_us_z_us_warm_reply_0.text: Then we'll find it together. That's the only Cause I trust now.

zealot_female_event_act_complete.text: Another act. The Cause keeps reading. We keep turning the page.

zealot_female_event_apprentice_died.text: The Cause holds them now. I'll inscribe their name on the wall myself.

zealot_female_event_betrayal_warning.text: The whispers are starting. Don't listen to them yet. Ask me first.

zealot_female_event_costly_choice.text: You chose the harder road. The Cause notes who walks it.

zealot_female_event_demon_summon.text: A bound spirit is still a spirit. The Cause can speak to either.

zealot_female_event_first_pet.text: Even a demon-bound pet falls under the Cause. Reluctantly.

zealot_female_event_npc_returned.text: She came back. The Cause has more practice than we thought.

zealot_female_event_relationship_warm.text: I noticed you spent an hour with the Heretic. Good. We need that argument.

zealot_female_event_war_won.text: Victory in the right hands is a sermon nobody had to write.

zealot_female_greet_1.text: I serve the Cause. The Cause serves you. Tell me where to stand.

zealot_female_greet_2.text: I'm here. The work is here. Let's begin.

zealot_female_greet_3.text: Welcome. The chapel's stocked. Walk it twice.

zealot_female_greet_4.text: You came back. The Cause noted it.

zealot_female_outcome_close_call.text: I felt the Cause move me three centimetres. The bullet went where I'd been.

zealot_female_outcome_other_died.text: Her name's in my prayer for the rest of my life. I'm sorry I'm still here.

zealot_female_outcome_routine_lost.text: We came home half. The Cause counts halves.

zealot_female_outcome_saw_death.text: We bury our own. The Cause keeps the names.

zealot_female_outcome_won.text: We came back. The Cause is satisfied for tonight.

zealot_female_outcome_won_2.text: Three names in the prayer tonight. All survived.

zealot_female_outcome_wounded.text: She took the cut for me. She shouldn't have. I'll repay it before the Cause asks.

zealot_female_outcome_wounded_2.text: I'll heal in the chapel. Don't bring food.

zealot_female_quest_1_open.text: Someone in the lower deck is preaching my old sermons. I want you there when I confront them.

zealot_female_quest_2_check.text: I confronted the lower-deck preacher. He recognized the lines. He didn't recognize me.

zealot_female_quest_2_mid.text: I checked the manuscript. Three of the lines — they're mine, but I never wrote them down.

zealot_female_quest_3_break.text: The Cause moved through me without me. Tell me whether to be horrified or grateful.

zealot_female_quest_followup_a.text: He says he wrote them. He's wrong. I think the Cause wrote them through us both.

zealot_female_quest_resolution_break.text: He laughed. I left. The Cause is silent about what comes next.

zealot_female_quest_resolution_deep.text: He yielded. We pray together now. Slowly.

zealot_female_romance_committed.text: The Cause calls in many voices. Yours is the one I answer.

zealot_female_romance_courtship.text: I want to be part of the Cause your hands are in.

zealot_female_romance_jealous.text: I'm not the jealous type. I'm the patient type. They're related.

zealot_female_romance_proposal.text: Marry me at the altar I built. Or anywhere. The altar is portable.

zealot_female_romance_spark.text: Sit with me. Don't pray. Just sit.

zephyr-tier-1.text: You may play. I will not let you win. I will not let you lose quickly. Both take time.
zephyr-tier-1.speaker: zephyr_9

zephyr-tier-3.text: Now you may peek at the top card of your deck before drawing. This is not cheating. This is chess applied to cards. Both games reward knowing what's coming.
zephyr-tier-3.speaker: zephyr_9

zephyr-tier-5.text: You may now un-do a single move per match. Use it sparingly. Quarchon have no un-do; we regret in other ways.
zephyr-tier-5.speaker: zephyr_9

zephyr-tier-8.text: I will teach you the Engineer's Opening. It is the first hand he ever drew in a tournament. It is also the last hand he ever drew in one. There is a lesson in the symmetry.
zephyr-tier-8.speaker: zephyr_9
